cards.gloss: "the two walked off together" (22:6), said again in 22:8. **Rashi**: Abraham, who knew what was coming, walked with the same willingness as Isaac, who did not.

cards.he: אֱלֹהִים יִרְאֶה־לּוֹ הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה
cards.tl: Elohim yir'eh lo haseh l'olah
cards.gloss: "It is God who will see to the sheep" (22:8): Abraham's answer to Isaac's question. The same verb, **to see**, names the place afterward: **Adonai yireh** (22:14).

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרָא אֵלָיו מַלְאַךְ יְיָ מִן־הַשָּׁמַיִם וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָהָם אַבְרָהָם וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר אַל־תִּשְׁלַח יָדְךָ אֶל־הַנַּעַר וְאַל־תַּעַשׂ לוֹ מְאוּמָה כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי־יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ אֶת־בִּנְךָ אֶת־יְחִידְךָ מִמֶּנִּי
cards.en: Then a messenger of יהוה called to him from heaven: “Abraham! Abraham!” And he answered, “Here I am.” “Do not raise your hand against the boy, or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your favored one, from Me.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra eilav mal'ach Adonai min hashamayim vayomer Avraham Avraham vayomer hineini
Vayomer al tishlach yadcha el hana-ar v'al ta-as lo m'umah ki atah yadati ki y'rei Elohim atah v'lo chasachta et bincha et y'chidcha mimeni

cards.title: The ram and the shofar
cards.body: Abraham looks up and sees **a ram caught by its horns** (22:13), and offers it instead of his son. **Rabbi Abbahu**: that's why the Rosh Hashanah shofar is a **ram's horn**. God says: blow it before Me, and I will **remember the binding of Isaac**.

cards.q: According to Rosh Hashanah 16a, why is the shofar a ram's horn?
choices: To recall the ram offered instead of Isaac
Rams were the only animals with horns
Abraham blew it on the mountain
cards.why: God says: sound a ram's horn, and **I will remember the binding of Isaac** for you.
wrong_why: Other animals have horns too; the Talmud gives a different reason.
The Torah doesn't say Abraham blew a horn.

cards.title: Where is Isaac?
cards.body: At the end, "**Abraham** then returned to his servants" (22:19). Isaac isn't mentioned. **Ibn Ezra** (12th-century Spain): he was there, in his father's care. Those who claim Isaac was actually slaughtered and revived, he says, **contradict the text**.

cards.q: How does Ibn Ezra explain why Isaac isn't named in 22:19?
choices: He was there, in Abraham's care
He had been slaughtered and revived
He had gone off on his own
cards.why: He reads Isaac as **present and safe**, and rejects the idea that he died.
wrong_why: Ibn Ezra rejects that reading as contradicting Scripture.
That isn't Ibn Ezra's explanation.

cards.body: The Talmud has this chapter read on the **second day of Rosh Hashanah**, to recall the binding on the day of judgment (Megillah 31a), and the **shofar** recalls it every year. Many congregations read it on Rosh Hashanah; check what CBB reads.

cards.prompt: Hineni means being fully present. Where in your life right now would you like to be able to say hineni?

points: **Hineni**: here I am, said to God, Isaac and the angel.
Rashi: "your son... your only one... whom you love... Isaac."
**The two walked together** (Rashi 22:6).
The ram's horn: **the shofar remembers the binding** (Rosh Hashanah 16a).
Ibn Ezra: Isaac was there, **safe**, at the end.

lessons.title: Abraham and Sarah (5): Sarah's life and the cave of Machpelah
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 23:1, 23:2 and 23:4, Bava Metzia 87a, Bereshit Rabbah 79:7 (read on Sefaria 11/09).

cards.title: A portion called "Life"
cards.body: This Torah portion is called **Chayei Sarah**, "the life of Sarah," yet it opens with **her death** (23:1-2). Abraham comes **to mourn her and to weep for her**, then rises to find her a resting place.

cards.q: How did Abraham get the cave of Machpelah?
choices: He paid full price for it
It was a gift he accepted
He took it in a war
cards.why: Ephron offers it as a gift, but Abraham **insists on paying** 400 shekels of silver (23:16).

cards.he:
וַיִּהְיוּ חַיֵּי שָׂרָה מֵאָה שָׁנָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְשֶׁבַע שָׁנִים שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי שָׂרָה
וַתָּמׇת שָׂרָה בְּקִרְיַת אַרְבַּע הִוא חֶבְרוֹן בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן וַיָּבֹא אַבְרָהָם לִסְפֹּד לְשָׂרָה וְלִבְכֹּתָהּ
cards.en: Sarah’s lifetime—the span of Sarah’s life—came to one hundred and twenty-seven years. Sarah died in Kiriath-arba—now Hebron—in the land of Canaan; and Abraham proceeded to mourn for Sarah and to bewail her.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayihyu chayei Sarah mei-ah shanah v'esrim shanah v'sheva shanim sh'nei chayei Sarah
Vatamot Sarah b'kiryat arba hi chevron b'eretz k'na-an vayavo Avraham lispod l'sarah v'livkotah

cards.he: שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי שָׂרָה
cards.tl: Sh'nei chayei Sarah
cards.gloss: "the years of Sarah's life" (23:1). The verse counts 100 years, 20 years and 7 years separately. **Rashi**: "years" is repeated to show that **all her years were equally good**.

cards.title: Why here?
cards.body: Sarah's death comes right after the binding of Isaac. **Rashi** quotes a midrash: when she heard that her son had been readied as an offering and nearly sacrificed, the shock was too much, and **she died**.

cards.q: Why does Rashi say the verse repeats the word "years"?
choices: To show all her years were equally good
To show she lived longer than Abraham
cards.why: The repetition tells us **every stage of her life was good**.
wrong_why: Rashi says nothing about comparing their ages.
Rashi reads it as praise, not doubt.

cards.he:
וַיָּקׇם אַבְרָהָם מֵעַל פְּנֵי מֵתוֹ וַיְדַבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי־חֵת לֵאמֹר
גֵּר־וְתוֹשָׁב אָנֹכִי עִמָּכֶם תְּנוּ לִי אֲחֻזַּת־קֶבֶר עִמָּכֶם וְאֶקְבְּרָה מֵתִי מִלְּפָנָי
cards.en: Then Abraham rose from beside his dead, and spoke to the Hittites, saying, “I am a resident alien among you; sell me a burial site among you, that I may remove my dead for burial.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayakom Avraham mei-al p'nei meito vaydabeir el b'nei cheit leimor
Geir v'toshav anochi imachem t'nu li achuzat kever imachem v'ekb'rah meiti mil'fanai

cards.he: גֵּר־וְתוֹשָׁב אָנֹכִי עִמָּכֶם
cards.tl: Geir v'toshav anochi imachem
cards.gloss: "I am a resident alien among you" (23:4): an outsider who has settled down. **Rashi** adds a midrash: if you sell, I'm a stranger and will pay; if not, I'll claim it as a resident, **by right**.

cards.q: What do the two words ger and toshav describe?
choices: An outsider who has settled down
cards.why: **Ger**, stranger, from another land; **toshav**, resident, settled among them. Abraham is both.
wrong_why: Neither word means king or servant.
The words describe Abraham alone.

cards.he:
וְעֶפְרוֹן יֹשֵׁב בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי־חֵת וַיַּעַן עֶפְרוֹן הַחִתִּי אֶת־אַבְרָהָם בְּאׇזְנֵי בְנֵי־חֵת לְכֹל בָּאֵי שַׁעַר־עִירוֹ לֵאמֹר
לֹא־אֲדֹנִי שְׁמָעֵנִי הַשָּׂדֶה נָתַתִּי לָךְ וְהַמְּעָרָה אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ לְךָ נְתַתִּיהָ לְעֵינֵי בְנֵי־עַמִּי נְתַתִּיהָ לָּךְ קְבֹר מֵתֶךָ
cards.en: Ephron was present among the Hittites; so Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, the assembly in his town’s gate, saying, “No, my lord, hear me: I give you the field and I give you the cave that is in it; I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'efron yosheiv b'toch b'nei cheit vaya-an efron hachiti et Avraham b'oznei v'nei cheit l'chol ba-ei sha-ar iro leimor
Lo adoni sh'ma-eini hasadeh natati lach v'ham'arah asher bo l'cha n'tatiha l'einei v'nei ami n'tatiha lach k'vor meitecha

cards.title: Say little, do much
cards.body: Ephron offers the field as a **gift**, in front of everyone (23:11). Then he names a price, 400 shekels: "what is that between you and me?" (23:15). **Rabbi Elazar**: the righteous **say little and do much**, like Abraham running to his guests; the wicked **say much and don't do even a little**, like Ephron.

cards.title: Paid in full
cards.body: Abraham **weighs out the silver** in public (23:16) and buries Sarah in the cave of Machpelah (23:19). A midrash: Machpelah is one of **three places** no one can call stolen, because they were bought: the cave of Machpelah, the Temple site and Joseph's tomb.

cards.q: Why does the midrash stress that Machpelah was paid for?
choices: So no one can say it was stolen
cards.why: It's one of three places **bought outright**, so no one can claim it was taken.
wrong_why: Ephron did offer a gift; Abraham chose to pay.
Nothing in the text says Ephron was poor.

cards.prompt: Abraham mourns, and then rises to do what has to be done (23:3). What helps you move between grieving and doing? It's fine to skip this one.

points: **Chayei Sarah**, the life of Sarah, opens with her death.
Rashi: **all her years were equally good**.
**Ger v'toshav**: an outsider who has settled down.
Bava Metzia 87a: **say little, do much** (Abraham, not Ephron).
Machpelah was **paid for**, never taken (Bereshit Rabbah 79:7).

lessons.title: Abraham and Sarah (6): Rebekah at the well
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 24:14, 24:57 and 24:67, Berakhot 26b (read on Sefaria 11/09). Ten camels: Genesis 24:10.

cards.title: A test of kindness
cards.body: Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac. At a well, the servant prays for a sign: the young woman who offers water **to him and to his camels** (24:12-14).

cards.q: What sign does the servant ask God for?
choices: A woman who offers water to him and his camels
The most beautiful woman at the well
A woman who knows Abraham's name
cards.why: The sign is **kindness beyond what's asked**: water for a stranger, and for his camels too.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמַר יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי אֲדֹנִי אַבְרָהָם הַקְרֵה־נָא לְפָנַי הַיּוֹם וַעֲשֵׂה־חֶסֶד עִם אֲדֹנִי אַבְרָהָם
הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי נִצָּב עַל־עֵין הַמָּיִם וּבְנוֹת אַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר יֹצְאֹת לִשְׁאֹב מָיִם
וְהָיָה הַנַּעֲרָ אֲשֶׁר אֹמַר אֵלֶיהָ הַטִּי־נָא כַדֵּךְ וְאֶשְׁתֶּה וְאָמְרָה שְׁתֵה וְגַם־גְּמַלֶּיךָ אַשְׁקֶה אֹתָהּ הֹכַחְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ לְיִצְחָק וּבָהּ אֵדַע כִּי־עָשִׂיתָ חֶסֶד עִם־אֲדֹנִי
cards.en: And he said, “O יהוה, God of my master Abraham’s [house], grant me good fortune this day, and deal graciously with my master Abraham: Here I stand by the spring as the daughters of the townspeople come out to draw water; let the maiden to whom I say, ‘Please, lower your jar that I may drink,’ and who replies, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels’—let her be the one whom You have decreed for Your servant Isaac. Thereby shall I know that You have dealt graciously with my master.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomar Adonai Elohei adoni Avraham hakrei na l'fanai hayom va-asei chesed im adoni Avraham
Hinei anochi nitzav al ein hamayim uv'not anshei ha-ir yotz'ot lish'ov mayim
V'hayah hana-ara asher omar eileha hati na chadeich v'eshteh v'amrah sh'tei v'gam g'malecha ashkeh otah hochachta l'avd'cha l'yitzchak uvah eida ki asita chesed im adoni

cards.he: וַעֲשֵׂה־חֶסֶד
cards.tl: Va-asei chesed
cards.gloss: "deal graciously" (24:12). **Chesed**, loving-kindness, is this chapter's key word: the servant asks God for chesed, and looks for a woman who shows it. **Rashi**: if she is fitting, "I shall know that thou hast shown kindness to my master."

cards.he:
וַיָּרׇץ הָעֶבֶד לִקְרָאתָהּ וַיֹּאמֶר הַגְמִיאִינִי נָא מְעַט־מַיִם מִכַּדֵּךְ
וַתֹּאמֶר שְׁתֵה אֲדֹנִי וַתְּמַהֵר וַתֹּרֶד כַּדָּהּ עַל־יָדָהּ וַתַּשְׁקֵהוּ
וַתְּכַל לְהַשְׁקֹתוֹ וַתֹּאמֶר גַּם לִגְמַלֶּיךָ אֶשְׁאָב עַד אִם־כִּלּוּ לִשְׁתֹּת
וַתְּמַהֵר וַתְּעַר כַּדָּהּ אֶל־הַשֹּׁקֶת וַתָּרׇץ עוֹד אֶל־הַבְּאֵר לִשְׁאֹב וַתִּשְׁאַב לְכׇל־גְּמַלָּיו
cards.en: The servant ran toward her and said, “Please, let me sip a little water from your jar.” “Drink, my lord,” she said, and she quickly lowered her jar upon her hand and let him drink. When she had let him drink his fill, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they finish drinking.” Quickly emptying her jar into the trough, she ran back to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayarotz ha-eved likratah vayomer hagmi-ini na m'at mayim mikadeich
Vatomer sh'tei adoni vat'maheir vatored kadah al yadah vatashkeihu
Vat'chal l'hashkoto vatomer gam ligmalecha esh'av ad im kilu lishtot
Vat'maheir vat'ar kadah el hashoket vatarotz od el hab'eir lish'ov vatish'av l'chol g'malav

cards.title: She ran
cards.body: Count Rebekah's verbs: she **hurries**, lowers her jar, gives him drink, empties it, **runs** back to the well, and draws for **all** his camels (24:18-20). He had ten camels (24:10). She does far more than she was asked.

cards.q: What made Rebekah the answer to the servant's prayer?
choices: She offered water to his camels too, without being asked
She asked who his master was
cards.why: His sign was **chesed beyond the request**, and she gave it, running back again and again.
wrong_why: She was family, but that wasn't the sign he prayed for.
She didn't ask; she simply helped.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמְרוּ נִקְרָא לַנַּעֲרָ וְנִשְׁאֲלָה אֶת־פִּיהָ
וַיִּקְרְאוּ לְרִבְקָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלֶיהָ הֲתֵלְכִי עִם־הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה וַתֹּאמֶר אֵלֵךְ
cards.en: And they said, “Let us call the girl and ask for her reply.” They called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomru nikra lana-ara v'nish'alah et piha
Vayikr'u l'rivkah vayomru eileha hateilchi im ha-ish hazeh vatomer eileich

cards.he: אֵלֵךְ
cards.tl: Eileich
cards.gloss: "I will" (24:58): one word. Her family says "let us call the girl and ask her." **Rashi**: from here we learn that a woman is not married **without her own consent**.

cards.q: What does Rashi learn from "let us call the girl and ask her"?
choices: A woman is not married without her consent
A bride must travel the same day
cards.why: Asking Rebekah teaches that **her own yes** is required.
wrong_why: The verse teaches the opposite: they ask her.
The timing isn't Rashi's point.

cards.he: לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה
cards.tl: Lasuach basadeh
cards.gloss: Isaac went out "walking in the field" toward evening (24:63). **Lasuach** can also mean to converse, so the Talmud reads it as **prayer**: Abraham began the morning prayer, and **Isaac began Minchah**, the afternoon prayer.

cards.q: According to Berakhot 26b, which prayer did Isaac begin?
cards.why: From "lasuach basadeh **toward evening**": Isaac's prayer is the afternoon one.
wrong_why: The Talmud credits Abraham with the morning prayer.
That isn't Isaac's; the verse says toward evening.

cards.title: Comfort after his mother
cards.body: Isaac brings Rebekah into **his mother Sarah's tent**, loves her, and is comforted after his mother (24:67). **Rashi** quotes a midrash: in Sarah's lifetime a **lamp burned** from one Shabbat eve to the next, there was **blessing in the dough** and a **cloud** over the tent. They stopped when she died, and **returned with Rebekah**.
In the Amidah's first blessing you say **Elohei Rivkah**, God of Rebekah, right after Elohei Sarah. And every **Minchah** is, in the Talmud's reading, Isaac's walk in the field.

points: The sign: **chesed beyond the request** (24:14).
Rebekah **runs** to water ten camels.
**Elech**, "I will": Rashi, no marriage **without her consent**.
**Lasuach basadeh**: Isaac begins **Minchah** (Berakhot 26b).
Sarah's lamp, dough and cloud **return with Rebekah** (Rashi 24:67).

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau (1): Twins and the birthright
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 25:22, 25:27 and 25:30 (with Bereshit Rabbah 63 and Bava Batra 16b), read on Sefaria 11/09. Note the Contemporary Torah renders yoshev ohalim as 'raising livestock'.

cards.title: Two in one womb
cards.body: Rebekah's twins **struggle inside her** (25:22). She asks the question people in pain ask, **why?**, and then goes **to inquire of God**.

cards.q: Rebekah keeps her distress to herself.
cards.why: She speaks it aloud and **goes to inquire of Adonai** (25:22), and God answers her.

cards.he:
וַיֶּעְתַּר יִצְחָק לַיהֹוָה לְנֹכַח אִשְׁתּוֹ כִּי עֲקָרָה הִוא וַיֵּעָתֶר לוֹ יְיָ וַתַּהַר רִבְקָה אִשְׁתּוֹ
וַיִּתְרֹצְצוּ הַבָּנִים בְּקִרְבָּהּ וַתֹּאמֶר אִם־כֵּן לָמָּה זֶּה אָנֹכִי וַתֵּלֶךְ לִדְרֹשׁ אֶת־יְיָ
וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גוֹיִם בְּבִטְנֵךְ וּשְׁנֵי לְאֻמִּים מִמֵּעַיִךְ יִפָּרֵדוּ וּלְאֹם מִלְאֹם יֶאֱמָץ וְרַב יַעֲבֹד צָעִיר
cards.en: Isaac pleaded with יהוה on behalf of his wife, because she was barren; and יהוה responded to his plea, and his wife Rebekah conceived. But the children struggled in her womb, and she said, “If so, why do I exist?” She went to inquire of יהוה, and יהוה answered her, “Two nations are in your womb, Two separate peoples shall issue from your body; One people shall be mightier than the other, And the older shall serve the younger.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayetar Yitzchak laihovah l'nochach ishto ki akarah hi vayei-ater lo Adonai vatahar Rivkah ishto
Vayitrotz'tzu habanim b'kirbah vatomer im kein lamah zeh anochi vateilech lidrosh et Adonai
Vayomer Adonai lah sh'nei goyim b'vitneich ush'nei l'umim mimei-ayich yipareidu ul'om mil'om ye-ematz v'rav ya-avod tza-ir

cards.he: לָמָּה זֶּה אָנֹכִי
cards.tl: Lamah zeh anochi
cards.gloss: "why do I exist?" (25:22). Rebekah doesn't stop at the question: she goes **lidrosh**, to seek out God.

cards.title: Running to the doors
cards.body: **Rashi** reads "struggled" as **running**: whenever Rebekah passed a house of Torah study, **Jacob** strained to come out; whenever she passed a pagan temple, **Esau** did. He also gives the plain reading: the twins **fought** with each other.

cards.q: In Rashi's midrash, why did the twins move inside Rebekah?
choices: Each was drawn to a different kind of place
They wanted to be born first
cards.why: Jacob toward **houses of study**, Esau toward **pagan temples**: two paths from the start.
wrong_why: Hunger isn't part of this midrash.
Rashi's midrash here is about where each was drawn, not birth order.

cards.he:
וַיִּגְדְּלוּ הַנְּעָרִים וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים
וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת־עֵשָׂו כִּי־צַיִד בְּפִיו וְרִבְקָה אֹהֶבֶת אֶת־יַעֲקֹב
cards.en: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the outdoors; but Jacob became a mild man, raising livestock. Isaac favored Esau because he had a taste for game; but Rebekah favored Jacob.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayigd'lu han'arim vay'hi eisav ish yodeia tzayid ish sadeh v'ya-akov ish tam yosheiv ohalim
Vaye-ehav Yitzchak et eisav ki tzayid b'fiv v'rivkah ohevet et Yaakov

cards.he: אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים
cards.tl: Ish tam yosheiv ohalim
cards.gloss: : this translation says "a mild man, raising livestock"; word for word, "a **whole** man, **dwelling in tents**." **Rashi**: tam means his heart matched his mouth, not clever at deceiving; the tents are the study tents of **Shem and Ever**.

cards.q: What does Rashi say tam means?
cards.why: **Tam**: whole, straightforward. What was in his heart was in his mouth.
wrong_why: Tam isn't about strength.
Tam describes character, not birth order.

cards.he:
וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד וַיָּבֹא עֵשָׂו מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה וְהוּא עָיֵף
וַיֹּאמֶר עֵשָׂו אֶל־יַעֲקֹב הַלְעִיטֵנִי נָא מִן־הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה כִּי עָיֵף אָנֹכִי עַל־כֵּן קָרָא־שְׁמוֹ אֱדוֹם
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב מִכְרָה כַיּוֹם אֶת־בְּכֹרָתְךָ לִי
cards.en: Once when Jacob was cooking a stew, Esau came in from the open, famished. And Esau said to Jacob, “Give me some of that red stuff to gulp down, for I am famished”—which is why he was named Edom. Jacob said, “First sell me your birthright.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayazed Yaakov nazid vayavo eisav min hasadeh v'hu ayeif
Vayomer eisav el Yaakov hal'iteini na min ha-adom ha-adom hazeh ki ayeif anochi al kein kara sh'mo edom
Vayomer Yaakov michrah chayom et b'choratcha li

cards.title: A mourner's meal
cards.body: Why was Jacob cooking lentils? **Rashi**: **Abraham died that day**, and Jacob was preparing the first meal for the mourners. Lentils are **round like a wheel**, because mourning is a wheel that comes around to everyone.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר עֵשָׂו הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ לָמוּת וְלָמָּה־זֶּה לִי בְּכֹרָה
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי כַּיּוֹם וַיִּשָּׁבַע לוֹ וַיִּמְכֹּר אֶת־בְּכֹרָתוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב
וְיַעֲקֹב נָתַן לְעֵשָׂו לֶחֶם וּנְזִיד עֲדָשִׁים וַיֹּאכַל וַיֵּשְׁתְּ וַיָּקׇם וַיֵּלַךְ וַיִּבֶז עֵשָׂו אֶת־הַבְּכֹרָה
cards.en: And Esau said, “I am at the point of death, so of what use is my birthright to me?” But Jacob said, “Swear to me first.” So he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob. Jacob then gave Esau bread and lentil stew; he ate and drank, and he rose and went away. Thus did Esau spurn the birthright.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer eisav hinei anochi holeich lamut v'lamah zeh li b'chorah
Vayomer Yaakov hishav'ah li kayom vayishava lo vayimkor et b'chorato l'ya-akov
V'ya-akov natan l'eisav lechem un'zid adashim vayochal vayeisht vayakom vayeilach vayivez eisav et hab'chorah

cards.he: וַיִּבֶז עֵשָׂו אֶת־הַבְּכֹרָה
cards.tl: Vayivez eisav et hab'chorah
cards.gloss: "thus did Esau spurn the birthright" (25:34). The Torah's own verdict comes after a rush of verbs: **he ate, drank, rose and went**.

cards.q: Whom does the last line of the story judge?
choices: Jacob, for driving a hard bargain
cards.why: The verse names **Esau**: he "spurn[ed] the birthright."
wrong_why: The Torah doesn't comment on Jacob here, though readers have long argued about him.
Isaac isn't in this scene.

cards.body: Jacob is the one who **dwells in tents**. Every Shabbat morning you open with **Mah tovu ohalecha Yaakov**, "how good are your tents, Jacob" (Numbers 24:5).

points: **Lamah zeh anochi**: Rebekah's why becomes a search for God.
Rashi: the twins ran toward **study houses** and **temples**.
**Ish tam**: heart and mouth matched (Rashi 25:27).
The lentils: **a mourner's meal** for Abraham (Rashi 25:30).
**Vayivez Esav**: the Torah's verdict on the sale.

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau (2): The stolen blessing
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 27:1, 27:19 and 27:22 (from Midrash Tanchuma) and Bereshit Rabbah 67:4, read on Sefaria 11/09.

cards.title: One blessing, two brothers
cards.body: Isaac is old and **cannot see**. He plans to bless **Esau**. Rebekah overhears, and sends **Jacob** in to take the blessing in disguise (27:1-17).

cards.q: When Isaac asks "Which of my sons are you?", what does Jacob answer?
cards.why: "**I am Esau, your first-born**" (27:19). Rashi works hard with those words, as you'll see.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי כִּי־זָקֵן יִצְחָק וַתִּכְהֶיןָ עֵינָיו מֵרְאֹת וַיִּקְרָא אֶת־עֵשָׂו בְּנוֹ הַגָּדֹל וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו בְּנִי וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו הִנֵּנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה־נָא זָקַנְתִּי לֹא יָדַעְתִּי יוֹם מוֹתִי
וְעַתָּה שָׂא־נָא כֵלֶיךָ תֶּלְיְךָ וְקַשְׁתֶּךָ וְצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה וְצוּדָה לִּי צָיִד
וַעֲשֵׂה־לִי מַטְעַמִּים כַּאֲשֶׁר אָהַבְתִּי וְהָבִיאָה לִּי וְאֹכֵלָה בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרֶכְךָ נַפְשִׁי בְּטֶרֶם אָמוּת
cards.en: When Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” He answered, “Here I am.” And he said, “I am old now, and I do not know how soon I may die. Take your gear, your quiver and bow, and go out into the open and hunt me some game. Then prepare a dish for me such as I like, and bring it to me to eat, so that I may give you my innermost blessing before I die.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi ki zakein Yitzchak vatichhena einav meir'ot vayikra et eisav b'no hagadol vayomer eilav b'ni vayomer eilav hineini
Vayomer hinei na zakanti lo yadati yom moti
V'atah sa na cheilecha tely'cha v'kashtecha v'tzei hasadeh v'tzudah li tzayid
Va-asei li mat'amim ka-asher ahavti v'havi-ah li v'ocheilah ba-avur t'varech'cha nafshi b'terem amut

cards.title: Why was Isaac blind?
cards.body: **Rashi** gives two midrashim: the **smoke** of the incense Esau's wives offered to idols dimmed his eyes; or, at the binding of Isaac, the **angels wept** and their tears fell into his eyes.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֶל־רִבְקָה אִמּוֹ הֵן עֵשָׂו אָחִי אִישׁ שָׂעִר וְאָנֹכִי אִישׁ חָלָק
אוּלַי יְמֻשֵּׁנִי אָבִי וְהָיִיתִי בְעֵינָיו כִּמְתַעְתֵּעַ וְהֵבֵאתִי עָלַי קְלָלָה וְלֹא בְרָכָה
וַתֹּאמֶר לוֹ אִמּוֹ עָלַי קִלְלָתְךָ בְּנִי אַךְ שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי וְלֵךְ קַח־לִי
cards.en: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “But my brother Esau is a hairy man and I am smooth-skinned. If my father touches me, I shall appear to him as a trickster and bring upon myself a curse, not a blessing.” But his mother said to him, “Your curse, my son, be upon me! Just do as I say and go fetch them for me.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Yaakov el Rivkah imo hein eisav achi ish sa-ir v'anochi ish chalak
Ulai y'musheini avi v'hayiti v'einav kimtateia v'heiveiti alai k'lalah v'lo v'rachah
Vatomer lo imo alai kil'latcha b'ni ach sh'ma b'koli v'leich kach li

cards.he:
וַיָּבֹא אֶל־אָבִיו וַיֹּאמֶר אָבִי וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֶּנִּי מִי אַתָּה בְּנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֶל־אָבִיו אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ עָשִׂיתִי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ אֵלָי קוּם־נָא שְׁבָה וְאׇכְלָה מִצֵּידִי בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרְכַנִּי נַפְשֶׁךָ
וַיֹּאמֶר יִצְחָק אֶל־בְּנוֹ מַה־זֶּה מִהַרְתָּ לִמְצֹא בְּנִי וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי הִקְרָה יְיָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְפָנָי
cards.en: He went to his father and said, “Father.” And he said, “Yes, which of my sons are you?” Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your first-born; I have done as you told me. Pray sit up and eat of my game, that you may give me your innermost blessing.” Isaac said to his son, “How did you succeed so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because your God יהוה granted me good fortune.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayavo el aviv vayomer avi vayomer hineni mi atah b'ni
Vayomer Yaakov el aviv anochi eisav b'chorecha asiti ka-asher dibarta eilai kum na sh'vah v'ochlah mitzeidi ba-avur t'varchani nafshecha
Vayomer Yitzchak el b'no ma zeh miharta limtzo b'ni vayomer ki hikrah Adonai Elohecha l'fanai

cards.title: A lie, or not quite?
cards.body: "Anochi Esav b'chorecha," I am Esau your firstborn. **Rashi** splits the sentence: "**I am** the one bringing you food" and "**Esau is** your firstborn." He reads the words so Jacob doesn't tell an outright lie.

cards.q: How does Rashi read Jacob's "I am Esau your firstborn"?
choices: As two statements: "I am the one bringing food" and "Esau is your firstborn"
As a plain lie the Torah approves
cards.why: Rashi **divides the sentence**, so each half is true.
wrong_why: Rashi tries to avoid that conclusion.
Rashi reads the Hebrew as it stands.

cards.he: הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו
cards.tl: Hakol kol Yaakov v'hayadayim y'dei eisav
cards.gloss: "the voice is the voice of Jacob, yet the hands are the hands of Esau" (27:22). **Rashi**: Jacob's voice was **gentle**, "Arise, I pray thee"; Esau would speak **harshly**, "Let my father arise" (27:31).

cards.q: According to Rashi, what gave Jacob's voice away?
cards.why: Jacob said **"please"**; Esau's way of speaking was harsh.
wrong_why: Rashi is about manner, not pitch.
Rashi says nothing about languages here.

cards.he:
וַיֶּחֱרַד יִצְחָק חֲרָדָה גְּדֹלָה עַד־מְאֹד וַיֹּאמֶר מִי־אֵפוֹא הוּא הַצָּד־צַיִד וַיָּבֵא לִי וָאֹכַל מִכֹּל בְּטֶרֶם תָּבוֹא וָאֲבָרְכֵהוּ גַּם־בָּרוּךְ יִהְיֶה
כִּשְׁמֹעַ עֵשָׂו אֶת־דִּבְרֵי אָבִיו וַיִּצְעַק צְעָקָה גְּדֹלָה וּמָרָה עַד־מְאֹד וַיֹּאמֶר לְאָבִיו בָּרְכֵנִי גַם־אָנִי אָבִי
cards.en: Isaac was seized with very violent trembling. “Who was it then,” he demanded, “that hunted game and brought it to me? Moreover, I ate of it before you came, and I blessed him; now he must remain blessed!” When Esau heard his father’s words, he burst into wild and bitter sobbing, and said to his father, “Bless me too, Father!”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayecherad Yitzchak charadah g'dolah ad m'od vayomer mi eifo hu hatzad tzayid vayavei li va-ochal mikol b'terem tavo va-avarcheihu gam baruch yihyeh
Kishmoa eisav et divrei aviv vayitz'ak tz'akah g'dolah umarah ad m'od vayomer l'aviv barcheini gam ani avi

cards.he: הַבְרָכָה אַחַת הִוא־לְךָ אָבִי
cards.tl: Havrachah achat hi l'cha avi
cards.gloss: "Have you but one blessing, Father?" (27:38). Then **Esau wept aloud**. The Torah lets us hear the pain of the brother who lost.

cards.title: The cry comes back
cards.body: **Rabbi Chanina**: Jacob caused Esau **one great and bitter cry**. It was repaid generations later in Shushan, when **Mordecai** cried out "a loud and bitter cry" (Esther 4:1). God is patient, the midrash says, but the debt is remembered.

cards.q: In Bereshit Rabbah 67:4, how was Esau's cry repaid?
choices: By Mordecai's bitter cry in Shushan
Jacob was never held to account
Esau later took the blessing back
cards.why: The same words, **a great and bitter cry**, come back in the Book of Esther.
wrong_why: The midrash says the opposite: God collects, patiently.
Nothing in the Torah says Esau took it back.

cards.prompt: Jacob is our ancestor, yet the Torah makes us hear Esau's sobbing. Why might it tell the story this way?

points: Isaac, blind, plans to bless **Esau**; Rebekah sends **Jacob**.
Rashi on 27:19: "**I am** (bringing food); **Esau is** your firstborn."
**The voice is Jacob's**: gentle, "please" (Rashi 27:22).
"**Have you but one blessing?**" Esau weeps.
Bereshit Rabbah 67:4: the cry returns as **Mordecai's**.

lessons.title: Jacob (3): The ladder
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Berakhot 26b, Rashi on Genesis 28:11, 28:12 and 28:16, Bereshit Rabbah 68:9 (read on Sefaria 11/09).

cards.title: A night on the road
cards.body: Jacob is **running from Esau**. At sunset he stops, puts a **stone** under his head, and sleeps in the open. Then he **dreams** (28:10-12).

cards.q: In Jacob's dream, which way do the angels move first?
cards.why: "**Going up and down**" (28:12): up first. Rashi asks why.

cards.he:
וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה
וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם וַיָּלֶן שָׁם כִּי־בָא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וַיִּקַּח מֵאַבְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם וַיָּשֶׂם מְרַאֲשֹׁתָיו וַיִּשְׁכַּב בַּמָּקוֹם הַהוּא
cards.en: Jacob left Beer-sheba, and set out for Haran. He came upon a certain place and stopped there for the night, for the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of that place, he put it under his head and lay down in that place.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayeitzei Yaakov mib'eir shava vayeilech charanah
Vayifga bamakom vayalen sham ki va hashemesh vayikach mei-avnei hamakom vayasem m'ra-ashotav vayishkav bamakom hahu

cards.he: וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם
cards.tl: Vayifga bamakom
cards.gloss: "he came upon a certain place" (28:11). The Talmud reads **pegiah**, encountering, as **prayer**: Jacob began **Ma'ariv**, the evening prayer. With Abraham's morning prayer and Isaac's afternoon prayer, that makes **three daily prayers**.

cards.q: According to Berakhot 26b, which prayer did Jacob begin?
cards.why: The sun had set (28:11): Jacob's prayer is the **evening** one.
wrong_why: The Talmud credits Abraham with the morning.
That was Isaac's, toward evening in the field.

cards.title: The stones that argued
cards.body: Jacob takes "one of the stones" (28:11), but in the morning he lifts "**the** stone" (28:18). **Rashi** quotes a midrash: he set several stones around his head, and they argued over who would hold the righteous man's head, so God **made them one**.

cards.he:
וַיַּחֲלֹם וְהִנֵּה סֻלָּם מֻצָּב אַרְצָה וְרֹאשׁוֹ מַגִּיעַ הַשָּׁמָיְמָה וְהִנֵּה מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים עֹלִים וְיֹרְדִים בּוֹ
וְהִנֵּה יְיָ נִצָּב עָלָיו וַיֹּאמַר אֲנִי יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִיךָ וֵאלֹהֵי יִצְחָק הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שֹׁכֵב עָלֶיהָ לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה וּלְזַרְעֶךָ
cards.en: He had a dream; a stairway was set on the ground and its top reached to the sky, and messengers of God were going up and down on it. And standing beside him was יהוה, who said, “I am יהוה, the God of your father Abraham’s [house] and the God of Isaac’s [house]: the ground on which you are lying I will assign to you and to your offspring.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayachalom v'hinei sulam mutzav artzah v'rosho magia hashamaymah v'hinei mal'achei Elohim olim v'yordim bo
V'hinei Adonai nitzav alav vayomar ani Adonai Elohei Avraham avicha v'Elohei Yitzchak ha-aretz asher atah shocheiv aleha l'cha et'nenah ul'zar'echa

cards.title: Up first, then down
cards.body: Why do the angels go **up** before they come down? **Rashi**: the angels who had escorted Jacob in the Land could not leave it, so they **went up**; angels for the journey abroad **came down** to accompany him.

cards.q: Why, in Rashi's reading, do the angels go up first?
choices: The Land's escort leaves and a new escort comes down
They were bringing Jacob's prayers to heaven
The ladder only went one way
cards.why: One group of escorts **goes up**, another **comes down** to travel with him.
wrong_why: That's a lovely idea, but not Rashi's here.
The verse says they went both ways.

cards.he: וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּלֵךְ
cards.tl: V'hinei anochi imach ush'marticha b'chol asher teileich
cards.gloss: "I am with you: I will protect you **wherever you go**" (28:15). God's promise to a man alone, at night, on the road.

cards.he:
וַיִּיקַץ יַעֲקֹב מִשְּׁנָתוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר אָכֵן יֵשׁ יְיָ בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה וְאָנֹכִי לֹא יָדָעְתִּי
וַיִּירָא וַיֹּאמַר מַה־נּוֹרָא הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם־בֵּית אֱלֹהִים וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם
cards.en: Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “Surely יהוה is present in this place, and I did not know it!” Shaken, he said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the abode of God, and that is the gateway to heaven.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikatz Yaakov mish'nato vayomer achein yeish Adonai bamakom hazeh v'anochi lo yadati
Vayira vayomar ma nora hamakom hazeh ein zeh ki im beit Elohim v'zeh sha-ar hashamayim

cards.he: אָכֵן יֵשׁ יְיָ בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה וְאָנֹכִי לֹא יָדָעְתִּי
cards.tl: Achein yeish Adonai bamakom hazeh v'anochi lo yadati
cards.gloss: "Surely Adonai is present in this place, and I did not know it!" (28:16). **Rashi**: had I known, I would not have slept in so holy a place.

cards.title: God, the Place
cards.body: The word **makom**, place, appears again and again in this story. The Rabbis call God **HaMakom**, the Place. **Bereshit Rabbah**: God is the place of the world, but the world is **not God's place**: the world is held in God, not the other way around.

cards.q: What does Bereshit Rabbah 68:9 mean by calling God "the Place"?
choices: The world exists within God, not God within the world
God is found only in holy buildings
cards.why: **God is the place of the world**; the world does not contain God.
wrong_why: The midrash says the opposite: no place contains God.
The point is that God is everywhere, holding the world.

cards.body: Friday night you pray **Ma'ariv Aravim**, "who brings on the evening," and **Hashkiveinu**, "help us lie down in peace." The Talmud traces the evening prayer to **Jacob's night** in this place.

points: **Vayifga bamakom**: Jacob begins **Ma'ariv** (Berakhot 26b).
The stones argued, and God **made them one** (Rashi 28:11).
Angels **up, then down**: a change of escort (Rashi 28:12).
"**I am with you** wherever you go" (28:15).
"Surely Adonai is present in this place"; **HaMakom**, God as the Place (Bereshit Rabbah 68:9).

lessons.title: Jacob (4): Rachel, Leah and the switch
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 29:11 and 29:17, Megillah 13b (cited by Rashi on 29:25), read on Sefaria 11/09.

cards.title: Love at the well
cards.body: Like his mother Rebekah, Jacob's story turns at **a well**. He sees **Rachel**, rolls the heavy stone off the well by himself, waters her flock, **kisses her and weeps** (29:9-11).

cards.q: Why did Jacob weep when he met Rachel, in one of Rashi's readings?
choices: He foresaw she would not be buried with him
He was exhausted from the journey
cards.why: Rashi gives two reasons; one is that he foresaw **she would not be buried beside him** in Machpelah.

cards.he:
עוֹדֶנּוּ מְדַבֵּר עִמָּם וְרָחֵל בָּאָה עִם־הַצֹּאן אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיהָ כִּי רֹעָה הִוא
וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה יַעֲקֹב אֶת־רָחֵל בַּת־לָבָן אֲחִי אִמּוֹ וְאֶת־צֹאן לָבָן אֲחִי אִמּוֹ וַיִּגַּשׁ יַעֲקֹב וַיָּגֶל אֶת־הָאֶבֶן מֵעַל פִּי הַבְּאֵר וַיַּשְׁקְ אֶת־צֹאן לָבָן אֲחִי אִמּוֹ
וַיִּשַּׁק יַעֲקֹב לְרָחֵל וַיִּשָּׂא אֶת־קֹלוֹ וַיֵּבְךְּ
cards.en: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s flock—for she was its shepherd. And when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, and the flock of his uncle Laban, Jacob went up and rolled the stone off the mouth of the well, and watered the flock of his uncle Laban. Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and broke into tears.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Odenu m'dabeir imam v'racheil ba-ah im hatzon asher l'aviha ki ro-ah hi
Vay'hi ka-asher ra-ah Yaakov et Rachel bat lavan achi imo v'et tzon lavan achi imo vayigash Yaakov vayagel et ha-even mei-al pi hab'eir vayashk et tzon lavan achi imo
Vayishak Yaakov l'racheil vayisa et kolo vayeivk

cards.title: Why he wept
cards.body: **Rashi** offers two answers. He foresaw that Rachel **would not be buried with him** in the cave of Machpelah. Or: he came **empty-handed**. His grandfather's servant had brought rings and bracelets for Rebekah; Jacob had nothing.

cards.he:
וּלְלָבָן שְׁתֵּי בָנוֹת שֵׁם הַגְּדֹלָה לֵאָה וְשֵׁם הַקְּטַנָּה רָחֵל
וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת וְרָחֵל הָיְתָה יְפַת־תֹּאַר וִיפַת מַרְאֶה
וַיֶּאֱהַב יַעֲקֹב אֶת־רָחֵל וַיֹּאמֶר אֶעֱבׇדְךָ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים בְּרָחֵל בִּתְּךָ הַקְּטַנָּה
cards.en: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older one was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel. Leah had weak eyes; Rachel was shapely and beautiful. Jacob loved Rachel; so he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Ul'lavan sh'tei vanot sheim hag'dolah Leah v'sheim hak'tanah Rachel
V'einei Leah rakot v'racheil haytah y'fat to-ar vifat mar'eh
Vaye-ehav Yaakov et Rachel vayomer e-evodcha sheva shanim b'racheil bit'cha hak'tanah

cards.he: וְעֵינֵי לֵאָה רַכּוֹת
cards.tl: V'einei Leah rakot
cards.gloss: "Leah had weak eyes" (29:17). **Rashi**: tender **from weeping**. People said Rebekah had two sons and Laban two daughters, the older for the older; so Leah cried, afraid she would have to marry **Esau**.

cards.he: וַיִּהְיוּ בְעֵינָיו כְּיָמִים אֲחָדִים בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתָהּ
cards.tl: Vayihyu v'einav k'yamim achadim b'ahavato otah
cards.gloss: Seven years of work, and "they seemed to him but a few days because of his love for her" (29:20).

cards.q: How did Jacob's seven years of work feel to him?
cards.why: "They seemed to him but **a few days** because of his love for her" (29:20).
wrong_why: The verse says the opposite.
The Torah ties the time to love, not punishment.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי בָעֶרֶב וַיִּקַּח אֶת־לֵאָה בִתּוֹ וַיָּבֵא אֹתָהּ אֵלָיו וַיָּבֹא אֵלֶיהָ
וַיִּתֵּן לָבָן לָהּ אֶת־זִלְפָּה שִׁפְחָתוֹ לְלֵאָה בִתּוֹ שִׁפְחָה
וַיְהִי בַבֹּקֶר וְהִנֵּה־הִוא לֵאָה וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־לָבָן מַה־זֹּאת עָשִׂיתָ לִּי הֲלֹא בְרָחֵל עָבַדְתִּי עִמָּךְ וְלָמָּה רִמִּיתָנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר לָבָן לֹא־יֵעָשֶׂה כֵן בִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ לָתֵת הַצְּעִירָה לִפְנֵי הַבְּכִירָה
cards.en: When evening came, he took his daughter Leah and brought her to him; and he cohabited with her.— Laban had given his maidservant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maid.— When morning came, there was Leah! So he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? I was in your service for Rachel! Why did you deceive me?” Laban said, “It is not the practice in our place to marry off the younger before the older.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi va-erev vayikach et Leah vito vayavei otah eilav vayavo eileha
Vayitein lavan lah et zilpah shifchato l'lei-ah vito shifchah
Vay'hi vaboker v'hinei hi Leah vayomer el lavan ma zot asita li halo v'racheil avadti imach v'lamah rimitani
Vayomer lavan lo yei-aseh chein bimkomeinu lateit hatz'irah lifnei hab'chirah

cards.title: Rachel's signs
cards.body: How could Jacob not know? The Talmud: Jacob and Rachel had agreed on **secret signs** so he would know her. When Laban planned the switch, Rachel thought her sister would be **put to shame**, and **gave Leah the signs**.

cards.q: In Megillah 13b, why did Rachel give Leah the secret signs?
choices: So her sister would not be shamed
Because she didn't want to marry Jacob
cards.why: Rachel chose **her sister's dignity** over her own wedding night.
wrong_why: The Talmud says she loved Jacob; she acted for Leah.
The Talmud credits Rachel's own choice.

cards.body: In the Amidah's first blessing you name both sisters: **Elohei Rachel v'Elohei Leah**, God of Rachel and God of Leah.

cards.prompt: Laban says: "It is not the practice in our place to marry off the younger before the older" (29:26). Jacob once took his older brother's place. What do you make of the echo?

points: Jacob meets Rachel **at a well**, and weeps (Rashi: two reasons).
Leah's eyes were tender **from weeping** (Rashi 29:17).
Seven years were **like a few days**.
Rachel gave Leah **the signs**, to spare her shame (Megillah 13b).
Both sisters are in the Amidah: **Elohei Rachel v'Elohei Leah**.

lessons.title: Jacob (5): Leah's thanks, Rachel's longing
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Berakhot 7b and Rashi on Genesis 30:22, read on Sefaria 11/09. The root link odeh / Yehudah / Modim is a plain fact of Hebrew.

cards.title: Two sisters, two kinds of pain
cards.body: **Leah** has children but is **unloved**. **Rachel** is loved but has **no children** (29:31). The Torah tells both sides.

cards.q: The Talmud says Leah was the first person ever to thank God.
cards.why: **Berakhot 7b**: from the day God created the world, no one thanked God until Leah.

cards.he: וַיַּרְא יְיָ כִּי־שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת־רַחְמָהּ וְרָחֵל עֲקָרָה
cards.en: Seeing that Leah was unloved, יהוה opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayar Adonai ki s'nu-ah Leah vayiftach et rachmah v'racheil akarah

cards.he: וַתַּהַר עוֹד וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתֹּאמֶר הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת־יְיָ עַל־כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יְהוּדָה וַתַּעֲמֹד מִלֶּדֶת
cards.en: She conceived again and bore a son, and declared, “This time I will praise יהוה.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vatahar od vateiled bein vatomer hapa-am odeh et Adonai al kein kar'ah sh'mo Y'hudah vata-amod miledet

cards.he: הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת־יְיָ
cards.tl: Hapa-am odeh et Adonai
cards.gloss: "This time I will praise Adonai" (29:35), and she names her fourth son **Yehudah**, Judah. **Berakhot 7b**: from the day the world was created, **no one thanked God until Leah**.

cards.title: One root, three words
cards.body: Leah's **odeh**, I will praise or thank, shares its root with **Yehudah**, Judah, the name behind the word **Jew**, and with **Modim** in the Amidah ("We are thankful to You," in the Metsudah translation).

cards.q: Why does Berakhot 7b single out Leah?
choices: She was the first person to thank God
She was the oldest of the matriarchs
cards.why: "This time I will praise Adonai": the Talmud calls it **the first thanks** since creation.
wrong_why: Age isn't the Talmud's point here.
She named her own sons, not all twelve.

cards.he:
וַתֵּרֶא רָחֵל כִּי לֹא יָלְדָה לְיַעֲקֹב וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל בַּאֲחֹתָהּ וַתֹּאמֶר אֶל־יַעֲקֹב הָבָה־לִּי בָנִים וְאִם־אַיִן מֵתָה אָנֹכִי
וַיִּחַר־אַף יַעֲקֹב בְּרָחֵל וַיֹּאמֶר הֲתַחַת אֱלֹהִים אָנֹכִי אֲשֶׁר־מָנַע מִמֵּךְ פְּרִי־בָטֶן
cards.en: When Rachel saw that she had borne Jacob no children, she became envious of her sister; and Rachel said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I shall die.” Jacob was incensed at Rachel, and said, “Can I take the place of God, who has denied you fruit of the womb?”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vateire Rachel ki lo yaldah l'ya-akov vat'kanei Rachel ba-achotah vatomer el Yaakov havah li vanim v'im ayin meitah anochi
Vayichar af Yaakov b'racheil vayomer hatachat Elohim anochi asher mana mimeich p'ri vaten

cards.title: Two cries
cards.body: Rachel: "Give me children, or I shall die." Jacob, angry: "Can I take the place of God, who has denied you fruit of the womb?" (30:1-2). The Torah keeps **both** voices, the pain and the anger, without smoothing them over.

cards.he:
וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת־רָחֵל וַיִּשְׁמַע אֵלֶיהָ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת־רַחְמָהּ
וַתַּהַר וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתֹּאמֶר אָסַף אֱלֹהִים אֶת־חֶרְפָּתִי
וַתִּקְרָא אֶת־שְׁמוֹ יוֹסֵף לֵאמֹר יֹסֵף יְיָ לִי בֵּן אַחֵר
cards.en: Now God remembered Rachel; God heeded her and opened her womb. She conceived and bore a son, and said, “God has taken away my disgrace.” So she named him Joseph, which is to say, “May יהוה add another son for me.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayizkor Elohim et Rachel vayishma eileha Elohim vayiftach et rachmah
Vatahar vateiled bein vatomer asaf Elohim et cherpati
Vatikra et sh'mo yoseif leimor yoseif Adonai li bein acheir

cards.title: God remembered Rachel
cards.body: **Rashi**: God remembered to Rachel's merit that she **gave her sister the signs**, and her fear that, being childless, she might be divorced and fall to **Esau**.

cards.q: According to Rashi, what did God remember about Rachel?
choices: That she gave Leah the signs
That she had prayed the longest
cards.why: Her kindness to her sister, years before, is **remembered** now.
wrong_why: Rashi doesn't make favoritism the reason.
Rashi names a different merit.

cards.body: When you bow at **Modim**, "We are thankful to You" (Metsudah), you use **Leah's word**.

points: Leah unloved, Rachel childless: **two kinds of pain**.
"**This time I will praise Adonai**": the first thanks (Berakhot 7b).
Odeh, **Yehudah**, **Modim**: one root.
Rachel's cry and Jacob's anger, both kept.
God remembered Rachel's **kindness to her sister** (Rashi 30:22).

lessons.title: Jacob (6): Rachel weeping for her children
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 48:7 and Megillah 31a, read on Sefaria 11/09. CBB's Rosh Hashanah haftarah not checked. Ben-oni left untranslated (the Contemporary Torah doesn't translate it).

cards.title: A grave by the road
cards.body: On the journey home, **Rachel dies giving birth** to her second son. Jacob buries her **by the road** to Ephrath, now Bethlehem, not in the family cave (35:16-20).

cards.q: Where does the Torah say Rachel was buried?
choices: On the road to Ephrath, now Bethlehem
cards.why: **On the road** (35:19), and Jacob set up a pillar over her grave.

cards.he:
וַיִּסְעוּ מִבֵּית אֵל וַיְהִי־עוֹד כִּבְרַת־הָאָרֶץ לָבוֹא אֶפְרָתָה וַתֵּלֶד רָחֵל וַתְּקַשׁ בְּלִדְתָּהּ
וַיְהִי בְהַקְשֹׁתָהּ בְּלִדְתָּהּ וַתֹּאמֶר לָהּ הַמְיַלֶּדֶת אַל־תִּירְאִי כִּי־גַם־זֶה לָךְ בֵּן
וַיְהִי בְּצֵאת נַפְשָׁהּ כִּי מֵתָה וַתִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ בֶּן־אוֹנִי וְאָבִיו קָרָא־לוֹ בִנְיָמִין
וַתָּמׇת רָחֵל וַתִּקָּבֵר בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶפְרָתָה הִוא בֵּית לָחֶם
וַיַּצֵּב יַעֲקֹב מַצֵּבָה עַל־קְבֻרָתָהּ הִוא מַצֶּבֶת קְבֻרַת־רָחֵל עַד־הַיּוֹם
cards.en: They set out from Bethel; but when they were still some distance short of Ephrath, Rachel was in childbirth, and she had hard labor. When her labor was at its hardest, the midwife said to her, “Have no fear, for it is another boy for you.” But as she breathed her last—for she was dying—she named him Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin. Thus Rachel died. She was buried on the road to Ephrath—now Bethlehem. Over her grave Jacob set up a pillar; it is the pillar at Rachel’s grave to this day.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayis'u mibeit eil vay'hi od kivrat ha-aretz lavo efratah vateiled Rachel vat'kash b'lidtah
Vay'hi v'hakshotah b'lidtah vatomer lah hamyaledet al tir'i ki gam zeh lach bein
Vay'hi b'tzeit nafshah ki meitah vatikra sh'mo ben oni v'aviv kara lo vinyamin
Vatamot Rachel vatikaveir b'derech efratah hi beit lachem
Vayatzeiv Yaakov matzeivah al k'vuratah hi matzevet k'vurat Rachel ad hayom

cards.he: בֶּן־אוֹנִי וְאָבִיו קָרָא־לוֹ בִנְיָמִין
cards.tl: Ben oni v'aviv kara lo vinyamin
cards.gloss: Dying, Rachel names her son **Ben-oni**; his father calls him **Benjamin** (35:18).

cards.title: Why by the road?
cards.body: Years later Jacob explains to Joseph. **Rashi**: God told him to bury her there, so that when her children were **led into exile** along that road, Rachel would come out of her grave and **weep and plead** for them.

cards.q: In Rashi's reading, why was Rachel buried on the road?
choices: So she could weep for her children going into exile
Because there was no time to reach Machpelah
cards.why: She would be **there, on their road**, to plead for them.
wrong_why: The verse itself gives no reason; Rashi gives God's.
Laban has no part in this.

cards.he:
כֹּה אָמַר יְיָ קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל־בָּנֶיהָ מֵאֲנָה לְהִנָּחֵם עַל־בָּנֶיהָ כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ
כֹּה אָמַר יְיָ מִנְעִי קוֹלֵךְ מִבֶּכִי וְעֵינַיִךְ מִדִּמְעָה כִּי יֵשׁ שָׂכָר לִפְעֻלָּתֵךְ נְאֻם־יְיָ וְשָׁבוּ מֵאֶרֶץ אוֹיֵב
cards.en: Thus said GOD: A cry is heard in Ramah— Wailing, bitter weeping— Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted For her children, who are gone. Thus said GOD: Restrain your voice from weeping, Your eyes from shedding tears; For there is a reward for your labor —declares GOD: They shall return from the enemy’s land.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Ko amar Adonai kol b'ramah nishma n'hi b'chi tamrurim Rachel m'vakah al baneha mei-anah l'hinacheim al baneha ki einenu
Ko amar Adonai min'i koleich mibechi v'einayich midim'ah ki yeish sachar lif'ulateich n'um Adonai v'shavu mei-eretz oyeiv

cards.he: קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל־בָּנֶיהָ
cards.tl: Kol b'ramah nishma n'hi b'chi tamrurim Rachel m'vakah al baneha
cards.gloss: "A cry is heard in Ramah... Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted" (Jeremiah 31:15). God doesn't scold her. God answers: "Restrain your voice from weeping... They shall return from the enemy's land" (31:16).

cards.q: In Jeremiah 31, how does God answer Rachel's weeping?
choices: With a promise that her children will return
By telling her to stop grieving
cards.why: "**They shall return** from the enemy's land."
wrong_why: God says to restrain her tears, but because of the promise that follows.
God answers her directly.

cards.body: The Talmud has **Jeremiah 31**, the chapter with Rachel's weeping, as a **Rosh Hashanah haftarah** (Megillah 31a). Check what CBB reads.

cards.prompt: Rachel refuses to be comforted, and God answers with hope instead of correction. What does that say to you about grief? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Rachel dies **on the road**, giving birth to Benjamin.
Rashi: buried there to **weep for her children** in exile.
**A cry is heard in Ramah**: Rachel refuses comfort (Jeremiah 31:15).
God's answer: **they shall return**.
Jeremiah 31 is a **Rosh Hashanah** haftarah (Megillah 31a).

lessons.title: Jacob (7): Wrestling until dawn
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 32:8, 32:11, 32:25 and 32:29 (read on Sefaria 11/10).

cards.title: Alone at night
cards.body: Twenty years after the stolen blessing, Jacob is about to meet **Esau** again. He is afraid. He prays, sends everyone across the river, and is **left alone**. A figure wrestles with him **until dawn** (32:8-25).

cards.q: What new name does Jacob receive that night?
cards.why: **Israel**, "for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed" (32:29).

cards.title: Two fears
cards.body: "Jacob was greatly frightened; in his anxiety..." (32:8). Why two words? **Rashi**: he was afraid **he would be killed**, and distressed that **he might have to kill** someone.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אַבְרָהָם וֵאלֹהֵי אָבִי יִצְחָק יְיָ הָאֹמֵר אֵלַי שׁוּב לְאַרְצְךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ וְאֵיטִיבָה עִמָּךְ
קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים וּמִכׇּל־הָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ אֶת־עַבְדֶּךָ כִּי בְמַקְלִי עָבַרְתִּי אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה וְעַתָּה הָיִיתִי לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת
cards.en: Then Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham’s [house] and God of my father Isaac’s [house], O יהוה, who said to me, ‘Return to your native land and I will deal bountifully with you’! I am unworthy of all the kindness that You have so steadfastly shown Your servant: with my staff alone I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Yaakov Elohei avi Avraham v'Elohei avi Yitzchak Adonai ha-omeir eilai shuv l'artz'cha ul'moladt'cha v'eitivah imach
Katonti mikol hachasadim umikol ha-emet asher asita et avdecha ki v'makli avarti et hayardein hazeh v'atah hayiti lishnei machanot

cards.he: קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים וּמִכׇּל־הָאֱמֶת
cards.tl: Katonti mikol hachasadim umikol ha-emet
cards.gloss: "I am unworthy of all the kindness that You have so steadfastly shown Your servant" (32:11). **Rashi**: my merits are **diminished** by all the kindness You have already shown me.

cards.q: In Rashi's reading of 32:8, what was Jacob's second fear?
choices: That he might have to kill someone
That Esau would take his flocks
cards.why: Afraid of **being killed**, and distressed at the thought of **killing**.
wrong_why: Rashi says nothing about the flocks here.
Rachel isn't part of Rashi's reading.

cards.he:
וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ עַד עֲלוֹת הַשָּׁחַר
וַיַּרְא כִּי לֹא יָכֹל לוֹ וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף־יְרֵכוֹ וַתֵּקַע כַּף־יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ
וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא אֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ כִּי אִם־בֵּרַכְתָּנִי
cards.en: Jacob was left alone. And a figure wrestled with him until the break of dawn. When he saw that he had not prevailed against him, he wrenched Jacob’s hip at its socket, so that the socket of his hip was strained as he wrestled with him. Then he said, “Let me go, for dawn is breaking.” But he answered, “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayivateir Yaakov l'vado vayei-aveik ish imo ad alot hashachar
Vayar ki lo yachol lo vayiga b'chaf y'reicho vateika kaf yerech Yaakov b'hei-avko imo
Vayomer shal'cheini ki alah hashachar vayomer lo ashaleichacha ki im beirachtani

cards.title: Who was the figure?
cards.body: The Torah says only **"a figure"** (in Hebrew, a man). **Rashi**: the Rabbis explained he was **Esau's guardian angel**. By morning Jacob says he has seen **a divine being face to face** (32:31).

cards.he: לֹא אֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ כִּי אִם־בֵּרַכְתָּנִי
cards.tl: Lo ashaleichacha ki im beirachtani
cards.gloss: "I will not let you go, unless you bless me" (32:27). Wounded at the hip, Jacob **holds on**.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו מַה־שְּׁמֶךָ וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב
וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא יַעֲקֹב יֵאָמֵר עוֹד שִׁמְךָ כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל
וַיִּשְׁאַל יַעֲקֹב וַיֹּאמֶר הַגִּידָה־נָּא שְׁמֶךָ וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָּה זֶּה תִּשְׁאַל לִשְׁמִי וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתוֹ שָׁם
cards.en: Said the other, “What is your name?” He replied, “Jacob.” Said he, “Your name shall no longer be Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed.” Jacob asked, “Pray tell me your name.” But he said, “You must not ask my name!” And he took leave of him there.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer eilav ma sh'mecha vayomer Yaakov
Vayomer lo Yaakov yei-ameir od shimcha ki im Yisrael ki sarita im Elohim v'im anashim vatuchol
Vayish'al Yaakov vayomer hagidah na sh'mecha vayomer lamah zeh tish'al lishmi vay'varech oto sham

cards.he: כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל
cards.tl: Ki im Yisrael ki sarita im Elohim v'im anashim vatuchol
cards.gloss: "...but Israel, for you have striven with beings divine and human, and have prevailed" (32:29). **Rashi**: no longer will it be said that the blessings came to you **by supplanting**, but by **noble conduct**, in the open.

cards.q: According to Rashi, what does the change from Jacob to Israel mean?
choices: His blessings now come openly, not by supplanting
He is forbidden to use the name Jacob
cards.why: **Yaakov** echoes the heel and supplanting; **Yisrael**, striving and prevailing in the open.
wrong_why: Rashi doesn't speak of kingship.
The Torah keeps calling him Jacob too; Rashi's point is how his blessings are earned.

cards.title: Limping into the sunrise
cards.body: Jacob names the place **Peniel**: "I have seen a divine being face to face, yet my life has been preserved." Then "the sun rose upon him" as he passed, **limping on his hip** (32:31-32).
Every time you say **Sh'ma Yisrael**, you use the name Jacob earned that night.

cards.prompt: Jacob won't let go until he's blessed, and walks away limping. Is there a struggle you've come through changed? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Rashi 32:8: afraid **to be killed**, and **to kill**.
"**I am unworthy** of all the kindness" (32:11).
A figure, Rashi: **Esau's guardian angel**.
"**I will not let you go, unless you bless me.**"
**Israel**: blessings won in the open (Rashi 32:29); Jacob limps into the sunrise.

lessons.title: Jacob (8): Esau runs to meet him
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 33:4 (from Bereshit Rabbah 78:8 and Sifrei Bamidbar 69), read on Sefaria 11/10. The dots over vayishakehu are in Sefaria's Masorah text.

cards.title: Four hundred men
cards.body: Jacob sees **Esau coming with four hundred men**. He places his family in rows, **Rachel and Joseph last**, walks ahead, and **bows to the ground seven times** (33:1-3).

cards.q: When they meet, Esau attacks Jacob.
cards.why: "Esau **ran** to greet him. He **embraced** him and, falling on his neck, he **kissed** him; and **they wept**" (33:4).

cards.he:
וַיִּשָּׂא יַעֲקֹב עֵינָיו וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה עֵשָׂו בָּא וְעִמּוֹ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אִישׁ וַיַּחַץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִים עַל־לֵאָה וְעַל־רָחֵל וְעַל שְׁתֵּי הַשְּׁפָחוֹת
וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־הַשְּׁפָחוֹת וְאֶת־יַלְדֵיהֶן רִאשֹׁנָה וְאֶת־לֵאָה וִילָדֶיהָ אַחֲרֹנִים וְאֶת־רָחֵל וְאֶת־יוֹסֵף אַחֲרֹנִים
וְהוּא עָבַר לִפְנֵיהֶם וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ אַרְצָה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים עַד־גִּשְׁתּוֹ עַד־אָחִיו
וַיָּרׇץ עֵשָׂו לִקְרָאתוֹ וַיְחַבְּקֵהוּ וַיִּפֹּל עַל־צַוָּארָו וַׄיִּׄשָּׁׄקֵׄהׄוּׄ וַיִּבְכּוּ
cards.en: Looking up, Jacob saw Esau coming, with a retinue of four hundred. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maids, putting the maids and their children first, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph last. He himself went on ahead and bowed low to the ground seven times until he was near his brother. Esau ran to greet him. He embraced him and, falling on his neck, he kissed him; and they wept.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayisa Yaakov einav vayar v'hinei eisav ba v'imo arba mei-ot ish vayachatz et hayladim al Leah v'al Rachel v'al sh'tei hash'fachot
Vayasem et hash'fachot v'et yaldeihen rishonah v'et Leah viladeha acharonim v'et Rachel v'et yoseif acharonim
V'hu avar lifneihem vayishtachu artzah sheva p'amim ad gishto ad achiv
Vayarotz eisav likrato vaychab'keihu vayipol al tzavarav vayishakeihu vayivku
Vayishakeihu
cards.gloss: "he kissed him" (33:4). In the Masoretic text this word carries **dots over its letters**. **Rashi**: the sages disagreed. Some say Esau **did not kiss him wholeheartedly**. **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**: Esau hated Jacob, but at that moment his **pity was truly aroused**, and he kissed him **with his whole heart**.

cards.q: What does Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai learn from the dots over "he kissed him"?
choices: At that moment Esau kissed him with his whole heart
cards.why: Despite the old hatred, **in that moment** Esau's pity was real.
wrong_why: That's the other opinion Rashi reports.
No one suggests erasing it; the dots invite interpretation.

cards.title: Why he embraced him
cards.body: **Rashi**: Esau's pity was aroused when he saw Jacob **bowing to the ground so many times**. Seven bows, and a twenty-year grudge gives way.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אַל־נָא אִם־נָא מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ מִנְחָתִי מִיָּדִי כִּי עַל־כֵּן רָאִיתִי פָנֶיךָ כִּרְאֹת פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים וַתִּרְצֵנִי
cards.en: But Jacob said, “No, I pray you; if you would do me this favor, accept from me this gift; for to see your face is like seeing the face of God, and you have received me favorably.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomer Yaakov al na im na matzati chein b'einecha v'lakachta minchati miyadi ki al kein ra-iti fanecha kir'ot p'nei Elohim vatirtzeini

cards.he: רָאִיתִי פָנֶיךָ כִּרְאֹת פְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים
cards.tl: Ra-iti fanecha kir'ot p'nei Elohim
cards.gloss: "to see your face is like seeing the face of God" (33:10). The night before, Jacob saw a divine being **face to face** (32:31). Now he sees God in **his brother's face**.

cards.q: What does Jacob tell Esau seeing his face is like?
cards.why: "To see your face is like **seeing the face of God**" (33:10).
wrong_why: Isaac isn't mentioned here.
Not in the text.

cards.prompt: Twenty years after the stolen blessing, Esau runs to his brother. What do you think made this meeting possible?

points: Jacob bows **seven times**; Esau **runs** to him.
Dots over "he kissed him": Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, **with his whole heart** (Rashi 33:4).
Esau's pity was aroused by Jacob's bowing.
"To see your face is like seeing **the face of God**."

lessons.title: Joseph (1): The tunic, the dreams and the pit
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 37:15, 37:24 and 37:35 (read on Sefaria 11/11). 'Coat of many colours' is the King James rendering.

cards.title: The favorite son
cards.body: "Israel loved Joseph best of all his sons" and gave him **an ornamented tunic**. His brothers **hated him**, and then Joseph told them **his dreams** (37:3-7).

cards.q: "The pit was empty; there was no water in it" (37:24). According to Rashi, what was in it?
cards.why: Why add "no water" if it was empty? **Rashi**: no water, but **snakes and scorpions**.

cards.he:
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת־יוֹסֵף מִכׇּל־בָּנָיו כִּי־בֶן־זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ וְעָשָׂה לוֹ כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים
וַיִּרְאוּ אֶחָיו כִּי־אֹתוֹ אָהַב אֲבִיהֶם מִכׇּל־אֶחָיו וַיִּשְׂנְאוּ אֹתוֹ וְלֹא יָכְלוּ דַּבְּרוֹ לְשָׁלֹם
cards.en: Now Israel loved Joseph best of all his sons—he was his “child of old age”; and he had made him an ornamented tunic. And when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of his brothers, they hated him so that they could not speak a friendly word to him.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'Yisrael ahav et yoseif mikol banav ki ven z'kunim hu lo v'asah lo k'tonet pasim
Vayir'u echav ki oto ahav avihem mikol echav vayisn'u oto v'lo yachlu dab'ro l'shalom

cards.he: כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים
cards.tl: K'tonet pasim
cards.gloss: "an ornamented tunic" (37:3). The rare Hebrew word for its decoration has been translated many ways; the King James Bible made it the famous "coat of many colours."

cards.he:
וַיַּחֲלֹם יוֹסֵף חֲלוֹם וַיַּגֵּד לְאֶחָיו וַיּוֹסִפוּ עוֹד שְׂנֹא אֹתוֹ
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם שִׁמְעוּ־נָא הַחֲלוֹם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר חָלָמְתִּי
וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶה וְהִנֵּה קָמָה אֲלֻמָּתִי וְגַם־נִצָּבָה וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמֹּתֵיכֶם וַתִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶיןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִי
cards.en: Once Joseph had a dream which he told to his brothers; and they hated him even more. He said to them, “Hear this dream which I have dreamed: There we were binding sheaves in the field, when suddenly my sheaf stood up and remained upright; then your sheaves gathered around and bowed low to my sheaf.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayachalom yoseif chalom vayageid l'echav vayosifu od s'no oto
Vayomer aleihem shim'u na hachalom hazeh asher chalamti
V'hinei anachnu m'al'mim alumim b'toch hasadeh v'hinei kamah alumati v'gam nitzavah v'hinei t'subenah alumoteichem vatishtachavena la-alumati

cards.title: The man in the field
cards.body: On his way to his brothers, "a man came upon him wandering in the fields" (37:15). An ordinary stranger? **Rashi**: this was **the angel Gabriel**.

cards.he: אֶת־אַחַי אָנֹכִי מְבַקֵּשׁ
cards.tl: Et achai anochi m'vakeish
cards.gloss: "I am looking for my brothers" (37:16): said by the boy his brothers hate, on his way to find them.

cards.q: Who does Rashi say the "man" in the field was?
cards.why: **Gabriel**: a hidden messenger who keeps the story moving.
wrong_why: The brothers were already gone to Dothan.
That's the plain reading; Rashi brings the midrash.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר־בָּא יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו וַיַּפְשִׁיטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף אֶת־כֻּתׇּנְתּוֹ אֶת־כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו
וַיִּקָּחֻהוּ וַיַּשְׁלִכוּ אֹתוֹ הַבֹּרָה וְהַבּוֹר רֵק אֵין בּוֹ מָיִם
cards.en: When Joseph came up to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the ornamented tunic that he was wearing, and took him and cast him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi ka-asher ba yoseif el echav vayafshitu et yoseif et kutonto et k'tonet hapasim asher alav
Vayikachuhu vayashlichu oto haborah v'habor reik ein bo mayim

cards.title: Empty, but not empty
cards.body: "The pit was **empty**; there was **no water** in it." Why say both? **Rashi**, from the Talmud: there was no water, but there were **snakes and scorpions**.

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרַע יַעֲקֹב שִׂמְלֹתָיו וַיָּשֶׂם שַׂק בְּמׇתְנָיו וַיִּתְאַבֵּל עַל־בְּנוֹ יָמִים רַבִּים
וַיָּקֻמוּ כׇל־בָּנָיו וְכׇל־בְּנֹתָיו לְנַחֲמוֹ וַיְמָאֵן לְהִתְנַחֵם וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי־אֵרֵד אֶל־בְּנִי אָבֵל שְׁאֹלָה וַיֵּבְךְּ אֹתוֹ אָבִיו
cards.en: Jacob rent his clothes, put sackcloth on his loins, and observed mourning for his son many days. All his sons and daughters sought to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted, saying, “No, I will go down mourning to my son in Sheol.” Thus his father bewailed him.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra Yaakov simlotav vayasem sak b'motnav vayit'abeil al b'no yamim rabim
Vayakumu chol banav v'chol b'notav l'nachamo vayma-ein l'hitnacheim vayomer ki eireid el b'ni aveil sh'olah vayeivk oto aviv

cards.title: He refused to be comforted
cards.body: Jacob mourns and **refuses to be comforted** (37:35). **Rashi**: no one can be comforted over someone **still alive** who is thought dead. It is decreed that the dead are slowly forgotten from the heart, but not the living. Joseph is alive.

cards.q: Why, in Rashi's reading, could Jacob not be comforted?
choices: He blamed himself for the tunic
cards.why: Comfort comes for **the dead**, who fade from the heart. Joseph was **alive**.
wrong_why: "All his sons and daughters sought to comfort him" (37:35).
Rashi gives a different reason.

points: A favorite son, **an ornamented tunic**, and dreams.
Rashi: the man in the field was **Gabriel**.
"**I am looking for my brothers.**"
The pit: no water, but **snakes and scorpions** (Rashi).
Jacob **refuses comfort**: Joseph is alive (Rashi 37:35).

lessons.title: Joseph (2): Judah and Tamar
lessons.check_note: Sotah 10b read on Sefaria 11/11. 'Haker na' in 37:32 and 38:25: same Hebrew words, checked in the Masorah text.

cards.title: A detour to Judah
cards.body: In the middle of Joseph's story, the Torah turns to **Judah**. His widowed daughter-in-law **Tamar** is denied the marriage she was promised. When she is found pregnant and condemned, she quietly sends Judah his own **seal, cord and staff** (38:24-25).

cards.q: Tamar publicly names Judah as the father.
cards.why: She only sends a message: "Examine these: whose seal and cord and staff are these?" (38:25). Judah must decide whether to speak.

cards.he:
הִוא מוּצֵאת וְהִיא שָׁלְחָה אֶל־חָמִיהָ לֵאמֹר לְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אֵלֶּה לּוֹ אָנֹכִי הָרָה וַתֹּאמֶר הַכֶּר־נָא לְמִי הַחֹתֶמֶת וְהַפְּתִילִים וְהַמַּטֶּה הָאֵלֶּה
וַיַּכֵּר יְהוּדָה וַיֹּאמֶר צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי כִּי־עַל־כֵּן לֹא־נְתַתִּיהָ לְשֵׁלָה בְנִי וְלֹא־יָסַף עוֹד לְדַעְתָּהּ
cards.en: As she was being brought out, she sent this message to her father-in-law, “It’s by the man to whom these belong that I’m pregnant.” And she added, “Examine these: whose seal and cord and staff are these?” Judah recognized them, and said, “She is more in the right than I, inasmuch as I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he was not intimate with her again.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Hi mutzeit v'hi shalchah el chamiha leimor l'ish asher eileh lo anochi harah vatomer haker na l'mi hachotemet v'hap'tilim v'hamateh ha-eileh
Vayakeir Y'hudah vayomer tzadkah mimeni ki al kein lo n'tatiha l'sheilah v'ni v'lo yasaf od l'datah

cards.title: Better a furnace than shaming another
cards.body: The Talmud learns from Tamar: she was ready to be **burned** rather than **humiliate Judah in public**. So it is better to throw yourself into a fiery furnace than to shame another person publicly.

cards.q: What does Sotah 10b learn from Tamar?
choices: Never shame another person in public, even at great cost
cards.why: Tamar risked her life **rather than shame Judah**.
wrong_why: She did the opposite, protecting Judah's dignity.
She sent the evidence, but privately.

cards.he: צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי
cards.tl: Tzadkah mimeni
cards.gloss: "She is more in the right than I" (38:26). **Judah's first admission** of wrong, long before he offers himself in Benjamin's place.

cards.he: הַכֶּר־נָא
cards.tl: Haker na
cards.gloss: "Examine these" (38:25). In Hebrew it is the very phrase the brothers used when they showed Jacob Joseph's bloodied tunic (37:32). The deceiver is now the one asked **to recognize**.

cards.q: Why does Tamar's "examine these" echo chapter 37?
choices: The brothers said the same words to Jacob about Joseph's tunic
It is the name of Judah's son
cards.why: The words that deceived Jacob now confront Judah.
wrong_why: Not those words in Pharaoh's court.
His sons are Er, Onan and Shelah.

cards.prompt: Tamar chose not to shame Judah, and Judah chose to tell the truth. Which of those two choices is harder for you?

points: Tamar sends Judah his **seal, cord and staff**, privately.
Sotah 10b: **better a furnace** than shaming someone in public.
"**She is more in the right than I**": Judah's first teshuvah.
"Examine these": the words of the tunic, **returned**.

lessons.title: Joseph (3): Adonai was with Joseph
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Rashi on Genesis 39:3 (from Tanchuma) and Sotah 36b (cited by Rashi on 39:11), read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: A slave in Egypt
cards.body: Sold by his brothers, Joseph becomes a slave in the house of Potiphar, an Egyptian official. Yet the Torah says, "Adonai was with Joseph" (39:2).

cards.q: Joseph's Egyptian master could tell that God was with him.
cards.why: "His master saw that Adonai was with him" (39:3). Rashi explains **how** he could see it.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי יְיָ אֶת־יוֹסֵף וַיְהִי אִישׁ מַצְלִיחַ וַיְהִי בְּבֵית אֲדֹנָיו הַמִּצְרִי
וַיַּרְא אֲדֹנָיו כִּי יְיָ אִתּוֹ וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־הוּא עֹשֶׂה יְיָ מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ
cards.en: יהוה was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he stayed in the house of his Egyptian master. And when his master saw that יהוה was with him and that יהוה lent success to everything he undertook,
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi Adonai et yoseif vay'hi ish matzliach vay'hi b'veit adonav hamitzri
Vayar adonav ki Adonai ito v'chol asher hu oseh Adonai matzliach b'yado

cards.title: God's name in his mouth
cards.body: How could an Egyptian **see** that God was with Joseph? **Rashi**: the name of God was **always on his lips**. God's presence showed in how Joseph spoke and acted.

cards.q: According to Rashi, how did Potiphar see that God was with Joseph?
choices: God's name was always on Joseph's lips
Joseph told him about his dreams
cards.why: Not miracles: **Joseph's own speech** made God visible.
wrong_why: The Torah describes no miracles here.
The dreams aren't part of Rashi's answer.

cards.he:
וַיְמָאֵן וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־אֵשֶׁת אֲדֹנָיו הֵן אֲדֹנִי לֹא־יָדַע אִתִּי מַה־בַּבָּיִת וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יֶשׁ־לוֹ נָתַן בְּיָדִי
אֵינֶנּוּ גָדוֹל בַּבַּיִת הַזֶּה מִמֶּנִּי וְלֹא־חָשַׂךְ מִמֶּנִּי מְאוּמָה כִּי אִם־אוֹתָךְ בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֵיךְ אֶעֱשֶׂה הָרָעָה הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת וְחָטָאתִי לֵאלֹהִים
cards.en: But he refused. He said to his master’s wife, “Look, with me here, my master gives no thought to anything in this house, and all that he owns he has placed in my hands. He wields no more authority in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except yourself, since you are his wife. How then could I do this most wicked thing, and sin before God?”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayma-ein vayomer el eishet adonav hein adoni lo yada iti ma babayit v'chol asher yesh lo natan b'yadi
Einenu gadol babayit hazeh mimeni v'lo chasach mimeni m'umah ki im otach ba-asher at ishto v'eich e-eseh hara-ah hag'dolah hazot v'chatati leilohim

cards.title: His father's face
cards.body: Potiphar's wife tries again and again to seduce Joseph. The Talmud: at the moment of greatest temptation, **his father's image appeared to him in the window**, and reminded him of **his place among his brothers**. Joseph fled.

cards.q: In Sotah 36b, what helped Joseph resist?
choices: His father's image appeared to him
cards.why: **Jacob's face**, and the memory of who Joseph was meant to be.
wrong_why: The Talmud's answer is more inward than that.
His own words (39:9) are about loyalty and sin, not fear.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו חֲלוֹם חָלַמְנוּ וּפֹתֵר אֵין אֹתוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם יוֹסֵף הֲלוֹא לֵאלֹהִים פִּתְרֹנִים סַפְּרוּ־נָא לִי
cards.en: And they said to him, “We had dreams, and there is no one to interpret them.” So Joseph said to them, “Surely God can interpret! Tell me [your dreams].”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomru eilav chalom chalamnu ufoteir ein oto vayomer aleihem yoseif halo leilohim pitronim sap'ru na li

cards.he: הֲלוֹא לֵאלֹהִים פִּתְרֹנִים
cards.tl: Halo leilohim pitronim
cards.gloss: "Surely God can interpret!" (40:8). In prison, Joseph gives the credit away before he even hears the dreams.

cards.prompt: Joseph is a slave, then a prisoner, and still the Torah says God was with him. In this story, where does God's presence actually show up?

points: "**Adonai was with Joseph**," even as a slave.
Rashi: God's name was **always on his lips**.
Sotah 36b: **his father's face** in the window.
"**Surely God can interpret!**"

lessons.title: Joseph (4): Pharaoh's dreams
lessons.check_note: Torah text only, plus the custom of blessing children with Ephraim and Manasseh (Genesis 48:20).

cards.title: From prison to palace
cards.body: Pharaoh dreams of **seven fat cows and seven lean ones**, and no one can explain it. Joseph is brought **straight from prison** (41:1-15).

cards.q: Pharaoh says Joseph can interpret any dream. What does Joseph answer?
choices: "Not I! God will see to Pharaoh's welfare."
cards.why: "**Not I!**" (41:16). Again Joseph points away from himself.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה אֶל־יוֹסֵף חֲלוֹם חָלַמְתִּי וּפֹתֵר אֵין אֹתוֹ וַאֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי עָלֶיךָ לֵאמֹר תִּשְׁמַע חֲלוֹם לִפְתֹּר אֹתוֹ
וַיַּעַן יוֹסֵף אֶת־פַּרְעֹה לֵאמֹר בִּלְעָדָי אֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶה אֶת־שְׁלוֹם פַּרְעֹה
cards.en: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have had a dream, but no one can interpret it. Now I have heard it said of you that for you to hear a dream is to tell its meaning.” Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Not I! God will see to Pharaoh’s welfare.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer par'o el yoseif chalom chalamti ufoteir ein oto va-ani shamati alecha leimor tishma chalom liftor oto
Vaya-an yoseif et par'o leimor bil'adai Elohim ya-aneh et sh'lom par'o

cards.he: בִּלְעָדָי אֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶה אֶת־שְׁלוֹם פַּרְעֹה
cards.tl: Bil'adai Elohim ya-aneh et sh'lom par'o
cards.gloss: "Not I! God will see to Pharaoh's welfare" (41:16). Before he names God, Joseph answers in **a single Hebrew word**.

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרָא יוֹסֵף אֶת־שֵׁם הַבְּכוֹר מְנַשֶּׁה כִּי־נַשַּׁנִי אֱלֹהִים אֶת־כׇּל־עֲמָלִי וְאֵת כׇּל־בֵּית אָבִי
וְאֵת שֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִי קָרָא אֶפְרָיִם כִּי־הִפְרַנִי אֱלֹהִים בְּאֶרֶץ עׇנְיִי
cards.en: Joseph named the first-born Manasseh, meaning, “God has made me forget completely my hardship and my parental home.” And the second he named Ephraim, meaning, “God has made me fertile in the land of my affliction.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra yoseif et sheim hab'chor m'nasheh ki nashani Elohim et kol amali v'eit kol beit avi
V'eit sheim hasheini kara efrayim ki hifrani Elohim b'eretz onyi

cards.title: Two names
cards.body: Joseph names his sons **Manasseh**, "God has made me forget completely my hardship," and **Ephraim**, "God has made me fertile in the land of my affliction" (41:51-52). Jacob later blesses them, and Jewish parents still bless their sons on Friday night to be like **Ephraim and Manasseh** (48:20).

cards.q: What does the name Ephraim say?
choices: God made me fertile in the land of my affliction
God made me forget my father's house
God made me ruler over Egypt
cards.why: **Ephraim**: fruitful **in the land of affliction** (41:52).
wrong_why: That's Manasseh's name.
Neither name says that.

cards.prompt: Ephraim: "fertile in the land of my affliction." Has anything grown for you in a hard place? It's fine to skip this one.

points: Joseph goes **from prison to Pharaoh**.
"**Not I!** God will see to Pharaoh's welfare."
**Manasseh** and **Ephraim**: forgetting hardship, and growing in it.
Children are still blessed **to be like Ephraim and Manasseh**.

lessons.title: Joseph (5): The brothers and Judah
lessons.check_note: Rambam, Mishneh Torah, Repentance 2:1 (Touger translation on Sefaria), read 11/11. The observation that Genesis 37 records no plea from Joseph is from the text itself.

cards.title: Bowing to a stranger
cards.body: Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt. They **bow** to the governor, as in Joseph's dream. Joseph recognizes them; **they do not recognize him** (42:6-8).

cards.q: When the brothers come to Egypt, they recognize Joseph.
cards.why: Joseph **recognized them**, but **they did not recognize him** (42:8).

cards.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו אֲבָל אֲשֵׁמִים אֲנַחְנוּ עַל־אָחִינוּ אֲשֶׁר רָאִינוּ צָרַת נַפְשׁוֹ בְּהִתְחַנְנוֹ אֵלֵינוּ וְלֹא שָׁמָעְנוּ עַל־כֵּן בָּאָה אֵלֵינוּ הַצָּרָה הַזֹּאת
