cards.en: They said to one another, “Alas, we are being punished on account of our brother, because we looked on at his anguish, yet paid no heed as he pleaded with us. That is why this distress has come upon us.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomru ish el achiv aval asheimim anachnu al achinu asher ra-inu tzarat nafsho b'hitchan'no eileinu v'lo shamanu al kein ba-ah eileinu hatzarah hazot

cards.title: We looked on at his anguish
cards.body: Years later, the brothers say they **watched his anguish** and ignored him **as he pleaded** (42:21). Chapter 37 never mentions Joseph pleading. We hear his cry only now, **through their guilt**.

cards.q: What do we first learn in 42:21 that chapter 37 didn't tell us?
choices: Joseph pleaded with his brothers from the pit
cards.why: The plea is told **only in memory**, when the brothers' guilt surfaces.
wrong_why: There's no third dream.
Reuben wanted to save him (37:22).

cards.he:
וְעַתָּה יֵשֶׁב־נָא עַבְדְּךָ תַּחַת הַנַּעַר עֶבֶד לַאדֹנִי וְהַנַּעַר יַעַל עִם־אֶחָיו
כִּי־אֵיךְ אֶעֱלֶה אֶל־אָבִי וְהַנַּעַר אֵינֶנּוּ אִתִּי פֶּן אֶרְאֶה בָרָע אֲשֶׁר יִמְצָא אֶת־אָבִי
cards.en: Therefore, please let your servant remain as a slave to my lord instead of the boy, and let the boy go back with his brothers. For how can I go back to my father unless the boy is with me? Let me not be witness to the woe that would overtake my father!”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'atah yeishev na avd'cha tachat hana-ar eved ladoni v'hana-ar ya-al im echav
Ki eich e-eleh el avi v'hana-ar einenu iti pen er'eh vara asher yimtza et avi

cards.title: Complete teshuvah
cards.body: Long ago, **Judah** proposed selling Joseph (37:26-27). Now Joseph tests them with Benjamin, Rachel's other son, and Judah offers to **stay as a slave in his place** (44:33). **Rambam**: complete teshuvah is when you face **the same situation** again and choose differently, not out of fear or weakness.

cards.q: Why is Judah's offer a model of complete teshuvah, in Rambam's terms?
choices: He faces the same situation and chooses differently
cards.why: Same test, a brother at risk, and **this time he protects him**.
wrong_why: Rambam asks for more than words.
Gifts aren't the measure here.

points: The brothers **bow**, and don't recognize Joseph.
Joseph's plea from the pit is heard **only in their guilt** (42:21).
**Judah** offers himself for Benjamin.
Rambam: complete teshuvah is choosing differently **in the same situation**.

lessons.title: Joseph (6): I am Joseph
lessons.check_note: My summaries of Bereshit Rabbah 93:10 and Zohar, Miketz 11:182 (Soncino translation on Sefaria), read 11/11.

cards.title: He could no longer hold back
cards.body: Judah's plea breaks Joseph open. He sends everyone else out and says: "I am Joseph. Is my father still well?" (45:1-3).

cards.q: After "I am Joseph," what does Joseph ask first?
cards.why: His first question is about **his father** (45:3).

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו אֲנִי יוֹסֵף הַעוֹד אָבִי חָי וְלֹא־יָכְלוּ אֶחָיו לַעֲנוֹת אֹתוֹ כִּי נִבְהֲלוּ מִפָּנָיו
וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו גְּשׁוּ־נָא אֵלַי וַיִּגָּשׁוּ וַיֹּאמֶר אֲנִי יוֹסֵף אֲחִיכֶם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי מִצְרָיְמָה
וְעַתָּה אַל־תֵּעָצְבוּ וְאַל־יִחַר בְּעֵינֵיכֶם כִּי־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי הֵנָּה כִּי לְמִחְיָה שְׁלָחַנִי אֱלֹהִים לִפְנֵיכֶם
cards.en: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still well?” But his brothers could not answer him, so dumbfounded were they on account of him. Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come forward to me.” And when they came forward, he said, “I am your brother Joseph, he whom you sold into Egypt. Now, do not be distressed or reproach yourselves because you sold me hither; it was to save life that God sent me ahead of you.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer yoseif el echav ani yoseif ha-od avi chai v'lo yachlu echav la-anot oto ki nivhalu mipanav
Vayomer yoseif el echav g'shu na eilai vayigashu vayomer ani yoseif achichem asher m'chartem oti mitzraymah
V'atah al tei-atzvu v'al yichar b'eineichem ki m'chartem oti heinah ki l'michyah sh'lachani Elohim lifneichem

cards.title: The day of rebuke
cards.body: "His brothers could not answer him." **Abba Kohen Bardela**: woe to us on **the day of rebuke**. Joseph was the youngest, and his brothers **could not withstand his rebuke**. How much more, when **God** comes to rebuke each person **according to who they are**.

cards.q: What does Abba Kohen Bardela learn from the brothers' silence?
choices: If they couldn't face Joseph, how much harder to face God's judgment
cards.why: "I am Joseph" was rebuke enough. **The day of judgment** will be harder.
wrong_why: The midrash isn't about language.
The midrash reads the silence as shame, not mishearing.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם יוֹסֵף אַל־תִּירָאוּ כִּי הֲתַחַת אֱלֹהִים אָנִי
וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה לְמַעַן עֲשֹׂה כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה לְהַחֲיֹת עַם־רָב
cards.en: But Joseph said to them, “Have no fear! Am I a substitute for God? Besides, although you intended me harm, God intended it for good, so as to bring about the present result—the survival of many people.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer aleihem yoseif al tira-u ki hatachat Elohim ani
V'atem chashavtem alai ra-ah Elohim chashavah l'tovah l'ma-an aso kayom hazeh l'hachayot am rav

cards.he: וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה
cards.tl: V'atem chashavtem alai ra-ah Elohim chashavah l'tovah
cards.gloss: "although you intended me harm, God intended it for good" (50:20). After Jacob dies, the brothers fear revenge. Joseph answers: "Have no fear! Am I a substitute for God?"

cards.title: Not repaying evil
cards.body: The **Zohar** holds up "Joseph the righteous" as the model of one who **does not repay evil**: when his brothers fell into his hands, he told himself, "wait for the Lord, and he will save thee" (Proverbs 20:22).

cards.q: Why does the Zohar call Joseph "the righteous" here?
choices: He had his brothers in his power and did not repay evil
cards.why: Power over those who hurt him, and **he chose not to use it**.
wrong_why: The Zohar's point here is restraint, not dreams.
Power alone isn't righteousness; how he used it is.

cards.prompt: Joseph says God meant it for good, but it's Joseph who chooses to forgive. Where do you see God in that choice?

points: "**I am Joseph.** Is my father still well?"
Bereshit Rabbah 93:10: **the day of rebuke**.
"You intended me harm, **God intended it for good**."
Zohar: Joseph the righteous **did not repay evil**.

lessons.title: Joseph (7): Going down to Egypt
lessons.check_note: Megillah 29a read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: A night vision on the way
cards.body: Joseph is alive. Old Jacob sets out for Egypt, and at night God speaks to him one last time: "Jacob! Jacob!" (46:1-2).

cards.q: What does God promise Jacob about going down to Egypt?
choices: "I Myself will go down with you"
cards.why: "**I Myself will go down with you** to Egypt, and I Myself will also bring you back" (46:4).

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַרְאֹת הַלַּיְלָה וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב יַעֲקֹב וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר אָנֹכִי הָאֵל אֱלֹהֵי אָבִיךָ אַל־תִּירָא מֵרְדָה מִצְרַיְמָה כִּי־לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל אֲשִׂימְךָ שָׁם
אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ מִצְרַיְמָה וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם־עָלֹה וְיוֹסֵף יָשִׁית יָדוֹ עַל־עֵינֶיךָ
cards.en: God called to Israel in a vision by night: “Jacob! Jacob!” He answered, “Here.” “I am God, the God of your father’s [house]. Fear not to go down to Egypt, for I will make you there into a great nation. I Myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I Myself will also bring you back; and Joseph’s hand shall close your eyes.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Elohim l'yisra-eil b'mar'ot halaylah vayomer Yaakov Yaakov vayomer hineini
Vayomer anochi ha-eil Elohei avicha al tira meirdah mitzraymah ki l'goi gadol asimcha sham
Anochi eireid im'cha mitzraymah v'anochi a-alcha gam alo v'yoseif yashit yado al einecha

cards.title: The Shechinah in exile
cards.body: **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**: see how beloved Israel is: **wherever they were exiled, the Divine Presence went with them**. To Egypt, to Babylonia, and beyond. God doesn't stay home while the people suffer.

cards.q: What does Megillah 29a teach about exile?
choices: The Divine Presence goes into exile with the people
cards.why: "**I Myself will go down with you**": the Shechinah shares every exile.
wrong_why: Megillah 29a teaches the opposite.
It names Egypt, Babylonia and more.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֶל־פַּרְעֹה יְמֵי שְׁנֵי מְגוּרַי שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה מְעַט וְרָעִים הָיוּ יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיַּי וְלֹא הִשִּׂיגוּ אֶת־יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי אֲבֹתַי בִּימֵי מְגוּרֵיהֶם
cards.en: And Jacob answered Pharaoh, “The years of my sojourn [on earth] are one hundred and thirty. Few and hard have been the years of my life, nor do they come up to the life spans of my ancestors during their sojourns.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomer Yaakov el par'o y'mei sh'nei m'gurai sh'loshim um'at shanah m'at v'ra-im hayu y'mei sh'nei chayai v'lo hisigu et y'mei sh'nei chayei avotai bimei m'gureihem

cards.title: Few and hard
cards.body: Pharaoh asks Jacob his age. Jacob answers: "Few and hard have been the years of my life" (47:9). A brother who wanted him dead, a deceiving uncle, Rachel lost on the road, a son lost for more than twenty years. The Torah lets the patriarch **say it plainly**.

cards.prompt: Jacob calls his years few and hard, and still God goes down with him. Where have you felt accompanied in a hard place? It's fine to skip this one.

points: "**I Myself will go down with you.**"
Megillah 29a: **the Shechinah goes into exile** with the people.
Jacob: "**Few and hard** have been the years of my life."

lessons.title: Joseph (8): Blessings and bones
lessons.check_note: Pesachim 56a and Sotah 13a read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: The last blessings
cards.body: Before he dies, Jacob blesses **Joseph's sons**, then gathers **his own twelve** (48-49). Then Joseph, too, grows old.

cards.q: In the Talmud's story, the line "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom" first came from Jacob.
cards.why: **Pesachim 56a**: Jacob said it on his deathbed, answering his sons' Sh'ma.

cards.he: וַיְבָרְכֵם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמוֹר בְּךָ יְבָרֵךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר יְשִׂמְךָ אֱלֹהִים כְּאֶפְרַיִם וְכִמְנַשֶּׁה וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־אֶפְרַיִם לִפְנֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
cards.en: So he blessed them that day, saying, “By you shall Israel invoke blessings, saying: God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.” Thus he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayvarcheim bayom hahu leimor b'cha y'vareich Yisrael leimor y'simcha Elohim k'efrayim v'chimnasheh vayasem et efrayim lifnei m'nasheh

cards.title: Ephraim before Manasseh
cards.body: Jacob crosses his hands and puts **the younger before the older** (48:20), one more time in Genesis. His words are still how parents bless their sons on Friday night: "God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh."

cards.he:
וַיִּקְרָא יַעֲקֹב אֶל־בָּנָיו וַיֹּאמֶר הֵאָסְפוּ וְאַגִּידָה לָכֶם אֵת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָא אֶתְכֶם בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים
הִקָּבְצוּ וְשִׁמְעוּ בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב וְשִׁמְעוּ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבִיכֶם
cards.en: And Jacob called his sons and said, “Come together that I may tell you what is to befall you in days to come. Assemble and hearken, O sons of Jacob; Hearken to Israel your father:
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayikra Yaakov el banav vayomer hei-asfu v'agidah lachem eit asher yikra etchem b'acharit hayamim
Hikavtzu v'shim'u b'nei Yaakov v'shim'u el Yisrael avichem

cards.title: Sh'ma, our father Israel
cards.body: Jacob wants to reveal **the end of days**, but the Divine Presence leaves him. He fears one of his sons is unfit, as Ishmael and Esau were. His sons answer: **"Hear, Israel"** (their father's name) **"the Lord is our God, the Lord is One."** Jacob answers: **"Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever."**

cards.q: In Pesachim 56a, why do Jacob's sons say "Hear, Israel"?
choices: To reassure their father, Israel, that they all share his one God
To ask him to bless them
cards.why: As there is one God in their father's heart, so there is in theirs. Jacob answers with **Baruch shem**.
wrong_why: The setting is a deathbed, not a service.
They reassure him; he already blessed them.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹסֵף אֶל־אֶחָיו אָנֹכִי מֵת וֵאלֹהִים פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד אֶתְכֶם וְהֶעֱלָה אֶתְכֶם מִן־הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת אֶל־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב
וַיַּשְׁבַּע יוֹסֵף אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד אֱלֹהִים אֶתְכֶם וְהַעֲלִתֶם אֶת־עַצְמֹתַי מִזֶּה
cards.en: At length, Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die. God will surely take notice of you and bring you up from this land to the land promised on oath to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.” So Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “When God has taken notice of you, you shall carry up my bones from here.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer yoseif el echav anochi meit veilohim pakod yifkod etchem v'he-elah etchem min ha-aretz hazot el ha-aretz asher nishba l'avraham l'yitzchak ul'ya-akov
Vayashba yoseif et b'nei Yisrael leimor pakod yifkod Elohim etchem v'ha-alitem et atzmotai mizeh

cards.title: Carry up my bones
cards.body: Joseph makes his brothers swear: "you shall carry up my bones from here" (50:25). Generations later, while all Israel gathered **Egypt's riches** at the Exodus, **Moses** busied himself with **Joseph's coffin**. The Talmud: see how beloved mitzvot are to Moses.

cards.q: What was Moses doing, according to Sotah 13a, while the people took Egypt's riches?
cards.why: **Keeping the oath** to Joseph: a mitzvah over treasure.
wrong_why: The Talmud highlights the coffin.
Not at that moment.

cards.body: Every time you say **Sh'ma Yisrael** and the quiet **Baruch shem k'vod malchuto**, you echo Jacob's sons and Jacob's answer.

points: "**God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.**"
Pesachim 56a: Jacob's sons say **Sh'ma**, Jacob answers **Baruch shem**.
"**Carry up my bones.**"
Sotah 13a: Moses chose **the coffin over the treasure**.

units.title: Elijah
units.subtitle: The prophet who did not die

lessons.title: Elijah (1): The key to the rain
lessons.check_note: Sanhedrin 113a and Chullin 5a read on Sefaria 11/12. English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive.

cards.title: No dew, no rain
cards.body: **Elijah** appears with no introduction and makes King **Ahab** an oath: no rain until Elijah says so.

cards.q: In the Talmud, which key did God take back from Elijah in exchange for another?
choices: The key of rain, for the key of reviving the dead
The key of the Temple, for the key of heaven
The key of birth, for the key of rain
cards.why: Three keys are not handed to an agent; Elijah could hold only one at a time.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּי מִתֹּשָׁבֵי גִלְעָד אֶל־אַחְאָב חַי־יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתִּי לְפָנָיו אִם־יִֽהְיֶה הַשָּׁנִים הָאֵלֶּה טַל וּמָטָר כִּי אִם־לְפִי דְבָרִֽי׃
cards.en: Elijah the Tishbite, an inhabitant of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the ETERNAL lives, the God of Israel whom I serve, there will be no dew or rain except at my bidding.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vayomer eiliyahu hatishbi mitoshavei gil'ad el ach'av chai Adonai Elohei Yisrael asher amadti l'fanav im yihyeh hashanim ha-eileh tal umatar ki im l'fi d'vari.

cards.he: אִם־יִֽהְיֶה הַשָּׁנִים הָאֵלֶּה טַל וּמָטָר כִּי אִם־לְפִי דְבָרִֽי׃
cards.tl: Im yihyeh hashanim ha-eileh tal umatar ki im l'fi d'vari.
cards.gloss: "there will be no dew or rain except at my bidding" (17:1).

cards.title: Why Elijah swore
cards.body: The Talmud sets the scene in a house of mourning. **Ahab** mocks Elijah: Moses warned that if Israel served other gods, the heavens would close and there would be no rain. Yet Ahab has set up an idol on every furrow, and the rain is so plentiful he can hardly get out to worship them. **Immediately** Elijah swears, prays, and is given **the key to the rain**.

cards.he: וְהָעֹרְבִים מְבִאִים לוֹ לֶחֶם וּבָשָׂר בַּבֹּקֶר וְלֶחֶם וּבָשָׂר בָּעָרֶב וּמִן־הַנַּחַל יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
cards.en: The ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and every evening, and he drank from the wadi.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'ha-orvim m'vi-im lo lechem uvasar baboker v'lechem uvasar ba-arev umin hanachal yishteh.

cards.title: Ravens
cards.body: Where did the ravens get bread and meat? **Rav**: from **Ahab's own slaughterhouse**. Were they really ravens? **Ravina**: yes, actual ravens, not two men who happened to be named Oreb.

cards.q: According to Rav, where did the ravens bring Elijah's meat from?
cards.why: The king who hunted Elijah **fed him**, without knowing it.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
He meets the widow later.

cards.he:
כִּי כֹה אָמַר יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּד הַקֶּמַח לֹא תִכְלָה וְצַפַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶן לֹא תֶחְסָר עַד יוֹם תֵּת־יְיָ גֶּשֶׁם עַל־פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
וַתֵּלֶךְ וַֽתַּעֲשֶׂה כִּדְבַר אֵלִיָּהוּ וַתֹּאכַל הִֽיא־וָהוּא וּבֵיתָהּ יָמִֽים׃
כַּד הַקֶּמַח לֹא כָלָתָה וְצַפַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶן לֹא חָסֵר כִּדְבַר יְיָ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר בְּיַד אֵֽלִיָּֽהוּ׃
cards.en: For thus said the ETERNAL, the God of Israel: The jar of flour shall not give out and the jug of oil shall not fail until the day that GOD sends rain upon the ground.” She went and did as Elijah had spoken, and she and he and her household had food for a long time. The jar of flour did not give out, nor did the jug of oil fail, just as GOD had spoken through Elijah.

cards.tl:
Ki cho amar Adonai Elohei Yisrael kad hakemach lo tichlah v'tzapachat hashemen lo techsar ad yom teit Adonai geshem al p'nei ha-adamah.
Vateilech vata-aseh kidvar eiliyahu vatochal hi vahu uveitah yamim.
Kad hakemach lo chalatah v'tzapachat hashemen lo chaseir kidvar Adonai asher diber b'yad eiliyahu.

cards.title: Three keys
cards.body: The stream dries up. The Talmud says God saw the world suffering while Elijah **was not moved by it**, so God sent him to a widow in Zarephath. When her son fell ill, Elijah asked for **the key to reviving the dead**. Heaven answered: three keys are not given to an agent, birth, rain and resurrection. People will say the student holds two keys and the Master one. **Give back the rain**, and take this key. A Galilean compared Elijah to a man who **slammed his door and lost his key**.

cards.q: Why, in Sanhedrin 113a, did Elijah have to give back the key to the rain?
choices: To receive the key to reviving the widow's son
The drought had ended by itself
cards.why: Compassion for one child **unlocks the rain** for everyone.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Elijah had to give the key back for rain to fall.

cards.title: Answer me, twice
cards.body: **Rabbi Abbahu**: why say "answer me" twice? The first: answer me with **fire** from heaven. The second: answer me so the people **will not say it was sorcery**. Elijah adds, "You have turned their hearts backward": the God who turned their hearts can **turn them back**.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Abbahu, what was Elijah's second "answer me" for?
choices: That the people would not dismiss the fire as sorcery
cards.why: A miracle is not enough; **hearts** have to turn too.

cards.title: Enough
cards.body: After Carmel, Queen **Jezebel** seeks Elijah's life. The prophet who called down fire runs into the wilderness, sits under a bush, and **asks to die**.

cards.q: According to the Midrash, Elijah attends every brit milah.

There was a great and mighty wind, splitting mountains and shattering rocks by GOD’s power; but GOD was not in the wind. After the wind—an earthquake; but GOD was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake—fire; but GOD was not in the fire. And after the fire—a soft murmuring sound.

וַיְהִי ׀ כִּשְׁמֹעַ אֵלִיָּהוּ וַיָּלֶט פָּנָיו בְּאַדַּרְתּוֹ וַיֵּצֵא וַֽיַּעֲמֹד פֶּתַח הַמְּעָרָה וְהִנֵּה אֵלָיו קוֹל וַיֹּאמֶר מַה־לְּךָ פֹה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
וַיֹּאמֶר קַנֹּא קִנֵּאתִי לַיהֹוָה ׀ אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת כִּֽי־עָזְבוּ בְרִֽיתְךָ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתֶיךָ הָרָסוּ וְאֶת־נְבִיאֶיךָ הָרְגוּ בֶחָרֶב וָאִוָּתֵר אֲנִי לְבַדִּי וַיְבַקְשׁוּ אֶת־נַפְשִׁי לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃
cards.en: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his mantle about his face and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. Then a voice addressed him: “Why are you here, Elijah?” He answered, “I am moved by zeal for the ETERNAL, the God of Hosts; for the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and have put Your prophets to the sword. I alone am left, and they are out to take my life.”

cards.tl:
Vay'hi  kishmoa eiliyahu vayalet panav b'adarto vayeitzei vaya-amod petach ham'arah v'hinei eilav kol vayomer ma l'cha fo eiliyahu.
Vayomer kano kineiti laihovah  Elohei tz'va-ot ki azvu v'ritcha b'nei Yisrael et mizb'chotecha harasu v'et n'vi-echa hargu vecharev va-ivateir ani l'vadi vayvakshu et nafshi l'kachtah.

cards.title: Always zealous
cards.body: In **Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer**, Elijah's complaint is about the **covenant of circumcision**, which the northern kingdom had abandoned. God answers: "Thou art always zealous." Then: by your life, Israel will not perform this covenant **until you see it with your own eyes**. So the Sages set **a seat of honor** at every brit for Elijah, called the Messenger of the Covenant (Malachi 3:1).

cards.q: In Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer 29, why is Elijah present at every brit?
choices: He said Israel had abandoned the covenant, so he must witness them keeping it
cards.why: The accuser becomes **the witness** to Israel's faithfulness.
wrong_why: Not in the Midrash.
Not in the Midrash.

cards.title: God in the quiet
cards.body: Your rabbi reads the Torah as a people **growing up**: from a child's hero-God who fixes everything, toward God present in quieter ways. Elijah lives both stages in two chapters. On Carmel, God answers with **fire**. At Horeb, God is not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but in **a soft murmuring sound**.

src.ref: Teaching from Jamie's rabbi (oral, as Jamie retold it); I Kings 18-19

cards.prompt: God was not in the fire, but in a soft murmuring sound. Where do you hear that quiet voice?

Not in wind, earthquake or fire: **a soft murmuring sound** (19:12).
Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer 29: "**always zealous**", so Elijah witnesses every brit.
Your rabbi: from fire to **quiet**.

cards.body: Elijah does not die. Walking and talking with his student **Elisha**, he is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.

cards.q: In the Talmud, how did God react when the Sages overruled a voice from heaven?
choices: God smiled: "My children have triumphed over Me"
cards.why: Elijah reports it to Rabbi Natan in Bava Metzia 59b.

cards.gloss: "He shall reconcile parents with children and children with their parents" (3:24). The prophets' last words promise that **Elijah comes back**.

cards.title: My children have triumphed
cards.body: In a famous dispute, a heavenly voice sides with Rabbi Eliezer. **Rabbi Yehoshua** stands and says, "It is not in heaven": the Torah was given at Sinai, and now the majority decides. Years later, **Rabbi Natan** meets Elijah and asks what God did at that moment. Elijah: God **smiled** and said, "My children have triumphed over Me."

cards.q: In Bava Metzia 59b, how does God respond to being overruled?
choices: With a smile and pride in the children
cards.why: Like a parent whose children have **grown up**.
wrong_why: Elijah says God smiled.
The majority's ruling stands.

cards.title: Today, if you listen
cards.body: **Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi** meets Elijah and asks when the Messiah will come. Go ask him, says Elijah: he sits at the gate of Rome **among the sick poor**, changing his bandages one at a time so he is always ready. The Messiah tells him, "Today." When he does not come, Elijah explains: "today, if you will listen to his voice" (Psalms 95:7).

cards.q: In Sanhedrin 98a, what did the Messiah's "today" mean?
choices: Today, if you will listen to his voice
cards.why: The coming depends on **us listening**.
wrong_why: He did not come that day.
Elijah reads it as a condition, not a refusal.

cards.title: A cup and a song
cards.body: Elijah is still expected: a cup is poured for him and the door opened at the **Passover seder**, and as Shabbat ends, **Havdalah** sings of אֵלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא.

Bava Metzia 59b: God smiles, "**My children have triumphed over Me**."
Sanhedrin 98a: "**today, if you will listen**."
A cup at the seder, a song at Havdalah.

cards.title: A book without God's name
cards.body: The Book of Esther **never names God**, not once. Its heroine hides too: a Jewish orphan in the Persian king's palace who keeps her people **secret** (2:7-10).

cards.q: God's name appears in the Book of Esther.
cards.why: Not once. The Rabbis found God **hidden** in the book instead.

cards.he: וַיְהִי אֹמֵן אֶת־הֲדַסָּה הִיא אֶסְתֵּר בַּת־דֹּדוֹ כִּי אֵין לָהּ אָב וָאֵם וְהַנַּעֲרָה יְפַת־תֹּאַר וְטוֹבַת מַרְאֶה וּבְמוֹת אָבִיהָ וְאִמָּהּ לְקָחָהּ מׇרְדֳּכַי לוֹ לְבַת
cards.en: He was foster father to Hadassah—that is, Esther—his uncle’s daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The maiden was shapely and beautiful; and when her father and mother died, Mordecai adopted her as his own daughter.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vay'hi omein et hadasah hi esteir bat dodo ki ein lah av va-eim v'hana-arah y'fat to-ar v'tovat mar'eh uv'mot aviha v'imah l'kachah mordochai lo l'vat

cards.he: לֹא־הִגִּידָה אֶסְתֵּר אֶת־עַמָּהּ וְאֶת־מוֹלַדְתָּהּ כִּי מׇרְדֳּכַי צִוָּה עָלֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר לֹא־תַגִּיד
cards.en: Esther did not reveal her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had told her not to reveal it.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Lo higidah esteir et amah v'et moladtah ki mordochai tzivah aleha asher lo tagid

cards.title: Why "Esther"?
cards.body: Her Hebrew name was **Hadassah**. Why call her Esther? **Rabbi Yehuda**: because she **concealed** (masteret) the truth about herself, as the verse says, she did not reveal her people.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Yehuda, why was Hadassah called Esther?
choices: Because she concealed who she was
cards.why: **Esther** sounds like **masteret**, concealing: she hid her people (2:10).
wrong_why: That's another opinion in the same passage, not Rabbi Yehuda's.
The Talmud doesn't say so.

cards.title: Hidden in the Torah
cards.body: The Talmud asks: where is Esther hinted at in the Torah? In God's warning, "**I will hide My face**" (Deuteronomy 31:18). In Hebrew, **haster astir**: "Esther" is hidden inside "I will hide."

cards.q: How does Chullin 139b find Esther in the Torah?
choices: In the words "I will hide My face" (haster astir)
It says she isn't hinted at
cards.why: **Haster astir**: God's hidden face, and Esther's name.
wrong_why: She has no genealogy in the Torah.
The Talmud finds a hint.

cards.prompt: Esther hides who she is, and God is hidden in her book. When have you had to hide part of yourself, and what did it cost?

points: Esther **never names God**.
Hadassah, called **Esther** because she **concealed** (Megillah 13a).
"**I will hide My face**": haster astir (Chullin 139b).

lessons.title: Esther (2): Mordecai would not bow
lessons.check_note: Megillah 13b read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: One man standing
cards.body: Every courtier at the palace gate **bows to Haman**, by royal order. **Mordecai** does not (3:2). Haman's fury turns into a plan to destroy all the Jews.

cards.q: Why was Haman glad when the lot fell on the month of Adar, according to the Talmud?
choices: Moses died in Adar, so it seemed an unlucky month for the Jews
cards.why: He knew Moses died in Adar. He didn't know Moses was also **born** in Adar.

cards.he: וְכׇל־עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בְּשַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ כֹּרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים לְהָמָן כִּי־כֵן צִוָּה־לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ וּמׇרְדֳּכַי לֹא יִכְרַע וְלֹא יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה
cards.en: All the king’s courtiers in the palace gate knelt and bowed low to Haman, for such was the king’s order concerning him; but Mordecai would not kneel or bow low.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'chol avdei hamelech asher b'sha-ar hamelech kor'im umishtachavim l'haman ki chein tzivah lo hamelech umordochai lo yichra v'lo yishtachaveh

cards.he: וּמׇרְדֳּכַי לֹא יִכְרַע וְלֹא יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה
cards.tl: Umordochai lo yichra v'lo yishtachaveh
cards.gloss: "but Mordecai would not kneel or bow low" (3:2). One man refuses, and the whole story turns on it.

cards.title: The lot in Adar
cards.body: Haman casts **pur**, a lot, for the date (3:7). It falls on **Adar**, and he rejoices: Moses died in Adar, a month of calamity for the Jews. **But he did not know** that Moses was also **born** in Adar.

cards.q: What did Haman not know about Adar, according to Megillah 13b?
choices: Moses was also born in Adar
Adar has two months in some years
The king was born in Adar
cards.why: A month of loss is also a month of birth: the turn is already hidden in the date.
wrong_why: That's true of the calendar, but not the Talmud's point.
The Talmud speaks of Moses.

cards.prompt: Mordecai would not bow, and Haman saw only the death in Adar, not the birth. Where might a hard date or season hold something you can't see yet?

points: Everyone bows; **Mordecai will not**.
Pur, the lot, falls on **Adar**.
Megillah 13b: Moses **died and was born** in Adar.

lessons.title: Esther (3): For just such a crisis
lessons.check_note: Esther 5:4 initials checked by script on the Masorah text. Makom as a name of God: Bereshit Rabbah 68:9 (read 11/09, see the Jacob's ladder lesson).

cards.title: Who knows?
cards.body: Esther hesitates: going to the king unbidden can mean death. Mordecai answers with the book's most famous words (4:13-14).

cards.q: What does Mordecai say might be the reason Esther became queen?
cards.why: "**Perhaps you have attained to royal position for just such a crisis**" (4:14).

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר מׇרְדֳּכַי לְהָשִׁיב אֶל־אֶסְתֵּר אַל־תְּדַמִּי בְנַפְשֵׁךְ לְהִמָּלֵט בֵּית־הַמֶּלֶךְ מִכׇּל־הַיְּהוּדִים
כִּי אִם־הַחֲרֵשׁ תַּחֲרִישִׁי בָּעֵת הַזֹּאת רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה יַעֲמוֹד לַיְּהוּדִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וְאַתְּ וּבֵית־אָבִיךְ תֹּאבֵדוּ וּמִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם־לְעֵת כָּזֹאת הִגַּעַתְּ לַמַּלְכוּת
cards.en: Mordecai had this message delivered to Esther: “Do not imagine that you, of all the Jews, will escape with your life by being in the king’s palace. On the contrary, if you keep silent in this crisis, relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another quarter, while you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows, perhaps you have attained to royal position for just such a crisis.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vayomer mordochai l'hashiv el esteir al t'dami v'nafsheich l'himaleit beit hamelech mikol hay'hudim
Ki im hachareish tacharishi ba-eit hazot revach v'hatzalah ya-amod lay'hudim mimakom acheir v'at uveit avich toveidu umi yodeia im l'eit kazot higa-at lamalchut

cards.he: מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר
cards.tl: Mimakom acheir
cards.gloss: "from another quarter" (4:14). In Hebrew, **mimakom acher**, from another **place**. **Makom**, place, is also a name the Rabbis gave to God: God is the place of the world. In a book that never names God, Mordecai speaks of help from "another place."

cards.he: לֵךְ כְּנוֹס אֶת־כׇּל־הַיְּהוּדִים הַנִּמְצְאִים בְּשׁוּשָׁן וְצוּמוּ עָלַי וְאַל־תֹּאכְלוּ וְאַל־תִּשְׁתּוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים לַיְלָה וָיוֹם גַּם־אֲנִי וְנַעֲרֹתַי אָצוּם כֵּן וּבְכֵן אָבוֹא אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר לֹא־כַדָּת וְכַאֲשֶׁר אָבַדְתִּי אָבָדְתִּי
cards.en: “Go, assemble all the Jews who live in Shushan, and fast in my behalf; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maids will observe the same fast. Then I shall go to the king, though it is contrary to the law; and if I am to perish, I shall perish!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Leich k'nos et kol hay'hudim hanimtz'im b'shushan v'tzumu alai v'al tochlu v'al tishtu sh'loshet yamim laylah vayom gam ani v'na-arotai atzum kein uv'chein avo el hamelech asher lo chadat v'cha-asher avadti avadti

cards.title: If I perish, I perish
cards.body: Esther asks all the Jews of Shushan to **fast for her three days**, and she and her maids will fast too. Then: "I shall go to the king, though it is contrary to the law; and if I am to perish, I shall perish!" (4:16). The orphan who hid becomes **the one who acts**.

cards.q: What changes in Esther in 4:16?
choices: She chooses to risk her life and act
She reveals that she is Persian
cards.why: From hiding to acting: "**If I am to perish, I shall perish.**"
wrong_why: She is Jewish, and soon reveals it.
She goes toward the king, not away.

cards.he: יָבוֹא הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן הַיּוֹם
cards.tl: Yavo hamelech v'haman hayom
cards.gloss: "let Your Majesty and Haman come today" (5:4). Esther's invitation, and the **first letters** of these four Hebrew words: yod, heh, vav, heh, **the four-letter Name**. God is present at the very moment Esther acts.

cards.q: Where is God's Name hidden in Esther 5:4?
choices: In the first letters of four words of Esther's invitation
cards.why: Yod, heh, vav, heh: hidden **in the words of Esther's own brave act**.
wrong_why: Not in Ahasuerus's name.
This verse is Esther speaking.

cards.prompt: God's Name appears, hidden, in the words Esther speaks when she finally acts. Is there a moment you are being asked to act "for just such a crisis"?

points: "**Who knows**, perhaps you have attained to royal position for just such a crisis."
**Mimakom acher**: help from "another place", and Makom is a name for God.
"**If I am to perish, I shall perish.**"
The Name hidden in **Esther's invitation** (5:4).

lessons.title: Esther (4): Turned upside down
lessons.check_note: Tikkunei Zohar 57b read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: The day it flipped
cards.body: On the very day the Jews' enemies expected to destroy them, "**the opposite happened**" (9:1). Grief becomes celebration, and Purim is born.

cards.q: Besides feasting, what does Esther 9:22 tell people to do on Purim?
choices: Send gifts to one another and presents to the poor
cards.why: "Sending gifts to one another and **presents to the poor**" (9:22).

cards.he: וּבִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הוּא־חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בּוֹ אֲשֶׁר הִגִּיעַ דְּבַר־הַמֶּלֶךְ וְדָתוֹ לְהֵעָשׂוֹת בַּיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר שִׂבְּרוּ אֹיְבֵי הַיְּהוּדִים לִשְׁלוֹט בָּהֶם וְנַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלְטוּ הַיְּהוּדִים הֵמָּה בְּשֹׂנְאֵיהֶם
cards.en: And so, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month—that is, the month of Adar—when the king’s command and decree were to be executed, the very day on which the enemies of the Jews had expected to get them in their power, the opposite happened, and the Jews got their enemies in their power.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Uvishneim asar chodesh hu chodesh adar bishloshah asar yom bo asher higia d'var hamelech v'dato l'hei-asot bayom asher sib'ru oyvei hay'hudim lishlot bahem v'nahafoch hu asher yishl'tu hay'hudim heimah b'son'eihem

cards.he: וְנַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא
cards.tl: V'nahafoch hu
cards.gloss: "the opposite happened" (9:1). In Hebrew, **v'nahafoch hu**, from the verb for turning over. Purim celebrations still quote it.

cards.he: כַּיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר־נָחוּ בָהֶם הַיְּהוּדִים מֵאֹיְבֵיהֶם וְהַחֹדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר נֶהְפַּךְ לָהֶם מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה וּמֵאֵבֶל לְיוֹם טוֹב לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹתָם יְמֵי מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה וּמִשְׁלֹחַ מָנוֹת אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיֹנִים
cards.en: the same days on which the Jews enjoyed relief from their foes and the same month that had been transformed for them from one of grief and mourning to one of festive joy. They were to observe them as days of feasting and merrymaking, and as an occasion for sending gifts to one another and presents to the poor.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Kayamim asher nachu vahem hay'hudim mei-oyveihem v'hachodesh asher nehpach lahem miyagon l'simchah umei-eivel l'yom tov la-asot otam y'mei mishteh v'simchah umishloach manot ish l'rei-eihu umatanot la-evyonim

cards.title: Joy that includes the poor
cards.body: The holiday is fixed as "days of feasting and merrymaking," with gifts to one another **and presents to the poor** (9:22). Purim's joy isn't complete until it reaches **those who have least**.

cards.title: A day like Purim
cards.body: The mystical **Tikkunei Zohar** hears **Purim** inside the name of the Day of Atonement, **Yom haKiPURIM**: the holiest fast and the most joyful feast are linked, and the day is destined to **change affliction into delight**.

cards.q: How does the Tikkunei Zohar connect Purim and Yom Kippur?
choices: It hears Purim in the name Yom haKippurim
cards.why: **Yom haKiPURIM**: the fast and the feast share a name, and both turn affliction into delight.
wrong_why: Purim is a feast, not a fast.
Yom Kippur is in Tishrei.

cards.prompt: In Ruth and Esther, God's hand is hidden and people act: Ruth's loyalty, Boaz's generosity, Esther's courage. Where is something in your life waiting to be turned around?

points: **V'nahafoch hu**: the day turned upside down.
Purim joy includes **presents to the poor**.
Tikkunei Zohar: Purim is heard in **Yom haKippurim**.

units.title: Exodus
units.subtitle: Moses, from the river to Mount Nebo

lessons.title: Moses (1): Drawn from the water
lessons.check_note: Sotah 11b and 12b read on Sefaria 11/11 (William Davidson). English: Contemporary Torah.

cards.title: Five women and a baby
cards.body: A new Pharaoh orders the **Hebrew midwives** to kill every newborn boy. Before Moses ever speaks a word, his life is saved again and again, **every time by a woman**.

cards.q: The Torah gives the names of the midwives who defied Pharaoh.
cards.why: **Shiphrah** and **Puah** (1:15). Pharaoh himself is never named.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם לַמְיַלְּדֹת הָעִבְרִיֹּת אֲשֶׁר שֵׁם הָאַחַת שִׁפְרָה וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית פּוּעָה
וַיֹּאמֶר בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן אֶת־הָעִבְרִיּוֹת וּרְאִיתֶן עַל־הָאׇבְנָיִם אִם־בֵּן הוּא וַהֲמִתֶּן אֹתוֹ וְאִם־בַּת הִוא וָחָיָה
וַתִּירֶאןָ הַמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא עָשׂוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶן מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם וַתְּחַיֶּיןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִים
cards.en: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah, saying, “When you deliver the Hebrew women, look at the birthstool: if it is a boy, kill him; if it is a girl, let her live.” The midwives, fearing God, did not do as the king of Egypt had told them; they let the boys live.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer melech mitzrayim lamyal'dot ha-ivriyot asher sheim ha-achat shifrah v'sheim hasheinit pu-ah
Vayomer b'yaledchen et ha-ivriyot ur'iten al ha-ovnayim im bein hu vahamiten oto v'im bat hi vachayah
Vatirena hamyal'dot et ha-Elohim v'lo asu ka-asher diber aleihen melech Mitzrayim vat'chayena et hayladim

cards.he: וַתִּירֶאןָ הַמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים
cards.tl: Vatirena hamyal'dot et ha-Elohim
cards.gloss: "The midwives, fearing God" (1:17). Here, fearing God means **refusing a king's order to kill**.

cards.title: Who were the midwives?
cards.body: In one view in the Talmud, **Shiphrah** was **Jochebed**, Moses' mother, and **Puah** was **Miriam**, his sister. Puah made soothing sounds to the newborns, and Miriam, speaking with divine inspiration, foresaw that her mother would bear a son **who would save the Jewish people**. (Another view: Jochebed and Elisheba, Aaron's wife.)

cards.q: In one view in Sotah 11b, who were Shiphrah and Puah?
choices: Jochebed and Miriam, Moses' mother and sister
cards.why: Moses' own **mother and sister** were already saving lives before he was born.
wrong_why: The Talmud identifies them as Israelite women.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.he:
וַיֵּלֶךְ אִישׁ מִבֵּית לֵוִי וַיִּקַּח אֶת־בַּת־לֵוִי
וַתַּהַר הָאִשָּׁה וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתֵּרֶא אֹתוֹ כִּי־טוֹב הוּא וַתִּצְפְּנֵהוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה יְרָחִים
וְלֹא־יָכְלָה עוֹד הַצְּפִינוֹ וַתִּקַּח־לוֹ תֵּבַת גֹּמֶא וַתַּחְמְרָהֿ בַחֵמָר וּבַזָּפֶת וַתָּשֶׂם בָּהּ אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד וַתָּשֶׂם בַּסּוּף עַל־שְׂפַת הַיְאֹר
cards.en: A certain member of the house of Levi went and took [into his household as his wife] a woman of Levi. The woman conceived and bore a son; and when she saw how beautiful he was, she hid him for three months. When she could hide him no longer, she got a wicker basket for him and caulked it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child into it and placed it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayeilech ish mibeit leivi vayikach et bat leivi
Vatahar ha-ishah vateiled bein vateire oto ki tov hu vatitzp'neihu sh'loshah y'rachim
V'lo yachlah od hatz'fino vatikach lo teivat gome vatachm'rah vacheimar uvazafet vatasem bah et hayeled vatasem basuf al s'fat hay'or

cards.he:
וַתֵּרֶד בַּת־פַּרְעֹה לִרְחֹץ עַל־הַיְאֹר וְנַעֲרֹתֶיהָ הֹלְכֹת עַל־יַד הַיְאֹר וַתֵּרֶא אֶת־הַתֵּבָה בְּתוֹךְ הַסּוּף וַתִּשְׁלַח אֶת־אֲמָתָהּ וַתִּקָּחֶהָ
וַתִּפְתַּח וַתִּרְאֵהוּ אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד וְהִנֵּה־נַעַר בֹּכֶה וַתַּחְמֹל עָלָיו וַתֹּאמֶר מִיַּלְדֵי הָעִבְרִים זֶה
cards.en: The daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe in the Nile, while her maidens walked along the Nile. She spied the basket among the reeds and sent her slave girl to fetch it. When she opened it, she saw that it was a child, a boy crying. She took pity on it and said, “This must be a Hebrew child.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vateired bat par'o lirchotz al hay'or v'na-aroteha holchot al yad hay'or vateire et hateivah b'toch hasuf vatishlach et amatah vatikacheha
Vatiftach vatir'eihu et hayeled v'hinei na-ar bocheh vatachmol alav vatomer miyaldei ha-ivrim zeh

cards.he: וַתַּחְמֹל עָלָיו
cards.tl: Vatachmol alav
cards.gloss: "She took pity on it" (2:6). Pharaoh's own daughter hears a Hebrew baby crying and chooses **compassion over her father's decree**.

cards.title: Why did she go down to the river?
cards.body: Rabbi Yochanan, in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: she went down to cleanse herself **from her father's idols**. Her bathing was an **immersion**, the first step of joining the people. Her maidens protested that a king's own household should obey his decree. She saved the child anyway.

cards.q: According to Sotah 12b, why did Pharaoh's daughter go down to the river?
choices: To cleanse herself of her father's idols
cards.why: Her bath becomes an **immersion**: she was already turning from her father's world.
wrong_why: She found the basket by chance; the Talmud reads her purpose differently.
The Talmud says the opposite: she left idolatry.

cards.he: וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד וַתְּבִאֵהוּ לְבַת־פַּרְעֹה וַיְהִי־לָהּ לְבֵן וַתִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ מֹשֶׁה וַתֹּאמֶר כִּי מִן־הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ
cards.en: When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, who made him her son. She named him Moses, explaining, “I drew him out of the water.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayigdal hayeled vat'vi-eihu l'vat par'o vay'hi lah l'vein vatikra sh'mo Moshe vatomer ki min hamayim m'shitihu

cards.he: כִּי מִן־הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ
cards.tl: Ki min hamayim m'shitihu
cards.gloss: "I drew him out of the water" (2:10). The name **Moses** comes from an Egyptian princess.

cards.prompt: Two midwives, a mother, a sister, and Pharaoh's daughter: women save Moses before he can do anything. Who quietly made your own story possible?

points: The midwives **feared God** and let the boys live.
Sotah 11b: Shiphrah and Puah were **Jochebed and Miriam**.
Sotah 12b: Pharaoh's daughter was leaving **her father's idols**.
"**I drew him out of the water**": Moses.

lessons.title: Moses (2): The bush that was not consumed
lessons.check_note: Shemot Rabbah 2:2, 2:5 (Sefaria Midrash Rabbah 2022) and Berakhot 9b read 11/11.

cards.title: A shepherd in the wilderness
cards.body: Moses has fled Egypt. Now he tends his father-in-law's sheep in Midian, far from his people, until something on the mountain **burns and does not burn up**.

cards.q: Why did God speak from a lowly thorn bush, according to one answer in the Midrash?
choices: No place is empty of God's presence, even a bush
cards.why: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha: **no place is empty of the Divine Presence**, even a bush.

cards.title: Tested with a flock
cards.body: The Midrash says God tested Moses **with sheep**. A young goat ran off, and Moses followed it until it stopped at a pool to drink. God said: you show such compassion to a flock that belongs to a human being, **you will shepherd My flock, Israel**.

cards.he:
וּמֹשֶׁה הָיָה רֹעֶה אֶת־צֹאן יִתְרוֹ חֹתְנוֹ כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן וַיִּנְהַג אֶת־הַצֹּאן אַחַר הַמִּדְבָּר וַיָּבֹא אֶל־הַר הָאֱלֹהִים חֹרֵבָה
וַיֵּרָא מַלְאַךְ יְיָ אֵלָיו בְּלַבַּת־אֵשׁ מִתּוֹךְ הַסְּנֶה וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה הַסְּנֶה בֹּעֵר בָּאֵשׁ וְהַסְּנֶה אֵינֶנּוּ אֻכָּל
וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אָסֻרָה־נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶה הַגָּדֹל הַזֶּה מַדּוּעַ לֹא־יִבְעַר הַסְּנֶה
וַיַּרְא יְיָ כִּי סָר לִרְאוֹת וַיִּקְרָא אֵלָיו אֱלֹהִים מִתּוֹךְ הַסְּנֶה וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּנִי
וַיֹּאמֶר אַל־תִּקְרַב הֲלֹם שַׁל־נְעָלֶיךָ מֵעַל רַגְלֶיךָ כִּי הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו אַדְמַת־קֹדֶשׁ הוּא
cards.en: Now Moses, tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, drove the flock into the wilderness, and came to Horeb, the mountain of God. A messenger of יהוה appeared to him in a blazing fire out of a bush. He gazed, and there was a bush all aflame, yet the bush was not consumed. Moses said, “I must turn aside to look at this marvelous sight; why doesn’t the bush burn up?” When יהוה saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him out of the bush: “Moses! Moses!” He answered, “Here I am.” And [God] said, “Do not come closer! Remove your sandals from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground!”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Umosheh hayah ro-eh et tzon yitro chotno kohein midyan vayinhag et hatzon achar hamidbar vayavo el har ha-Elohim choreivah
Vayeira mal'ach Adonai eilav b'labat eish mitoch has'neh vayar v'hinei has'neh bo-eir ba-eish v'has'neh einenu ukol
Vayomer Moshe asurah na v'er'eh et hamar'eh hagadol hazeh madua lo yiv'ar has'neh
Vayar Adonai ki sar lir'ot vayikra eilav Elohim mitoch has'neh vayomer Moshe Moshe vayomer hineini
Vayomer al tikrav halom shal n'alecha mei-al raglecha ki hamakom asher atah omeid alav admat kodesh hu

cards.he: וְהַסְּנֶה אֵינֶנּוּ אֻכָּל
cards.tl: V'has'neh einenu ukol
cards.gloss: "yet the bush was not consumed" (3:2).

cards.title: Why a thorn bush?
cards.body: The Midrash gives many answers. **Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha**: "there is no place that is vacant of the Divine Presence, even a bush." **Rabbi Eliezer**: the bush is the lowliest of trees, as Israel was lowly in Egypt. And God speaks from the thorns to say, "I am party to their suffering."

cards.q: Which is one answer the Midrash gives for why God spoke from a thorn bush?
choices: God shares Israel's suffering, speaking from among the thorns
Thorn bushes were sacred in Egypt
Moses was afraid of tall trees
cards.why: From the thorns, God says: "**I am party to their suffering.**"
wrong_why: The Midrash doesn't say so.
The Midrash doesn't say so.

cards.he: אָסֻרָה־נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה
cards.tl: Asurah na v'er'eh
cards.gloss: "I must turn aside to look" (3:3). Only **when God saw that he had turned aside** does God call his name (3:4).

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִים הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָא אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתִּי לָהֶם אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם שְׁלָחַנִי אֲלֵיכֶם וְאָמְרוּ־לִי מַה־שְּׁמוֹ מָה אֹמַר אֲלֵהֶם
וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל־מֹשֶׁה אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה וַיֹּאמֶר כֹּה תֹאמַר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶהְיֶה שְׁלָחַנִי אֲלֵיכֶם
cards.en: Moses said to God, “When I come to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers’ [house] has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is [God’s] name?’ what shall I say to them?” And God said to Moses, “Ehyeh-Asher-Ehyeh,” continuing, “Thus shall you say to the Israelites, ‘Ehyeh sent me to you.’”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Moshe el ha-Elohim hinei anochi va el b'nei Yisrael v'amarti lahem Elohei avoteichem sh'lachani aleichem v'amru li ma sh'mo mah omar aleihem
Vayomer Elohim el Moshe ehyeh asher ehyeh vayomer ko tomar livnei Yisrael ehyeh sh'lachani aleichem

cards.he: אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה
cards.tl: Ehyeh asher ehyeh
cards.gloss: God's answer when Moses asks for a name (3:14). The Contemporary Torah leaves it in Hebrew; the Talmud's English renders it "I will be that I will be."

cards.title: I will be with them
cards.body: Why the doubled **ehyeh**? God told Moses: tell Israel I was with you in this enslavement, and **I will be with you** in enslavements to come. Moses answered: it is **enough for them to endure** what they suffer now. God agreed: tell them only, "I will be has sent me."

cards.q: In Berakhot 9b, why does Moses ask God to shorten the message?
choices: Their present suffering is already enough to bear
The full name was too holy to say
cards.why: Moses protects the people: **today's suffering is enough** without news of future exile.
wrong_why: The Talmud's reason is the people's burden.
The Talmud's reason is the people's burden.

cards.prompt: The Midrash says no place is empty of God, even a thorn bush, and Moses sees it only because he turns aside. What might you see if you turned aside today?

points: Moses was chosen for **compassion to a flock** (Shemot Rabbah 2:2).
The bush **burned and was not consumed**.
No place is empty of God, **even a bush** (Shemot Rabbah 2:5).
**Ehyeh**: I will be with them (Berakhot 9b).

lessons.title: Moses (3): A hardened heart
lessons.check_note: Mishneh Torah, Repentance 6:3 (Touger) read 11/11.

cards.title: Refused, again and again
cards.body: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let the people go. Plague after plague falls, and Pharaoh refuses each time. But the Torah describes his refusal **in more than one way**.

cards.q: In the Torah, only God ever hardens Pharaoh's heart.
cards.why: In the early plagues **Pharaoh hardens his own heart** (8:11). Only later does the Torah say God did it.

cards.he: וַאֲנִי אַקְשֶׁה אֶת־לֵב פַּרְעֹה וְהִרְבֵּיתִי אֶת־אֹתֹתַי וְאֶת־מוֹפְתַי בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם
cards.en: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, that I may multiply My signs and marvels in the land of Egypt.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Va-ani aksheh et leiv par'o v'hirbeiti et ototai v'et moftai b'eretz Mitzrayim

cards.he: וַיַּרְא פַּרְעֹה כִּי הָיְתָה הָרְוָחָה וְהַכְבֵּד אֶת־לִבּוֹ וְלֹא שָׁמַע אֲלֵהֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְיָ
cards.en: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he became stubborn and would not heed them, as יהוה had spoken.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayar par'o ki haytah harvachah v'hachbeid et libo v'lo shama aleihem ka-asher diber Adonai

cards.he: וְהַכְבֵּד אֶת־לִבּוֹ
cards.tl: V'hachbeid et libo
cards.gloss: "he became stubborn" (8:11). In Hebrew, Pharaoh does this to **his own heart**: the relief comes, and he chooses not to listen.

cards.q: Who hardens Pharaoh's heart in 8:11?
cards.why: When the relief came, **Pharaoh** made his own heart heavy.
wrong_why: Not yet. That comes later (9:12).
Moses only asks.

cards.he: וַיְחַזֵּק יְיָ אֶת־לֵב פַּרְעֹה וְלֹא שָׁמַע אֲלֵהֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְיָ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה
cards.en: But יהוה stiffened the heart of Pharaoh, and he would not heed them, just as יהוה had told Moses.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vaychazeik Adonai et leiv par'o v'lo shama aleihem ka-asher diber Adonai el Moshe

cards.title: Why would God harden a heart?
cards.body: **Maimonides** answers: Pharaoh "began to sin on his own initiative," oppressing Israel in his land. Someone who sins **willfully and greatly** can reach a point where **the way back is held closed**. So God hardened his heart, and he could no longer repent.

cards.q: According to Maimonides, why did God harden Pharaoh's heart?
choices: Pharaoh first chose evil freely, until the way back closed
God planned for him to fail from the start
cards.why: Pharaoh's own choices came **first**; the hardening was their consequence.
wrong_why: Maimonides stresses that Pharaoh began on his own.
Not in the text.

cards.prompt: Pharaoh hardens his own heart before anything is done to it. Is there a refusal in your life that has gotten harder to undo the longer it has gone on?

points: God foretells: **I will harden Pharaoh's heart** (7:3).
At first **Pharaoh hardens his own heart** (8:11).
Later **God stiffens it** (9:12).
Maimonides: willful sin can **close the way back**.

lessons.title: Moses (4): At the Sea
lessons.check_note: Sotah 37a and Megillah 10b read 11/11. Friedman: see Genesis (1).

cards.title: Trapped
cards.body: The Israelites are free, and then trapped: Pharaoh's chariots behind them, **the sea in front**. They cry out to God, and Moses prays.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Yehuda in the Talmud, who went into the sea first?
cards.why: Every tribe hung back, until **Nahshon ben Amminadab** jumped in.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה מַה־תִּצְעַק אֵלָי דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסָּעוּ
וְאַתָּה הָרֵם אֶת־מַטְּךָ וּנְטֵה אֶת־יָדְךָ עַל־הַיָּם וּבְקָעֵהוּ וְיָבֹאוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה
cards.en: Then יהוה said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward. And you lift up your rod and hold out your arm over the sea and split it, so that the Israelites may march into the sea on dry ground.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Adonai el Moshe ma titz'ak eilai dabeir el b'nei Yisrael v'yisa-u
V'atah hareim et mat'cha un'tei et yadcha al hayam uv'ka-eihu v'yavo-u v'nei Yisrael b'toch hayam bayabashah

cards.he: מַה־תִּצְעַק אֵלָי
cards.tl: Ma titz'ak eilai
cards.gloss: "Why do you cry out to Me?" (14:15). God's answer to prayer is: "Tell the Israelites to go forward."

cards.title: Nahshon
cards.body: **Rabbi Yehuda**: no tribe wanted to go into the sea first. Then **Nahshon ben Amminadab**, prince of Judah, jumped in, his tribe after him. Meanwhile Moses kept praying at length, and God told him that **His beloved ones were drowning** while he prolonged his prayer: speak to the people, and lift your rod.

cards.q: In Sotah 37a, why does God interrupt Moses' long prayer?
choices: The people were already in the water and needed action
Moses was praying in the wrong place
Prayer was forbidden at the Sea
cards.why: Nahshon was already **drowning**; it was time to **lift the rod**, not lengthen the prayer.
wrong_why: The Talmud's point is urgency.
The Talmud's point is urgency.

cards.he:
וַיֵּט מֹשֶׁה אֶת־יָדוֹ עַל־הַיָּם וַיּוֹלֶךְ יְיָ  אֶת־הַיָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כׇּל־הַלַּיְלָה וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם
וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חוֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם
cards.en: Then Moses held out his arm over the sea and יהוה drove back the sea with a strong east wind all that night, and turned the sea into dry ground. The waters were split, and the Israelites went into the sea on dry ground, the waters forming a wall for them on their right and on their left.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayeit Moshe et yado al hayam vayolech Adonai  et hayam b'ruach kadim azah kol halaylah vayasem et hayam lecharavah vayibak'u hamayim
Vayavo-u v'nei Yisrael b'toch hayam bayabashah v'hamayim lahem chomah miminam umis'molam

cards.he: מִי־כָמֹכָה בָּאֵלִם יְיָ        מִי כָּמֹכָה נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ        נוֹרָא תְהִלֹּת עֹשֵׂה פֶלֶא
cards.en: Who is like You, יהוה, among the celestials; Who is like You, majestic in holiness, Awesome in splendor, working wonders!
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Mi chamochah ba-eilim Adonai        mi kamochah nedar bakodesh        nora t'hilot osei fele

cards.body: Every evening and every morning, after the Sh'ma and its blessings, we sing **Mi Chamocha**: these words from the shore of the Sea.

cards.he:
וַתִּקַּח מִרְיָם הַנְּבִיאָה אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן אֶת־הַתֹּף בְּיָדָהּ וַתֵּצֶאןָ כׇל־הַנָּשִׁים אַחֲרֶיהָ בְּתֻפִּים וּבִמְחֹלֹת
וַתַּעַן לָהֶם מִרְיָם שִׁירוּ לַיהֹוָה כִּי־גָאֹה גָּאָה סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם
cards.en: Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron’s sister, picked up a hand-drum, and all the women went out after her in dance with hand-drums. And Miriam chanted for them: Sing to יהוה, for He has triumphed gloriously; Horse and driver He has hurled into the sea.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vatikach Miriam han'vi-ah achot aharon et hatof b'yadah vateitzena chol hanashim achareha b'tupim uvimcholot
Vata-an lahem Miriam shiru laihovah ki ga-o ga-ah sus v'rochvo ramah vayam

cards.title: When not to sing
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan**: that night, the angels wanted to sing. God stopped them: the Egyptians, **the work of My hands**, are drowning, and you would sing? The Talmud concludes that God **does not rejoice** over the downfall of the wicked.

cards.q: In Megillah 10b, why did God stop the angels from singing?
choices: The Egyptians, God's creatures too, were drowning
Only Miriam was allowed to sing
cards.why: **The work of My hands** were drowning: even a rescue is not a reason to rejoice in anyone's death.
wrong_why: Not the Talmud's reason.
Not the Talmud's reason.

cards.title: God, openly
cards.body: At the Sea, God acts **openly**, for everyone to see. Biblical scholar **Richard Elliott Friedman** traces how this visible presence **fades** across the Bible, until in Esther God is never named. From here on, the people will have to do more of the acting themselves.

src.ref: Richard Elliott Friedman, The Hidden Face of God (1995)

cards.prompt: Nahshon steps in before the sea splits; Miriam sings after it closes, and God remembers the drowned. Which is harder for you: stepping in before you're sure, or celebrating without forgetting the cost?

points: "**Why do you cry out to Me?**" God says: go forward.
**Nahshon** went in first (Sotah 37a).
**Mi Chamocha** comes from the Sea (15:11).
God **does not rejoice** at the drowning (Megillah 10b).

lessons.title: Moses (5): At the foot of the mountain
lessons.check_note: Shabbat 88a and Shemot Rabbah 29:9 read 11/11.

cards.title: Sinai
cards.body: Three months out of Egypt, the people camp at the mountain. Thunder, lightning, a cloud, and **the blast of a shofar**. Moses leads them out to meet God.

cards.q: According to the Talmud, Israel promised to do the commandments before promising to hear them.
cards.why: They said "**We will do**" before "**We will hear**," and the Talmud calls it the angels' secret.

cards.he: וַיּוֹצֵא מֹשֶׁה אֶת־הָעָם לִקְרַאת הָאֱלֹהִים מִן־הַמַּחֲנֶה וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ בְּתַחְתִּית הָהָר
cards.en: Moses led the people out of the camp toward God, and they took their places at the foot of the mountain.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayotzei Moshe et ha-am likrat ha-Elohim min hamachaneh vayityatz'vu b'tachtit hahar

cards.he: וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ בְּתַחְתִּית הָהָר
cards.tl: Vayityatz'vu b'tachtit hahar
cards.gloss: "they took their places at the foot of the mountain" (19:17). The Hebrew can also be read as **under** the mountain, and the Talmud reads it that way.

cards.title: A mountain held overhead
cards.body: **Rabbi Avdimi**: God held the mountain over them **like a tub**: accept the Torah, or this will be your burial. But a covenant accepted under force is weak. **Rava** answers: they **accepted it again, willingly**, in the days of Ahasuerus, as Esther says, "The Jews ordained, and took upon them" (Esther 9:27).

cards.q: According to Rava in Shabbat 88a, when did Israel accept the Torah freely?
choices: In the days of Ahasuerus, in the Purim story
At the moment of the Ten Commandments
cards.why: At Sinai, under the mountain; in **Esther's** time, by choice. A people grown up enough to choose.
wrong_why: The Talmud reads Sinai as under compulsion.
Not in this passage.

cards.he: אָנֹכִי יְיָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִ͏ים
cards.en: I יהוה am your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, the house of bondage:
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Anochi Adonai Elohecha asher hotzeiticha mei-eretz mitzrayim mibeit avadim

cards.title: Silence
cards.body: **Rabbi Abbahu** in the name of **Rabbi Yochanan**: when God gave the Torah, no bird sang, no ox lowed, the sea did not stir, the angels did not say "Holy." The entire world was quiet and silent, and **the voice** went out: "I am the Lord your God."

cards.he: וַיִּקַּח סֵפֶר הַבְּרִית וַיִּקְרָא בְּאׇזְנֵי הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּר יְיָ נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע
cards.en: Then he took the record of the covenant and read it aloud to the people. And they said, “All that יהוה has spoken we will faithfully do!”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayikach seifer hab'rit vayikra b'oznei ha-am vayomru kol asher diber Adonai na-aseh v'nishma

cards.he: נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע
cards.tl: Na-aseh v'nishma
cards.gloss: Two Hebrew verbs, which the Contemporary Torah renders together as "we will faithfully do" (24:7). The Talmud's English hears them one at a time: "We will do" and "We will hear."

cards.title: The angels' secret
cards.body: **Rabbi Simai**: because Israel put "We will do" before "We will hear," **600,000 angels** tied **two crowns** on each person, one for each promise. **Rabbi Elazar**: a heavenly voice asked, "Who revealed to my children this secret that the ministering angels use?" Angels **act first, then listen**.

cards.q: Why does the Talmud call putting "We will do" before "We will hear" the angels' secret?
choices: Angels act on God's word first, and understand after
Only angels heard the Ten Commandments
cards.why: Doing first, understanding after: **na'aseh v'nishma**.
wrong_why: Not the Talmud's point.
Not the Talmud's point.

cards.prompt: The people promise to do before they understand. Where in your practice has doing come before understanding, and what did the doing teach you?

points: At **the foot of the mountain**, or under it (Shabbat 88a).
Accepted again, **freely**, in Esther's time (Rava).
The world fell **silent** for "I am" (Shemot Rabbah 29:9).
**Na'aseh v'nishma**: the angels' secret.

lessons.title: Moses (6): V'shamru
lessons.check_note: Beitzah 16a read 11/11.

cards.title: A pause in the building
cards.body: God is giving Moses detailed plans for the **Tabernacle**. Then, before the work begins, the Torah stops for **Shabbat**.

cards.q: According to Resh Lakish, what does God give each person on Shabbat eve?
cards.why: A **neshamah yeteirah**, an additional soul, taken back when Shabbat ends.

cards.he:
וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לְדֹרֹתָם בְּרִית עוֹלָם
בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹת הִוא לְעֹלָם כִּי־שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְיָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ
cards.en: The Israelite people shall keep the sabbath, observing the sabbath throughout the ages as a covenant for all time: it shall be a sign for all time between Me and the people of Israel. For in six days יהוה made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day [God] ceased from work and was refreshed.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
V'shamru v'nei Yisrael et haShabbat la-asot et haShabbat l'dorotam b'rit olam
Beini uvein b'nei Yisrael ot hi l'olam ki sheishet yamim asah Adonai et hashamayim v'et ha-aretz uvayom hash'vi-i shavat vayinafash

cards.body: These are the words of **V'shamru**, which we sing on Shabbat.

cards.he: שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ
cards.tl: Shavat vayinafash
cards.gloss: "[God] ceased from work and was refreshed" (31:17). The last word, **vayinafash**, shares its root with **nefesh**, soul.

cards.title: An additional soul
cards.body: **Resh Lakish**: God gives a person **an additional soul** on Shabbat eve and takes it back when Shabbat ends. He reads **vayinafash** as **vai, nefesh**: woe for the soul that is lost.

cards.q: How does Resh Lakish read the word vayinafash?
choices: As vai, nefesh: "woe for the additional soul that is lost" when Shabbat ends
As a word for rest, and nothing more
cards.why: **Vai, nefesh**: the additional soul leaves as Shabbat goes out.
wrong_why: He finds more in the word.
Not his reading.

cards.prompt: Resh Lakish says Shabbat brings you an additional soul, and its leaving is felt. What in you feels larger on Shabbat?

points: The Torah pauses the building **for Shabbat**.
**V'shamru**: a sign between God and Israel (31:16-17).
Beitzah 16a: **an additional soul** on Shabbat.

lessons.title: Moses (7): Broken tablets
lessons.check_note: Shabbat 87a and Berakhot 8b read 11/11.

cards.title: Forty days
cards.body: Moses has been on the mountain forty days. Below, the people lose hope and make **a golden calf**. Moses comes down carrying the tablets.

cards.q: According to the Talmud, what was kept in the Ark with the second tablets?
choices: The broken pieces of the first tablets
cards.why: **Both** the whole tablets and the **broken** ones (Berakhot 8b).

cards.he: וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר קָרַב אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶה וַיַּרְא אֶת־הָעֵגֶל וּמְחֹלֹת וַיִּחַר־אַף מֹשֶׁה וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ מִיָּדָו אֶת־הַלֻּחֹת וַיְשַׁבֵּר אֹתָם תַּחַת הָהָר
cards.en: As soon as Moses came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he became enraged; and he hurled the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vay'hi ka-asher karav el hamachaneh vayar et ha-eigel um'cholot vayichar af Moshe vayashleich miyadav et haluchot vayshabeir otam tachat hahar

cards.title: God agreed
cards.body: Moses did **three things on his own judgment**, and God agreed with him. One was **breaking the tablets**. His reasoning: if one who has turned from God may not eat even the Passover lamb, one mitzvah, how could a people worshipping a calf receive **the whole Torah**?

cards.q: In Shabbat 87a, how did God respond to Moses breaking the tablets?
cards.why: One of three things Moses did **on his own**, and God **agreed**.
wrong_why: The Talmud says the opposite.
The Talmud says God agreed.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה פְּסׇל־לְךָ שְׁנֵי־לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים כָּרִאשֹׁנִים וְכָתַבְתִּי עַל־הַלֻּחֹת אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ עַל־הַלֻּחֹת הָרִאשֹׁנִים אֲשֶׁר שִׁבַּרְתָּ
cards.en: יהוה said to Moses: “Carve two tablets of stone like the first, and I will inscribe upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vayomer Adonai el Moshe p'sol l'cha sh'nei luchot avanim karishonim v'chatavti al haluchot et had'varim asher hayu al haluchot harishonim asher shibarta

cards.title: Whole and broken, side by side
cards.body: **Both the whole tablets and the broken tablets** were placed in the Ark. So, says **Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi**, honor an elder who has forgotten their learning through no fault of their own: like the broken tablets, they are still holy.

cards.q: What lesson does Berakhot 8b draw from the broken tablets?
choices: Honor an elder who has lost their learning; what is broken is still holy
cards.why: The broken tablets stayed **in the Ark**, beside the whole ones.
wrong_why: The Talmud says they were kept, not buried.
Not the Talmud's lesson here.

cards.prompt: The broken tablets were kept in the Ark beside the whole ones. What broken piece do you carry, and does it still deserve a holy place?

points: Moses **shattered** the tablets (32:19).
Shabbat 87a: **God agreed** with him.
Berakhot 8b: **whole and broken** together in the Ark.

lessons.title: Moses (8): Thirteen attributes
lessons.check_note: Rosh Hashanah 17b read 11/11. Liturgy card: CHECK with cantor where Mishkan HaNefesh and CBB use the Thirteen Attributes.

cards.title: Show me
cards.body: After the calf, Moses asks to see God's presence. God answers: you cannot see My face, but I will **pass before you** and proclaim My name.

cards.q: In the Talmud, God appears to Moses wrapped in a tallit, like a prayer leader.
cards.why: Rabbi Yochanan: "were it not explicitly written" it would be impossible to say.

cards.he:
וַיַּעֲבֹר יְיָ  עַל־פָּנָיו וַיִּקְרָא יְיָ  יְיָ אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת
נֹצֵר חֶסֶד לָאֲלָפִים נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן וָפֶשַׁע וְחַטָּאָה וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה פֹּקֵד  עֲוֺן אָבוֹת עַל־בָּנִים וְעַל־בְּנֵי בָנִים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִים
cards.en: יהוה passed before him and proclaimed: “!יהוה! יהוה a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and faithfulness, extending kindness to the thousandth generation, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin—yet not remitting all punishment, but visiting the iniquity of parents upon children and children’s children, upon the third and fourth generations.”
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vaya-avor Adonai  al panav vayikra Adonai  Adonai eil rachum v'chanun erech apayim v'rav chesed ve-emet
Notzeir chesed la-alafim nosei avon vafesha v'chata-ah v'nakei lo y'nakeh pokeid  avon avot al banim v'al b'nei vanim al shileishim v'al ribei-im

cards.he: אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד
cards.tl: Eil rachum v'chanun erech apayim v'rav chesed
cards.gloss: "a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness" (34:6). The opening of the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy**.

cards.title: God in a tallit
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan**: were it not written, it would be impossible to say it. God **wrapped in a tallit like a prayer leader** and showed Moses the order of prayer: whenever Israel sins, let them recite **the thirteen attributes** before Me, and I will forgive them. **Rav Yehuda**: there is a covenant that they **never return empty-handed**.

cards.q: In Rosh Hashanah 17b, what did God teach Moses?
choices: An order of prayer: recite the Thirteen Attributes when Israel sins
cards.why: God as **prayer leader**, teaching the words that bring forgiveness.
wrong_why: Not in this passage.
Not in this passage.

cards.title: Truth, then kindness
cards.body: The verse says both "abounding in **kindness**" and "**faithfulness**," which the Talmud reads as **truth**, strict justice. **Ilfa**: God begins with justice, but seeing that **the world cannot survive on judgment alone**, turns to kindness.

cards.q: According to Ilfa, why does kindness win out over strict justice?
choices: The world could not survive on judgment alone
cards.why: Judgment first, then **mercy**, because without it the world could not stand.
wrong_why: Not Ilfa's reason.
Ilfa keeps both.

cards.title: In the prayer book
cards.body: These words return in Jewish prayer on **festivals and the High Holy Days**, often as the Ark is opened.

src.ref: Exodus 34:6-7 in festival and High Holy Day liturgy

cards.prompt: In the Talmud, God gives Moses words to pray when the people have failed. When you have fallen short, what words help you begin again?

points: God **passes before** Moses and proclaims (34:6-7).
God in **a tallit**, teaching an order of prayer (Rosh Hashanah 17b).
The Thirteen Attributes **never return empty**.
Justice first, then **kindness**.

lessons.title: Moses (9): The shining face
lessons.check_note: Shemot Rabbah 47:6 (Sefaria Midrash Rabbah 2022) read 11/12. English: Contemporary Torah.

cards.title: Coming down again
cards.body: Moses comes down Mount Sinai a second time, carrying the new tablets. Something about him has changed, and **he is the only one who does not know it**.

cards.q: Which is one Midrash's answer to where Moses' radiance came from?
choices: A bit of ink left on his quill, passed over his head
The fire of the burning bush
cards.why: Resh Lakish's answer, one of three in Shemot Rabbah 47:6.

cards.he:
וַיְהִי בְּרֶדֶת מֹשֶׁה מֵהַר סִינַי וּשְׁנֵי לֻחֹת הָֽעֵדֻת בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה בְּרִדְתּוֹ מִן־הָהָר וּמֹשֶׁה לֹֽא־יָדַע כִּי קָרַן עוֹר פָּנָיו בְּדַבְּרוֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃
וַיַּרְא אַהֲרֹן וְכׇל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־מֹשֶׁה וְהִנֵּה קָרַן עוֹר פָּנָיו וַיִּֽירְאוּ מִגֶּשֶׁת אֵלָֽיו׃
cards.en: So Moses came down from Mount Sinai. And as Moses came down from the mountain bearing the two tablets of the Pact, Moses was not aware that the skin of his face was radiant, since he had spoken with God. Aaron and all the Israelites saw that the skin of Moses’ face was radiant; and they shrank from coming near him.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'hi b'redet Moshe meihar sinai ush'nei luchot ha-eidut b'yad Moshe b'ridto min hahar umosheh lo yada ki karan or panav b'dab'ro ito.
Vayar aharon v'chol b'nei Yisrael et Moshe v'hinei karan or panav vayir'u migeshet eilav.

cards.he: וּמֹשֶׁה לֹֽא־יָדַע כִּי קָרַן עוֹר פָּנָיו
cards.tl: Umosheh lo yada ki karan or panav
cards.gloss: "Moses was not aware that the skin of his face was radiant" (34:29). The same letters, ק־ר־ן, spell **horn** in Hannah's song (1 Samuel 2:1).

cards.title: Where did the light come from?
cards.body: The Midrash gives three answers. **The Rabbis**: from the cleft of the rock, where God's glory passed by (33:22). **Rabbi Berekhya**: the tablets were six handbreadths long; Moses held two, the Divine Presence held two, and **from the space between** came the rays. **Resh Lakish**: a bit of ink was left on the quill after writing the Torah, and Moses passed it over his head.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Berekhya, where did the rays come from?
choices: The space on the tablets between Moses' hands and the Divine Presence
cards.why: Light from **the space between** the human hand and God's.
wrong_why: Not in this Midrash.
Not in this Midrash.

cards.he:
וַיְכַל מֹשֶׁה מִדַּבֵּר אִתָּם וַיִּתֵּן עַל־פָּנָיו מַסְוֶֽה׃
וּבְבֹא מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי יְיָ לְדַבֵּר אִתּוֹ יָסִיר אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶה עַד־צֵאתוֹ וְיָצָא וְדִבֶּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵת אֲשֶׁר יְצֻוֶּֽה׃
וְרָאוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־פְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה כִּי קָרַן עוֹר פְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה וְהֵשִׁיב מֹשֶׁה אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶה עַל־פָּנָיו עַד־בֹּאוֹ לְדַבֵּר אִתּֽוֹ׃
cards.en: And when Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face. Whenever Moses went in before יהוה to converse, he would leave the veil off until he came out; and when he came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded, the Israelites would see how radiant the skin of Moses’ face was. Moses would then put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with God.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vay'chal Moshe midabeir itam vayitein al panav masveh.
Uv'vo Moshe lifnei Adonai l'dabeir ito yasir et hamasveh ad tzeito v'yatza v'diber el b'nei Yisrael eit asher y'tzuveh.
V'ra-u v'nei Yisrael et p'nei Moshe ki karan or p'nei Moshe v'heishiv Moshe et hamasveh al panav ad bo-o l'dabeir ito.

cards.he: וַיִּתֵּן עַל־פָּנָיו מַסְוֶֽה׃
cards.tl: Vayitein al panav masveh.
cards.gloss: "he put a veil over his face" (34:33).

cards.q: When did Moses take the veil off?
choices: When he spoke with God, and while he taught the people
cards.why: Face uncovered **before God**, and while passing God's words **to the people** (34:34-35).
wrong_why: Not in the text.
He took it off each time he went in before God.

cards.prompt: Moses does not know his face is shining; everyone else sees it first. What have others seen in you that you could not see yourself?

points: Moses' face was **radiant**, and he **did not know** (34:29).
Shemot Rabbah 47:6: from the cleft, from **between** the hands, or from **the ink**.
A **veil**, lifted before God and while teaching.

lessons.title: Moses (10): Bezalel the builder
lessons.check_note: Berakhot 55a read 11/12.

cards.title: Called by name
cards.body: God has given Moses plans for **the Tabernacle**. Now God names the artist who will build it.

cards.q: In the Talmud, Bezalel knew how to join the letters with which heaven and earth were created.
cards.why: Rav's teaching in Berakhot 55a.

cards.he:
וַיְדַבֵּר יְיָ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
רְאֵה קָרָאתִֽי בְשֵׁם בְּצַלְאֵל בֶּן־אוּרִי בֶן־חוּר לְמַטֵּה יְהוּדָֽה׃
וָאֲמַלֵּא אֹתוֹ רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים בְּחׇכְמָה וּבִתְבוּנָה וּבְדַעַת וּבְכׇל־מְלָאכָֽה׃
cards.en: יהוה spoke to Moses: See, I have singled out by name Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. I have endowed him with a divine spirit of skill, ability, and knowledge in every kind of craft;
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vaydabeir Adonai el Moshe leimor.
R'ei karati v'sheim b'tzal'eil ben uri ven chur l'matei Y'hudah.
Va-amalei oto ruach Elohim b'chochmah uvitvunah uv'da-at uv'chol m'lachah.

cards.he: בְּצַלְאֵל
cards.tl: B'tzal'eil
cards.gloss: Bezalel (31:2). The Talmud hears his name as בְּצֵל אֵל, **in God's shadow**.

cards.title: In God's shadow
cards.body: **Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani**: God said tabernacle, then ark and vessels. Moses told Bezalel the reverse: ark, vessels, then tabernacle. Bezalel objected: people build the house first, then bring in the furniture; where would I put the vessels? Moses answered: "Perhaps you were in God’s shadow," and knew exactly what God said.

cards.q: In Berakhot 55a, how did Bezalel know Moses had the order backward?
choices: You build the house before you put the vessels in it
He read it on the tablets
cards.why: Common sense, and a name: **in God's shadow**.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.he: בְּחׇכְמָה וּבִתְבוּנָה וּבְדַעַת
cards.tl: B'chochmah uvitvunah uv'da-at
cards.gloss: "skill, ability, and knowledge" (31:3).

cards.title: The letters of creation
cards.body: **Rav**: "Bezalel knew how to join the letters with which heaven and earth were created." The proof: the same three words that describe Bezalel, **wisdom, understanding and knowledge**, describe how God founded the earth and the heavens (Proverbs 3:19-20).

cards.q: How does Rav show that Bezalel knew the letters of creation?
choices: The same three gifts describe Bezalel and God's making of heaven and earth
He was born on the first day
cards.why: **Wisdom, understanding, knowledge**: the tools of creation, given to an artist.
wrong_why: Moses wrote the Torah.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.title: Ask the people
cards.body: **Rabbi Yitzchak**: a leader may be appointed only **with the community's consent**. God asked Moses whether Bezalel was suitable, then told him: go ask Israel too. They answered: if he is right in God's eyes and yours, all the more so in ours.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר מַרְבִּים הָעָם לְהָבִיא מִדֵּי הָֽעֲבֹדָה לַמְּלָאכָה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּה יְיָ לַעֲשֹׂת אֹתָֽהּ׃
וַיְצַו מֹשֶׁה וַיַּעֲבִירוּ קוֹל בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה לֵאמֹר אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה אַל־יַעֲשׂוּ־עוֹד מְלָאכָה לִתְרוּמַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וַיִּכָּלֵא הָעָם מֵהָבִֽיא׃
וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם לְכׇל־הַמְּלָאכָה לַעֲשׂוֹת אֹתָהּ וְהוֹתֵֽר׃
