cards.en: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than is needed for the tasks entailed in the work that יהוה has commanded to be done.” Moses thereupon had this proclamation made throughout the camp: “Let no man or woman make further effort toward gifts for the sanctuary!” So the people stopped bringing: their efforts had been more than enough for all the tasks to be done.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomru el Moshe leimor marbim ha-am l'havi midei ha-avodah lam'lachah asher tzivah Adonai la-asot otah.
Vaytzav Moshe vaya-aviru kol bamachaneh leimor ish v'ishah al ya-asu od m'lachah litrumat hakodesh vayikalei ha-am meihavi.
V'ham'lachah haytah dayam l'chol ham'lachah la-asot otah v'hoteir.

cards.he: מַרְבִּים הָעָם לְהָבִיא
cards.tl: Marbim ha-am l'havi
cards.gloss: "The people are bringing more than is needed" (36:5). Moses has to tell them to **stop giving**.

cards.prompt: Bezalel understood the plan better than the instructions he was given. When has making something with your hands taught you what words could not?

points: Bezalel, **called by name** (31:2).
Berakhot 55a: **in God's shadow**, house before vessels.
Rav: he knew **the letters of creation**.
A leader needs **the people's consent**.
The people gave **more than enough** (36:5).

lessons.title: Moses (11): On Mount Nebo
lessons.check_note: Bava Batra 15a, 17a and Sotah 14a read 11/12.

cards.title: The view from the mountain
cards.body: Moses climbs **Mount Nebo**. From the summit, God shows him the whole land, the land he will **not** enter.

cards.q: In one view in the Talmud, Moses himself wrote the verses about his own death.
cards.why: Rabbi Shimon: God dictated, and "Moses wrote with tears."

cards.he: וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה מֵעַרְבֹת מוֹאָב אֶל־הַר נְבוֹ רֹאשׁ הַפִּסְגָּה אֲשֶׁר עַל־פְּנֵי יְרֵחוֹ וַיַּרְאֵהוּ יְיָ אֶת־כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ אֶת־הַגִּלְעָד עַד־דָּֽן׃
cards.en: Moses went up from the steppes of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, opposite Jericho, and יהוה showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan;
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: Vaya-al Moshe mei-arvot mo-av el har n'vo rosh hapisgah asher al p'nei y'reicho vayar'eihu Adonai et kol ha-aretz et hagil'ad ad dan.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ אֵלָיו זֹאת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב לֵאמֹר לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה הֶרְאִיתִיךָ בְעֵינֶיךָ וְשָׁמָּה לֹא תַעֲבֹֽר׃
וַיָּמׇת שָׁם מֹשֶׁה עֶבֶד־יְיָ בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹאָב עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָֽה׃
וַיִּקְבֹּר אֹתוֹ בַגַּי בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹאָב מוּל בֵּית פְּעוֹר וְלֹא־יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת־קְבֻרָתוֹ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
וּמֹשֶׁה בֶּן־מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה בְּמֹתוֹ לֹא־כָהֲתָה עֵינוֹ וְלֹא־נָס לֵחֹֽה׃
cards.en: And יהוה said to him, “This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, ‘I will assign it to your offspring.’ I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you shall not cross there.” So Moses the servant of יהוה died there, in the land of Moab, at the command of יהוה. [God] buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, near Beth-peor; and no one knows his burial place to this day. Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eyes were undimmed and his vigor unabated.
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl:
Vayomer Adonai eilav zot ha-aretz asher nishbati l'avraham l'yitzchak ul'ya-akov leimor l'zar'acha et'nenah her'iticha v'einecha v'shamah lo ta-avor.
Vayamot sham Moshe eved Adonai b'eretz mo-av al pi Adonai.
Vayikbor oto vagai b'eretz mo-av mul beit p'or v'lo yada ish et k'vurato ad hayom hazeh.
Umosheh ben mei-ah v'esrim shanah b'moto lo chahatah eino v'lo nas leicho.

cards.he: עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָֽה׃
cards.tl: Al pi Adonai.
cards.gloss: "at the command of יהוה" (34:5). The Talmud reads the Hebrew literally: **by the mouth** of God.

cards.title: A kiss
cards.body: Six people, the Sages teach, were beyond the Angel of Death's power: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, **Moses, Aaron and Miriam**. Of Moses and Aaron the Torah says they died **by the mouth** of God, meaning **with a kiss**. Rabbi Elazar includes Miriam too.

cards.q: How does Bava Batra 17a read "by the mouth" of God?
choices: Moses died with a kiss, not by the Angel of Death
cards.why: The last touch was **God's kiss**.
wrong_why: Not the Talmud's reading.
Not the Talmud's reading.

cards.title: God buried him
cards.body: Who buried Moses? **God**. So, says **Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina**, follow God's ways: God clothed the naked, visited the sick, comforted mourners, and **buried the dead**; so should you. **Rabbi Samlai**: the Torah begins with kindness (clothing Adam and Eve) and **ends with kindness** (burying Moses).

cards.q: What does Sotah 14a learn from God burying Moses?
choices: We should bury the dead, as God did
cards.why: God's acts are **our pattern**: clothe, visit, comfort, bury.
wrong_why: The Talmud notes the secret grave, but the lesson is kindness.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.title: Written with tears
cards.body: Who wrote "Moses died there"? **Rabbi Yehuda**: Joshua wrote the last eight verses. **Rabbi Shimon**: the Torah cannot be missing a letter. Until here God dictated and Moses wrote; from here, God dictated and "Moses wrote with tears." So the last eight verses are read by **one person**, without a break.

cards.he: וְלֹא־קָם נָבִיא עוֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה אֲשֶׁר יְדָעוֹ יְיָ פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִֽים׃
cards.en: Never again did there arise in Israel a prophet like Moses—whom יהוה singled out, face to face,
cards.en_src: The Contemporary Torah, Jewish Publication Society, 2006
cards.tl: V'lo kam navi od b'Yisrael k'mosheh asher y'da-o Adonai panim el panim.

cards.he: פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִֽים׃
cards.tl: Panim el panim.
cards.gloss: "face to face" (34:10).

cards.prompt: Moses sees the land but does not enter it, and others carry on. What work of yours might someone else finish after you?

points: From Nebo, Moses **sees** the land he will not enter.
Bava Batra 17a: he died **with a kiss**.
Sotah 14a: **God buried him**; the Torah ends in kindness.
Bava Batra 15a: "Moses wrote **with tears**."
**Face to face** (34:10).

units.title: Hannah
units.subtitle: A woman's prayer, and the rules of prayer

lessons.title: Hannah (1): A rival and a husband
lessons.check_note: Bava Batra 16a, Rosh Hashanah 11a, Megillah 31a read on Sefaria 11/12. English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive. CHECK: Mishkan HaNefesh / CBB read Hannah as the Rosh Hashanah haftarah (and on which day).

cards.title: Year after year
cards.body: Every year Elkanah and his family go up to **the House of GOD**. His wife Peninnah has children. His wife **Hannah** has none, and every year it hurts again.

cards.q: In one view in the Talmud, Peninnah taunted Hannah for the sake of Heaven.
cards.why: Rabbi Levi: she upset Hannah "in order to motivate her to pray."

cards.he: וְלוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֵׁם אַחַת חַנָּה וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית פְּנִנָּה וַיְהִי לִפְנִנָּה יְלָדִים וּלְחַנָּה אֵין יְלָדִֽים׃
cards.en: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah; Peninnah had children, but Hannah was childless.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'lo sh'tei nashim sheim achat chanah v'sheim hasheinit p'ninah vay'hi lifninah y'ladim ul'chanah ein y'ladim.

cards.he: וּלְחַנָּה אֵין יְלָדִֽים׃
cards.tl: Ul'chanah ein y'ladim.
cards.gloss: "but Hannah was childless" (1:2).

cards.he:
וְכִעֲסַתָּה צָרָתָהּ גַּם־כַּעַס בַּעֲבוּר הַרְּעִמָהּ כִּֽי־סָגַר יְיָ בְּעַד רַחְמָֽהּ׃
וְכֵן יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה מִדֵּי עֲלֹתָהּ בְּבֵית יְיָ כֵּן תַּכְעִסֶנָּה וַתִּבְכֶּה וְלֹא תֹאכַֽל׃
וַיֹּאמֶר לָהּ אֶלְקָנָה אִישָׁהּ חַנָּה לָמֶה תִבְכִּי וְלָמֶה לֹא תֹֽאכְלִי וְלָמֶה יֵרַע לְבָבֵךְ הֲלוֹא אָֽנֹכִי טוֹב לָךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָה בָּנִֽים׃
cards.en: Moreover, her rival, to make her miserable, would taunt her that GOD had closed her womb. This happened year after year: Every time she went up to the House of GOD, the other would taunt her, so that she wept and would not eat. Her husband Elkanah said to her, “Hannah, why are you crying and why aren’t you eating? Why are you so sad? Am I not more devoted to you than ten sons?”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
V'chi-asatah tzaratah gam ka-as ba-avur har'imah ki sagar Adonai b'ad rachmah.
V'chein ya-aseh shanah v'shanah midei alotah b'veit Adonai kein tach'isenah vativkeh v'lo tochal.
Vayomer lah elkanah ishah chanah lameh tivki v'lameh lo tochli v'lameh yeira l'vaveich halo anochi tov lach mei-asarah banim.

cards.he: וְכִעֲסַתָּה צָרָתָהּ גַּם־כַּעַס בַּעֲבוּר הַרְּעִמָהּ
cards.tl: V'chi-asatah tzaratah gam ka-as ba-avur har'imah
cards.gloss: "her rival, to make her miserable, would taunt her" (1:6).

cards.title: For the sake of Heaven?
cards.body: **Rabbi Levi**: both Satan, who accused Job, and **Peninnah** acted for the sake of Heaven. Peninnah upset Hannah "in order to motivate her to pray." The Talmud adds that when this was taught, Satan came and **kissed the teacher's feet** in gratitude.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Levi, why did Peninnah taunt Hannah?
choices: To make Elkanah send her away
cards.why: Rabbi Levi reads even the taunting as aimed at **prayer**.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Rabbi Levi reads her more generously.

cards.he: הֲלוֹא אָֽנֹכִי טוֹב לָךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָה בָּנִֽים׃
cards.tl: Halo anochi tov lach mei-asarah banim.
cards.gloss: "Am I not more devoted to you than ten sons?" (1:8). Elkanah answers her grief with **his love**.

cards.title: Remembered on Rosh Hashanah
cards.body: The Talmud teaches that on Rosh Hashanah, **Sarah, Rachel and Hannah** were remembered by God and conceived sons. **Rabbi Elazar** links the word **remembered** in Hannah's story (1:19) to the Rosh Hashanah verse "memorial proclaimed with the blast of a shofar" (Leviticus 23:24).

cards.q: Which women does the Talmud say were remembered on Rosh Hashanah?
cards.why: Three women who waited for a child: **Sarah, Rachel and Hannah**.
wrong_why: Not this list.
Not this list.

cards.title: Read on Rosh Hashanah
cards.body: So the Talmud names Hannah's story, **1 Samuel 1:1 to 2:10**, as a haftarah for Rosh Hashanah, because she too was blessed with a child on that day.

cards.prompt: Peninnah's taunts and Elkanah's love both miss what Hannah needs. When have you felt unseen by people close to you?

points: Hannah has **no children**; Peninnah **taunts** her (1:2, 1:6).
Rabbi Levi: Peninnah meant to **move her to pray**.
"**Am I not more devoted to you than ten sons?**"
Remembered on **Rosh Hashanah**, read on Rosh Hashanah.

lessons.title: Hannah (2): Only her lips moved
lessons.check_note: Berakhot 31a-b and Zohar Vayigash 10:99 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12.

cards.title: The priest is watching
cards.body: Hannah rises and prays before GOD. **Eli the priest** watches her mouth, and he gets it wrong.

cards.q: Which rule for the Amidah does the Talmud learn from Hannah?
choices: Say the words with your lips, but quietly
Pray aloud so others can answer amen
cards.why: Her lips moved, and **her voice could not be heard** (1:13).

cards.he:
וְהָיָה כִּי הִרְבְּתָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לִפְנֵי יְיָ וְעֵלִי שֹׁמֵר אֶת־פִּֽיהָ׃
וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל־לִבָּהּ רַק שְׂפָתֶיהָ נָּעוֹת וְקוֹלָהּ לֹא יִשָּׁמֵעַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ עֵלִי לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה׃
cards.en: As she kept on praying before GOD, Eli watched her mouth. Now Hannah was praying in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
V'hayah ki hirb'tah l'hitpaleil lifnei Adonai v'eili shomeir et piha.
V'chanah hi m'daberet al libah rak s'fateha na-ot v'kolah lo yishameia vayachsh'veha eili l'shikorah.

cards.he: וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל־לִבָּהּ רַק שְׂפָתֶיהָ נָּעוֹת וְקוֹלָהּ לֹא יִשָּׁמֵעַ
cards.tl: V'chanah hi m'daberet al libah rak s'fateha na-ot v'kolah lo yishameia
cards.gloss: "Hannah was praying in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard" (1:13).

cards.title: Laws from one verse
cards.body: **Rav Hamnuna** draws laws of prayer from this verse. **In her heart**: focus your heart on your prayer. **Only her lips moved**: say the words with your lips, not only in your mind. **Her voice could not be heard**: do not raise your voice in the Amidah. **Eli thought she was drunk**: a drunk person may not pray.

cards.q: What does Rav Hamnuna learn from "only her lips moved"?
choices: Say the words with your lips, not only in your heart
Pray as quickly as you can
Never pray when you are sad
cards.why: Prayer is **spoken**, even when it is silent.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Hannah prays in great sorrow.

cards.body: These are the rules for the **Amidah**, the standing prayer, which begins with **Avot**: said quietly, with the lips, and with the heart.

cards.title: The voice that cannot be heard
cards.body: The **Zohar** says true prayer is "another voice attached to the voice which is heard." So a person should pray with the voice no one else hears, **like Hannah**, whose voice could not be heard.

cards.he: וַתַּעַן חַנָּה וַתֹּאמֶר לֹא אֲדֹנִי אִשָּׁה קְשַׁת־רוּחַ אָנֹכִי וְיַיִן וְשֵׁכָר לֹא שָׁתִיתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּךְ אֶת־נַפְשִׁי לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָֽה׃
cards.en: And Hannah replied, “Oh no, my lord! I am a very unhappy woman. I have drunk no wine or other strong drink, but I have been pouring out my heart to GOD.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vata-an chanah vatomer lo adoni ishah k'shat ruach anochi v'yayin v'sheichar lo shatiti va-eshpoch et nafshi lifnei Adonai.

cards.he: וָאֶשְׁפֹּךְ אֶת־נַפְשִׁי
cards.tl: Va-eshpoch et nafshi
cards.gloss: "I have been pouring out my heart to GOD" (1:15).

cards.title: Not a master here
cards.body: On "Oh no, my lord!", one sage says Hannah was hinting: in this matter **you are not a master**, and the Divine Spirit is not on you, since you suspect me falsely. **Rabbi Elazar** learns two more rules: someone wrongly suspected should **say so** and clear her name, and someone who suspected wrongly must **make peace and bless**, as Eli does next.

cards.he: וַיַּעַן עֵלִי וַיֹּאמֶר לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם וֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יִתֵּן אֶת־שֵׁלָתֵךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתְּ מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃
cards.en: “Then go in peace,” said Eli, “and may the God of Israel grant you what you have asked.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vaya-an eili vayomer l'chi l'shalom v'Elohei Yisrael yitein et sheilateich asher sha-alt mei-imo.

cards.q: What does Rabbi Elazar learn from Eli's "Then go in peace"?
choices: Whoever wrongly suspects someone must make peace and bless them
Never pray in a public place
cards.why: Eli was wrong, and he **blesses** her.
wrong_why: The Talmud says Eli was wrong here.
Not the Talmud's lesson.

cards.prompt: To the priest, Hannah's prayer looked like drunkenness. What does your most honest prayer look like from the outside?

points: "**Only her lips moved**, but her voice could not be heard" (1:13).
Rav Hamnuna: **heart, lips, quiet**, and never drunk.
Zohar: the **voice no one hears**.
Eli was wrong, so he **blesses** her (Berakhot 31b).

lessons.title: Hannah (3): God of Hosts
lessons.check_note: Berakhot 31b and Zohar Toldot 3:20 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12. Rabbi's-teaching card: the connection is mine; check with Jamie.

cards.title: A vow
cards.body: Weeping, Hannah makes **a vow**: if God gives her a child, she will give the child back to God.

cards.q: According to the Talmud, Hannah was the first person ever to call God "Lord of Hosts."
cards.why: Rabbi Elazar: no one, since Creation, until Hannah.

cards.he:
וְהִיא מָרַת נָפֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל־יְיָ וּבָכֹה תִבְכֶּֽה׃
וַתִּדֹּר נֶדֶר וַתֹּאמַר יְיָ צְבָאוֹת אִם־רָאֹה תִרְאֶה ׀ בׇּעֳנִי אֲמָתֶךָ וּזְכַרְתַּנִי וְלֹא־תִשְׁכַּח אֶת־אֲמָתֶךָ וְנָתַתָּה לַאֲמָתְךָ זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים וּנְתַתִּיו לַֽיהֹוָה כׇּל־יְמֵי חַיָּיו וּמוֹרָה לֹא־יַעֲלֶה עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃
cards.en: In her wretchedness, she prayed to GOD, weeping all the while. And she made this vow: “O GOD of Hosts, if You will look upon the suffering of Your maidservant and will remember me and not forget Your maidservant, and if You will grant Your maidservant a child like the others have, I will dedicate it to GOD for all the days of its life; and no razor shall ever touch its head.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
V'hi marat nafesh vatitpaleil al Adonai uvacho tivkeh.
Vatidor neder vatomar Adonai tz'va-ot im ra-o tir'eh  bo-oni amatecha uz'chartani v'lo tishkach et amatecha v'natatah la-amatcha zera anashim un'tativ laihovah kol y'mei chayav umorah lo ya-aleh al rosho.

cards.he: יְיָ צְבָאוֹת
cards.tl: Adonai tz'va-ot
cards.gloss: "O GOD of Hosts" (1:11).

cards.title: The first to say it
cards.body: **Rabbi Elazar**: from the day God created the world, no one called God **Lord of Hosts** until Hannah. Her argument: of all the hosts upon hosts You created, is it so hard for You to give me **one son**?

cards.q: In Berakhot 31b, why does Hannah call God "Lord of Hosts"?
choices: Among all the hosts God made, one son should not be hard to give
It was the Temple's usual name for God
cards.why: **Hosts upon hosts**, and she asks for one child.
wrong_why: The Talmud says no one had used it before her.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.he: וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל־יְיָ
cards.tl: Vatitpaleil al Adonai
cards.gloss: "she prayed to GOD" (1:10). The Hebrew preposition here is unusual: **upon** or **onto** God, and the Talmud notices it.

cards.title: Speaking boldly upward
cards.body: **Rabbi Elazar**: "Hannah spoke impertinently toward God on High," since the verse says she prayed **onto** God, not to God. He also reads her doubled "if You will look" as a dare: if You look now, good; if not, **You will see** anyway, and she tells God how she will hold God to the Torah's own promise.

cards.title: Above the stars
cards.body: The **Zohar** reads the same word another way: Hannah's prayer went **above** ordinary fate. Like Isaac's prayer for Rebekah, it rose "above the planetary influences."

cards.q: How does Rabbi Elazar read Hannah praying "onto" God?
choices: She spoke boldly, even impertinently, toward Heaven
She prayed on someone else's behalf
cards.why: Hannah does not only plead; she **argues**.
wrong_why: Not the Talmud's reading.
She prays for herself.

cards.title: A people growing up
cards.body: Your rabbi reads the Torah as a people **growing up**: from a child's hero-God, through a strained and complicated relationship, toward God present in our own choices. Hannah is a grown-up's prayer: no priest needed, her own words, even **arguing with God**. On the same page of Talmud, Rabbi Akiva says, "The Torah spoke in the language of men."

src.ref: Teaching from Jamie's rabbi (oral, as Jamie retold it); Berakhot 31b
src.note: connection to Hannah is mine; check with Jamie

cards.he:
אֶל־הַנַּעַר הַזֶּה הִתְפַּלָּלְתִּי וַיִּתֵּן יְיָ לִי אֶת־שְׁאֵלָתִי אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃
וְגַם אָנֹכִי הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ לַֽיהֹוָה כׇּל־הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר הָיָה הוּא שָׁאוּל לַיהֹוָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ שָׁם לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
cards.en: It was this boy I prayed for; and GOD has granted me what I asked. I, in turn, hereby lend him to GOD. For as long as he lives he is lent to GOD.” And they bowed low there before GOD.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
El hana-ar hazeh hitpalalti vayitein Adonai li et sh'eilati asher sha-alti mei-imo.
V'gam anochi hish'iltihu laihovah kol hayamim asher hayah hu sha-ul laihovah vayishtachu sham laihovah.

cards.he: וְגַם אָנֹכִי הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ לַֽיהֹוָה
cards.tl: V'gam anochi hish'iltihu laihovah
cards.gloss: "I, in turn, hereby lend him to GOD" (1:28). **Asked** (שָׁאַלְתִּי, 1:27) and **lent** (הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ) come from the same root.

cards.title: For this boy I prayed
cards.body: The Talmud tells a story behind 1:25-27. Young **Samuel** ruled, correctly, that anyone may slaughter an offering, not only a priest. But he ruled **in front of his teacher**, Eli, who said that deserved death. Hannah cried out: "I am the woman who stood here with you." Eli offered to pray for a greater son. She answered: for **this** boy I prayed, and I want no other.

cards.prompt: Hannah bargains, dares, and argues with God, and the Talmud learns its rules of prayer from her. Is there something you would only say to God boldly?

points: Hannah is the first to say **Lord of Hosts** (Berakhot 31b).
She prays **onto** God: boldly, even impertinently.
Zohar: her prayer rose **above fate**.
Asked, then **lent** to GOD (1:27-28).
For **this** boy she prayed (Berakhot 31b).

lessons.title: Hannah (4): My heart exults
lessons.check_note: Megillah 14a and Berakhot 29a read on Sefaria 11/12. CHECK: how Mishkan HaNefesh treats the nine-blessing Musaf (Reform practice may differ).

cards.title: A song
cards.body: Samuel is born, weaned, and brought to serve at the House of GOD. Then Hannah prays again, this time **a song**.

cards.q: The Talmud links the nine blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf Amidah to what?
choices: The nine mentions of God's name in Hannah's prayer
cards.why: Rabbi Yitzchak of Kartignin, in Berakhot 29a.

cards.he:
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל חַנָּה וַתֹּאמַר עָלַץ לִבִּי בַּֽיהֹוָה רָמָה קַרְנִי בַּֽיהֹוָה רָחַב פִּי עַל־אוֹיְבַי כִּי שָׂמַחְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
אֵין־קָדוֹשׁ כַּיהֹוָה כִּי אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ וְאֵין צוּר כֵּאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
cards.en: And Hannah prayed: My heart exults in GOD; I have triumphed through GOD. I gloat over my enemies; I rejoice in Your deliverance. There is no holy one like GOD, Truly, there is none beside You; There is no rock like our God.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vatitpaleil chanah vatomar alatz libi baihovah ramah karni baihovah rachav pi al oyvai ki samachti bishu-atecha.
Ein kadosh kaihovah ki ein biltecha v'ein tzur keiloheinu.

cards.he: רָמָה קַרְנִי בַּֽיהֹוָה
cards.tl: Ramah karni baihovah
cards.gloss: "I have triumphed through GOD" (2:1). The Talmud reads the Hebrew image word by word: my **horn** is exalted.

cards.title: A prophetess
cards.body: The Talmud counts **seven prophetesses**: Sarah, Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, Abigail, Huldah and Esther. Hannah's proof is the **horn**: she said my horn, not my pitcher. David and Solomon were anointed from a horn and their kingship lasted; Saul and Jehu were anointed from a pitcher and theirs did not. Hannah **foresaw** it.

cards.q: Why does Megillah 14a call Hannah a prophetess?
choices: Her "horn" foresaw which anointed kings would last
cards.why: **Horn**, not pitcher: her song looks ahead to David.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Eli misjudged her.

cards.title: No artist like our God
cards.body: On "There is no rock like our God" (2:2), the Talmud reads **rock** as **artist**. A person paints a form on a wall but cannot give it breath. God forms a child **inside its mother** and gives it breath and a soul. Fitting words from Hannah.

cards.he:
יְיָ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה מוֹרִיד שְׁאוֹל וַיָּֽעַל׃
יְיָ מוֹרִישׁ וּמַעֲשִׁיר מַשְׁפִּיל אַף־מְרוֹמֵֽם׃
מֵקִים מֵעָפָר דָּל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב עִם־נְדִיבִים וְכִסֵּא כָבוֹד יַנְחִלֵם כִּי לַֽיהֹוָה מְצֻקֵי אֶרֶץ וַיָּשֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶם תֵּבֵֽל׃
cards.en: GOD deals death and gives life, Casts down into Sheol and raises up. GOD makes poor and makes rich, Casts down, and also lifts high— Raising the poor from the dust, Lifting up the needy from the dunghill, To set them with nobles, Granting them seats of honor. For the pillars of the earth belong to GOD, Who has set the world upon them.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Adonai meimit um'chayeh morid sh'ol vaya-al.
Adonai morish uma-ashir mashpil af m'romeim.
Meikim mei-afar dal mei-ashpot yarim evyon l'hoshiv im n'divim v'chisei chavod yanchileim ki laihovah m'tzukei eretz vayashet aleihem teiveil.

cards.he: יְיָ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה
cards.tl: Adonai meimit um'chayeh
cards.gloss: "GOD deals death and gives life" (2:6).

cards.body: Every Amidah's **G'vurot** praises God in the same words: מֶלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה.

cards.title: Nine blessings
cards.body: **Rabbi Yitzchak of Kartignin**: the nine blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf prayer correspond to the **nine mentions of God's name** in Hannah's prayer. The reason: on Rosh Hashanah, Sarah, Rachel and **Hannah** were remembered.

cards.q: According to Berakhot 29a, why does Hannah's prayer shape the Rosh Hashanah Musaf?
choices: She was remembered on Rosh Hashanah
She prayed in the Temple on Yom Kippur
cards.why: Remembered on Rosh Hashanah, so her prayer gives the day its **nine blessings**.
wrong_why: Not in the Talmud.
Not in the Talmud.

cards.he: מֵקִים מֵעָפָר דָּל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן
cards.tl: Meikim mei-afar dal mei-ashpot yarim evyon
cards.gloss: "Raising the poor from the dust, Lifting up the needy from the dunghill" (2:8). The song turns the world **upside down**, as Hannah's own life was turned.

cards.prompt: Hannah's song is full of reversals: the poor raised, the mighty brought low. Where have you seen a reversal you once could not imagine?

points: "**My heart exults in GOD**" (2:1).
Megillah 14a: Hannah, **a prophetess**: horn, not pitcher.
**No artist** like our God.
"**GOD deals death and gives life**": the G'vurot.
Berakhot 29a: **nine blessings** of Rosh Hashanah Musaf.

units.title: Holiday stories
units.subtitle: The stories behind Shavuot, Hanukkah and Yom Kippur afternoon

lessons.title: Ruth: The stranger who stayed
lessons.check_note: My retelling of Ruth 1-4 and Leviticus 19:9-10; quotes are paraphrased. Check most closely: Ruth Rabbah 2:14 (purpose of the book) and the Shavuot traditions. Does CBB read Ruth on Shavuot?

cards.title: Three widows
cards.body: A famine drives **Elimelech and Naomi** from Bethlehem to **Moab**, an old rival nation. Their sons marry Moabite women, **Orpah and Ruth**. Then all three men die, leaving three widows with no one to support them.

cards.q: Naomi tells both daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' homes. What does Ruth do?
choices: Asks Naomi to stay in Moab
cards.why: Ruth **refuses to leave**. Naomi's people will be her people, and Naomi's God her God.

cards.title: Where you go, I will go
cards.body: Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye. Ruth holds on. Wherever Naomi goes and wherever she sleeps, Ruth will too; **Naomi's people will be her people and Naomi's God her God**, and only death will part them.

cards.he:
וַתֹּאמֶר רוּת אַל־תִּפְגְּעִי־בִי לְעׇזְבֵךְ לָשׁוּב מֵאַחֲרָיִךְ כִּי אֶל־אֲשֶׁר תֵּלְכִי אֵלֵךְ וּבַאֲשֶׁר תָּלִינִי אָלִין עַמֵּךְ עַמִּי וֵאלֹהַיִךְ אֱלֹהָֽי׃
בַּאֲשֶׁר תָּמוּתִי אָמוּת וְשָׁם אֶקָּבֵר כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂה יְיָ לִי וְכֹה יוֹסִיף כִּי הַמָּוֶת יַפְרִיד בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵֽךְ׃
cards.en: But Ruth replied, “Do not urge me to leave you, to turn back and not follow you. For wherever you go, I will go; wherever you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus and more may GOD do to me if anything but death parts me from you.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vatomer Rut al tifg'i vi l'ozveich lashuv mei-acharayich ki el asher teilchi eileich uva-asher talini alin ameich ami veilohayich Elohai.
Ba-asher tamuti amut v'sham ekaveir ko ya-aseh Adonai li v'cho yosif ki hamavet yafrid beini uveineich.

cards.title: Gleaning
cards.body: They reach Bethlehem as the **barley harvest** begins. Ruth goes out to **glean**, picking up the grain the reapers leave behind. The Torah tells farmers to leave the edges of the field and the fallen grain **for the poor and the stranger**. Ruth is both.

cards.q: Why could Ruth gather grain in a field that wasn't hers?
choices: The Torah leaves gleanings for the poor and the stranger
Naomi owned part of the field
cards.why: Leaving gleanings is a **Torah law**: the edges and the fallen grain belong to the poor and the stranger.
wrong_why: Boaz only notices her after she is already gleaning. He never hires her.
Naomi came home with nothing. She had no crop.

cards.title: Boaz
cards.body: The field belongs to **Boaz**, a relative of Elimelech. He has heard how Ruth stood by Naomi. He tells her to stay in his field, orders his workers not to bother her, and has them pull out extra stalks for her to gather.

cards.title: The redeemer
cards.body: Naomi sends Ruth to ask Boaz to be her **go'el**, redeemer: the relative who takes responsibility for a family's land and name. A closer relative turns it down and seals it by handing over his sandal. **Boaz marries Ruth.**

cards.he: כִּי גֹאֵל אָתָּה
cards.tl: Ki go-eil atah
cards.gloss: "For you are a **redeemer**" (3:9). Ruth asks Boaz to step in as **go'el**, the relative who takes responsibility for the family.

cards.q: What was a go'el, a redeemer, in Ruth's world?
choices: A relative who takes responsibility for a family's land and name
cards.why: The go'el is a **relative** who steps in for a family that has lost its men.
wrong_why: Boaz settles it at the town gate in front of elders, but as a relative, not as a judge.
No priest appears anywhere in the book.

cards.title: Great-grandmother of a king
cards.body: Their son is **Obed**, the father of Jesse, the father of **King David**. The book ends with a family tree: Israel's greatest king descends from a woman of Moab.

cards.q: Who is Ruth's great-grandson?
cards.why: Obed, then Jesse, then **David**.
wrong_why: Solomon is David's son, one generation further down.
Samuel anoints David as king but isn't related to Ruth.

cards.title: Hesed
cards.body: A midrash asks why this book was written at all, since it teaches no laws. Its answer: **to teach how great the reward is for hesed**, loyal kindness. Ruth shows it to Naomi, and Boaz to Ruth, each going beyond what was required.

cards.he: הֵיטַבְתְּ חַסְדֵּךְ הָאַחֲרוֹן מִן־הָרִאשׁוֹן
cards.tl: Heitavt chasdeich ha-acharon min harishon
cards.gloss: "Your latest **hesed** is greater than your first" (3:10). Boaz praises Ruth's loyal kindness: first to Naomi, now to the whole family.

cards.q: Put the story in order.
items: Famine and the move to Moab
cards.why: Loss, then loyalty, then kindness answered with kindness, then a royal line.

cards.body: Many congregations read Ruth on **Shavuot**. It is a harvest story for a harvest festival, and Ruth's choice to join the Jewish people is often linked to Israel accepting the Torah at Sinai. A tradition also holds that David was born and died on Shavuot.

cards.prompt: Ruth committed before she knew anything would turn out well. Where in your own Jewish life did you choose first and understand later?

points: Three widows; Ruth **won't leave Naomi**.
She **gleans**, a right the Torah gives the poor and the stranger.
Boaz acts as **go'el** and marries her.
Their great-grandson is **King David**.
The midrash: the book teaches **hesed**.

lessons.title: Hanukkah: The rededication
lessons.check_note: Dates follow the usual scholarly reconstruction from 1 Maccabees. 'Hammer' for Maccabee is the common explanation, not certain. Decide whether the app should mention the classical Reform framing (religious freedom).

cards.title: A story outside the Bible
cards.body: Hanukkah's story **isn't in the Hebrew Bible**. It comes from the **books of Maccabees**, written in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE and left out of the Jewish canon, and from the **Talmud**, centuries later.

src.note: Kept in the Septuagint and Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, not in the Tanakh.

cards.q: What did the first Hanukkah celebrate?
choices: A jar of oil lasting eight days
cards.why: The earliest source celebrates **rededicating the Temple**. The oil story appears centuries later.

cards.body: Judea is ruled by the **Seleucid** Greek kingdom. Many Jews have taken up Greek culture, and Jews argue bitterly among themselves about how far to go.
King **Antiochus IV** bans Shabbat, circumcision and Torah study, and sets up pagan worship in the **Temple in Jerusalem**.

cards.title: Mattathias says no
cards.body: In the village of **Modi'in**, an old priest named **Mattathias** refuses to sacrifice to the king's gods. He and his sons flee to the hills and start a revolt.

cards.q: What started the revolt?
choices: A priest refused to offer a pagan sacrifice
The Temple ran out of oil
cards.why: In Modi'in, **Mattathias refused** to sacrifice to the king's gods.
wrong_why: The oil story is about the end of the war, and it comes from a much later source.
1 Maccabees tells it as a fight over religion, not money.

cards.title: The hammer
cards.body: His son **Judah** leads the fighting and is nicknamed **Maccabee**, usually explained as "the hammer." Against a much larger army, the rebels win back Jerusalem.

src.note: The meaning of Maccabee is uncertain.

cards.body: They purify the Temple, build a new altar and **rededicate** it with eight days of celebration. **Hanukkah** means "dedication."

src.note: 2 Maccabees 10:6 says the eight days were kept like a late Sukkot.

cards.he: חֲנֻכַּת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
cards.tl: Chanukat hamizbeiach
cards.gloss: "The **dedication of the altar**" (Numbers 7:84). The same word names the dedication of the Tabernacle's altar in the Torah. That chapter is the Torah reading during Hanukkah.

cards.q: What does the word Hanukkah mean?
cards.why: It names the **rededication** of the Temple and its altar.
wrong_why: Light is the holiday's symbol, but the word itself means dedication.
The victory made it possible, but the name is about the Temple.

cards.title: The jar of oil
cards.body: Centuries later the **Talmud** asks, "What is Hanukkah?" and tells a new story: one sealed jar of pure oil, enough for one day, **burned for eight**.

cards.q: Where does the story of the oil first appear?
cards.why: The Babylonian **Talmud**, Shabbat 21b.
wrong_why: 1 Maccabees has eight days of celebration but no oil miracle.
Hanukkah happened long after the Torah was written.

cards.title: Not by might
cards.body: The haftarah for Shabbat of Hanukkah answers the war story. The prophet Zechariah sees a golden lampstand and hears: **not by might and not by power, but by My spirit**.

cards.he: וַיַּעַן וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי לֵאמֹר זֶה דְּבַר־יְיָ אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶל לֵאמֹר לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם־בְּרוּחִי אָמַר יְיָ צְבָאֽוֹת׃
cards.en: Then he explained to me as follows: “This is the word of GOD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit—said GOD of Hosts.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vaya-an vayomer eilai leimor zeh d'var Adonai el Z'rubavel leimor lo v'chayil v'lo v'choach ki im b'ruchi amar Adonai tz'va-ot.

cards.q: Put the events in order.
cards.why: Persecution, refusal, revolt, victory, rededication.

cards.body: When you light the candles you hold **both stories**: a stubborn fight for the freedom to live as Jews, and a small light that lasts longer than it should. Different generations have leaned on one or the other.

cards.prompt: Which story speaks to you more right now, the fight or the light? Why?

points: The story comes from **Maccabees** and the **Talmud**, not the Bible.
Antiochus IV **banned Jewish practice**; Mattathias refused.
Judah **the Maccabee** retook Jerusalem.
Hanukkah means **dedication**: the Temple, 25 Kislev.
The **oil** story is from the Talmud; the haftarah says **not by might**.

lessons.title: Jonah: The prophet who ran
lessons.check_note: My retelling of Jonah 1-4; quotes are paraphrased. Confirm that Mishkan HaNefesh and CBB read Jonah on Yom Kippur afternoon.

cards.title: The other direction
cards.body: God tells **Jonah** to go to **Nineveh**, capital of Assyria, Israel's enemy, and call out against its evil. Jonah goes down to **Jaffa** and boards a ship sailing the opposite way, to **Tarshish**.

cards.q: Why did Jonah run, by his own account?
choices: He knew God would forgive Nineveh
He was afraid of being killed
He didn't believe God had spoken
cards.why: He says it himself near the end: he knew God was **gracious and compassionate** and would relent.

cards.title: The storm
cards.body: A great storm hits. The sailors pray, each to his own god, and **cast lots**; the lot falls on Jonah, asleep below deck. He tells them to **throw him overboard**. They try rowing to shore first, then do it, and the sea goes calm.

cards.title: The fish
cards.body: God sends a **great fish** to swallow Jonah. He is inside it for three days and three nights, and **he prays**. Then the fish spits him out onto dry land.

cards.q: How did the sailors find out the storm was about Jonah?
choices: Another prophet on board told them
cards.why: They **cast lots**, and the lot fell on Jonah.
wrong_why: He explains himself only after the lot falls on him.
There is no other prophet in the story.

cards.title: Five words
cards.body: God asks a second time, and Jonah goes. His whole message is **five words in Hebrew**: forty more days, and Nineveh will be overturned.

cards.he: וַיָּחֶל יוֹנָה לָבוֹא בָעִיר מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם אֶחָד וַיִּקְרָא וַיֹּאמַר עוֹד אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְנִֽינְוֵה נֶהְפָּֽכֶת׃
cards.en: Jonah started out and made his way into the city the distance of one day’s walk, and proclaimed: “Forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayachel Yonah lavo va-ir mahalach yom echad vayikra vayomar od arba-im yom v'Nin'veih nehpachet.

cards.title: A city turns
cards.body: The people believe. **Everyone fasts and wears sackcloth**, from the king down, and the king orders even the **animals** to fast. They turn from violence, and God does not destroy the city.

cards.he: כִּי־שָׁבוּ מִדַּרְכָּם הָרָעָה
cards.tl: Ki shavu midarkam hara-ah
cards.gloss: "They **turned** from their evil way" (3:10). **Shavu**, they turned, comes from the same root as **teshuvah**.

cards.q: Who repents in Nineveh?
choices: Only the people who heard Jonah
cards.why: The king's decree covers **people and animals alike**.
wrong_why: The king leads, but his decree covers the whole city.
The people start it, but the king's decree spreads it to everyone, animals included.

cards.title: Jonah's anger
cards.body: Jonah is furious. This is why he ran, he says: he knew God is **gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in kindness**, and would relent. He is quoting the attributes God revealed to Moses.

cards.q: Why does Jonah's complaint sound familiar?
choices: He quotes God's attributes from Exodus 34
cards.why: He turns God's own words to Moses, **gracious and compassionate**, into a complaint.
wrong_why: The sailors' prayer asks not to be blamed for his death; it has different words.
The king hopes God may relent, but Jonah's words come from Exodus.

cards.title: The plant
cards.body: Jonah sits outside the city to see what will happen. God grows a plant to shade him, then sends a worm to kill it. In the hot sun, Jonah says he would rather die.

cards.title: The last question
cards.body: God answers: you care about a plant you didn't plant or grow. **Should I not care about Nineveh**, with more than 120,000 people who can't tell their right hand from their left, and many animals? The book ends there. **Jonah never answers.**

cards.q: Put the story in order.
cards.why: Flight, storm, prayer, warning, repentance, and a question left open.

cards.body: Jonah is read on **Yom Kippur afternoon**. On the day of teshuvah, turning, you hear about a whole city that turned, and a prophet who found God's mercy hard to accept. All day you also sing the same attributes Jonah quotes.

cards.prompt: The book ends with a question nobody answers. How would you answer in Jonah's place?

points: Jonah **runs** from his mission to Nineveh.
Storm, lots, and **three days in the fish**.
**Five words**, and the whole city repents, animals too.
Jonah is angry that God is **gracious and compassionate** (Exodus 34).
The book ends with **God's question**, unanswered.

units.title: Jonah
units.subtitle: The prophet who ran, and the city that turned

lessons.title: Jonah (1): Running away
lessons.check_note: Mekhilta Pischa 1 (Silverstein), Nedarim 38a, Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 10 (Friedlander), Zohar Vayakhel 7:81-83 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12. English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive. Overview lesson: x-st-hol-03.

cards.title: A prophet who says no
cards.body: God tells **Jonah** to go to **Nineveh**, that great city, and proclaim judgment upon it. Jonah gets up, and heads the other way: **down to the sea**.

cards.q: According to one Midrash, why did Jonah run?
choices: He knew Nineveh would repent, and Israel would look worse by comparison
He was afraid the Assyrians would kill him
He did not believe God had really spoken
cards.why: The Mekhilta says Jonah knew that "the gentiles are close to repentance."

cards.he:
וַֽיְהִי דְּבַר־יְיָ אֶל־יוֹנָה בֶן־אֲמִתַּי לֵאמֹֽר׃
קוּם לֵךְ אֶל־נִֽינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה וּקְרָא עָלֶיהָ כִּֽי־עָלְתָה רָעָתָם לְפָנָֽי׃
וַיָּקׇם יוֹנָה לִבְרֹחַ תַּרְשִׁישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵי יְיָ וַיֵּרֶד יָפוֹ וַיִּמְצָא אֳנִיָּה ׀ בָּאָה תַרְשִׁישׁ וַיִּתֵּן שְׂכָרָהּ וַיֵּרֶד בָּהּ לָבוֹא עִמָּהֶם תַּרְשִׁישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָֽה׃
cards.en: The word of GOD came to Jonah son of Amittai: Go at once to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim judgment upon it; for their wickedness has come before Me. Jonah, however, started out to flee to Tarshish from GOD’s service. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare and went aboard to sail with the others to Tarshish, away from GOD’s service.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl:
Vay'hi d'var Adonai el Yonah ven amitai leimor.
Kum leich el ninvei ha-ir hag'dolah uk'ra aleha ki altah ra-atam l'fanai.
Vayakom Yonah livroach tarshishah milifnei Adonai vayeired yafo vayimtza oniyah  ba-ah tarshish vayitein s'charah vayeired bah lavo imahem tarshishah milifnei Adonai.

cards.he: לִבְרֹחַ תַּרְשִׁישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵי יְיָ
cards.tl: Livroach tarshishah milifnei Adonai
cards.gloss: "started out to flee to Tarshish from GOD’s service" (1:3). The Midrash asks whether anyone can flee from God at all, and answers with Psalm 139: wherever you go, God is there.

cards.title: Why he ran
cards.body: The **Mekhilta** says Jonah meant to leave the Land of Israel, where, in its view, the Divine Presence reveals itself. His reason: "the gentiles are close to repentance." If Nineveh turned at once, Israel, which had not turned, would look guilty by comparison. God's answer: **I have many messengers like you**, and God sends the wind.

cards.q: In the Mekhilta, why did Jonah flee?
choices: He was protecting Israel: Nineveh would repent quickly and make Israel look worse
He was afraid of the sailors
He wanted to be a merchant
cards.why: Jonah ran **for Israel's sake**, not out of fear for himself.
wrong_why: The sailors come later, and the Midrash's reason is Israel.
Not in the Midrash.

cards.title: Paid in full
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan**: "He paid the cost of the entire ship." **Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer** adds that the ship was two days away, and God sent a storm to bring it back to Jaffa, **to test Jonah**. Jonah took it as a sign his escape would succeed, and in his joy he paid his fare in advance.

cards.he:
וַיִּֽירְאוּ הַמַּלָּחִים וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ אִישׁ אֶל־אֱלֹהָיו וַיָּטִלוּ אֶת־הַכֵּלִים אֲשֶׁר בָּֽאֳנִיָּה אֶל־הַיָּם לְהָקֵל מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם וְיוֹנָה יָרַד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה וַיִּשְׁכַּב וַיֵּרָדַֽם׃
וַיִּקְרַב אֵלָיו רַב הַחֹבֵל וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ מַה־לְּךָ נִרְדָּם קוּם קְרָא אֶל־אֱלֹהֶיךָ אוּלַי יִתְעַשֵּׁת הָאֱלֹהִים לָנוּ וְלֹא נֹאבֵֽד׃
cards.en: In their fright, the sailors cried out, each to his own god; and they flung the ship’s cargo overboard to make it lighter for them. Jonah, meanwhile, had gone down into the hold of the vessel where he lay down and fell asleep. The captain went over to him and cried out, “How can you be sleeping so soundly! Up, call upon your god! Perhaps the god will be kind to us and we will not perish.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl:
Vayir'u hamalachim vayiz'aku ish el Elohav vayatilu et hakeilim asher ba-oniyah el hayam l'hakeil mei-aleihem v'yonah yarad el yark'tei has'finah vayishkav vayeiradam.
Vayikrav eilav rav hachoveil vayomer lo ma l'cha nirdam kum k'ra el Elohecha ulai yit'asheit ha-Elohim lanu v'lo noveid.

cards.he: וְיוֹנָה יָרַד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה וַיִּשְׁכַּב וַיֵּרָדַֽם׃
cards.tl: V'yonah yarad el yark'tei has'finah vayishkav vayeiradam.
cards.gloss: "Jonah, meanwhile, had gone down into the hold of the vessel where he lay down and fell asleep" (1:5). Down to Jaffa, down into the ship, down into the hold: the verb **went down**, יָרַד, keeps returning (1:3, 1:5).

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם עִבְרִי אָנֹכִי וְאֶת־יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם אֲנִי יָרֵא אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה אֶת־הַיָּם וְאֶת־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃
cards.en: “I am a Hebrew,” he replied. “I worship the ETERNAL, the God of Heaven, who made both sea and land.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayomer aleihem ivri anochi v'et Adonai Elohei hashamayim ani yarei asher asah et hayam v'et hayabashah.

cards.title: A soul on a ship
cards.body: The **Zohar** reads the story as "the whole of a man’s career in this world." Jonah going down into the ship is **the soul coming down into a body**. The storm is the judgment that follows a person, and the captain who wakes Jonah is the good inner voice: it is no time to sleep, **return to your Master**.

cards.q: In the Zohar's reading, what does Jonah going down into the ship stand for?
choices: The soul coming down into a body in this world
cards.why: The ship is life in this world, and Jonah is **the soul** in it.
wrong_why: Not the Zohar's reading here.
Not the Zohar's reading here.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם שָׂאוּנִי וַהֲטִילֻנִי אֶל־הַיָּם וְיִשְׁתֹּק הַיָּם מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶם כִּי יוֹדֵעַ אָנִי כִּי בְשֶׁלִּי הַסַּעַר הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
cards.en: He answered, “Heave me overboard, and the sea will calm down for you; for I know that this terrible storm came upon you on my account.”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayomer aleihem sa-uni vahatiluni el hayam v'yishtok hayam mei-aleichem ki yodeia ani ki v'sheli hasa-ar hagadol hazeh aleichem.

cards.title: Ready to give his life
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan** (in the Mekhilta): Jonah boarded the ship **only to cast himself into the sea**. Moses offered his life for Israel ("blot me out of Your book"), and so did David. Jonah, too, gave his life for his people.

cards.prompt: Jonah runs, sleeps through the storm, and then offers his own life for the sailors. Is there something you know is yours to do that you have been sailing away from?

points: Jonah flees **toward Tarshish** (1:3).
Mekhilta: he ran **for Israel's sake**, knowing Nineveh would repent.
**Down**, down, down: Jaffa, the ship, the hold.
Zohar: Jonah is **the soul** on the ship of this world.
"**Heave me overboard**": ready to give his life.

lessons.title: Jonah (2): Inside the fish
lessons.check_note: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 10 (Friedlander) and Zohar Vayakhel 7:88-92 (Soncino) read on Sefaria 11/12. G'vurot wording from data/prayers.json.

cards.title: Three days down
cards.body: The sailors throw Jonah into the sea, and the storm stops. Jonah sinks, and is **swallowed**.

cards.q: The book of Jonah says Jonah was swallowed by a whale.
cards.why: The text says **a huge fish**, דָּג גָּדוֹל. No species is named.

cards.he:
וַיְמַן יְיָ דָּג גָּדוֹל לִבְלֹעַ אֶת־יוֹנָה וַיְהִי יוֹנָה בִּמְעֵי הַדָּג שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לֵילֽוֹת׃
וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל יוֹנָה אֶל־יְיָ אֱלֹהָיו מִמְּעֵי הַדָּגָֽה׃
cards.en: GOD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah; and Jonah remained in the fish’s belly three days and three nights. Jonah prayed to the ETERNAL his God from the belly of the fish.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl:
Vayman Adonai dag gadol livloa et Yonah vay'hi Yonah bim'ei hadag sh'loshah yamim ush'loshah leilot.
Vayitpaleil Yonah el Adonai Elohav mim'ei hadagah.

cards.he: דָּג גָּדוֹל
cards.tl: Dag gadol
cards.gloss: "a huge fish" (2:1). Notice who **provided** it: GOD.

cards.title: Prepared from Creation
cards.body: **Rabbi Tarfon**: this fish was appointed **from the six days of Creation** to swallow Jonah. He entered its mouth as a person enters a great synagogue, and its two eyes were "like windows of glass giving light to Jonah." **Rabbi Meir**: a pearl hung inside the fish, shining like the noon sun, and showed him **everything in the sea**.

cards.q: In Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer, when was Jonah's fish appointed?
choices: During the six days of Creation
On the morning of the storm
cards.why: The rescue was **prepared before the running began**.
wrong_why: Earlier: Rabbi Tarfon says from Creation.
Earlier: Rabbi Tarfon says from Creation.

cards.title: Under the Temple
cards.body: In the same Midrash, the fish shows Jonah the path Israel took **through the Reed Sea**, the pillars of the earth, and at last the **Foundation Stone beneath the Temple**. There the sons of Korah stand praying. They tell him: you are standing beneath God's Temple; pray, and you will be answered. So Jonah asks the fish to stop, and **begins to pray**.

cards.he: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל יוֹנָה אֶל־יְיָ אֱלֹהָיו מִמְּעֵי הַדָּגָֽה׃
cards.tl: Vayitpaleil Yonah el Adonai Elohav mim'ei hadagah.
cards.gloss: "Jonah prayed to the ETERNAL his God from the belly of the fish" (2:2). On the ship, the sailors cried out and Jonah slept (1:5-6). Now **Jonah prays**.

cards.q: In Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer, why is Jonah told to pray where he is?
choices: He is beneath the Temple, where prayer is answered
The fish is about to die
cards.why: Even at the bottom of the sea, Jonah is **beneath the Temple**.
wrong_why: Not the Midrash's reason.
The sailors are back on the ship.

cards.body: In this Midrash Jonah prays to God as the One who kills and the One who makes alive. Every Amidah praises God in the same way in the **G'vurot**: מֶלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה.

cards.title: The fish is the grave
cards.body: The **Zohar** continues its reading: the fish that swallowed Jonah **is the grave**, and its belly is the belly of Sheol, the underworld (2:3). The three days and nights are a person's first days in the grave. When God speaks to the fish and it **spews Jonah out upon dry land**, the Zohar reads it as the day God will **awaken the dead**.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ לַדָּג וַיָּקֵא אֶת־יוֹנָה אֶל־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃
cards.en: GOD commanded the fish, and it spewed Jonah out upon dry land.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayomer Adonai ladag vayakei et Yonah el hayabashah.

cards.prompt: Jonah prays only after he has gone as far down as anyone can go. What has a low place taught you about prayer?

points: God **provided a huge fish** (2:1).
Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer: prepared **from Creation**, lit by **a pearl**.
Beneath **the Temple**, Jonah prays.
G'vurot: God who **kills and gives life**.
Zohar: the fish is **the grave**, dry land is **life again**.

lessons.title: Jonah (3): What God saw
lessons.check_note: Taanit 16a, Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:1 (Guggenheimer), Megillah 31a read on Sefaria 11/12. Reform Yom Kippur afternoon practice: see x-st-hol-03 note.

cards.title: Sackcloth, and something more
cards.body: Jonah's five words reach the king. He leaves his throne, puts on **sackcloth**, and decrees a fast for every person and every animal in Nineveh.

cards.q: On a public fast day, what does the Talmud say an elder reminds the people about Nineveh?
choices: God saw their deeds, not their sackcloth and fasting
cards.why: The verse says God saw **what they did** (3:10).

cards.he: וְיִתְכַּסּוּ שַׂקִּים הָֽאָדָם וְהַבְּהֵמָה וְיִקְרְאוּ אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּחׇזְקָה וְיָשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ מִדַּרְכּוֹ הָֽרָעָה וּמִן־הֶחָמָס אֲשֶׁר בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃
cards.en: They shall be covered with sackcloth—human and animal—and shall cry mightily to God. Let everyone turn back from their own evil ways and from the injustice of which they are guilty.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: V'yitkasu sakim ha-adam v'hab'heimah v'yikr'u el Elohim b'chozkah v'yashuvu ish midarko hara-ah umin hechamas asher b'chapeihem.

cards.he: וּמִן־הֶחָמָס אֲשֶׁר בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃
cards.tl: Umin hechamas asher b'chapeihem.
cards.gloss: "from the injustice of which they are guilty" (3:8). The king names not only evil ways but the injustice in their own hands.

cards.title: Tear down the building
cards.body: **Shmuel**: the king of Nineveh proclaimed that even someone who **stole a beam** and built it into a house must **tear down the whole building** and return the beam. The Talmud notes that the Sages require only money in such a case; Nineveh went further, to remove every trace of what was stolen.

cards.q: In Taanit 16a, what did Nineveh's king require of someone who had built a stolen beam into a house?
choices: Tear the building down and return the beam
Pay a fine to the king
cards.why: Repair, not just regret: **give back what you took**.
wrong_why: Shmuel says they went further than money.
Not in Shmuel's teaching.

cards.he: וַיַּרְא הָֽאֱלֹהִים אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כִּי־שָׁבוּ מִדַּרְכָּם הָרָעָה וַיִּנָּחֶם הָאֱלֹהִים עַל־הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּר לַעֲשׂוֹת־לָהֶם וְלֹא עָשָֽׂה׃
cards.en: God saw what they did, how they were turning back from their evil ways. And God renounced the punishment that had been planned for them, and did not carry it out.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayar ha-Elohim et ma-aseihem ki shavu midarkam hara-ah vayinachem ha-Elohim al hara-ah asher diber la-asot lahem v'lo asah.

cards.title: Deeds, not sackcloth
cards.body: On a public fast, the Talmud has an elder say: "it is not sackcloth and fasting that cause atonement for our sins." **Repentance and good deeds** do. The verse does not say God saw their sackcloth and their fasting; it says **God saw what they did**.

cards.q: According to Taanit 16a, what brings atonement?
cards.why: God saw **their deeds** (3:10).
wrong_why: The elder says these are not what atones.
A sign of mourning, not what atones.

cards.title: Was it real?
cards.body: The two Talmuds read Nineveh differently. In the Babylonian Talmud, the people separate the animals from their young and plead: even if we are not worthy, **these animals have not sinned**. In the Jerusalem Talmud, **Resh Lakish** says "the people of Nineveh repented in trickery": the separated animals were crying so God would give in. **Rabbi Yochanan** adds that they returned what was in their hands, **but not what was locked in their chests**.

cards.q: How does Resh Lakish judge Nineveh's repentance in the Jerusalem Talmud?
choices: As partly a trick, to pressure God
cards.why: Even a famous repentance can be **only partly honest**. The Babylonian Talmud reads the same scene as a sincere plea.
wrong_why: The Babylonian Talmud is kinder; Resh Lakish is not.
He agrees they did something; he doubts their motive.

cards.title: Why on Yom Kippur
cards.body: The Talmud says Jonah is read on **Yom Kippur afternoon**, as the haftarah, the book "which mentions the repentance of the people of Nineveh."

cards.prompt: The Talmud says God looked past the sackcloth to the deeds, and one rabbi still doubts what was hidden in the chests. What would a change in your deeds, not only your words, look like this year?

points: **Turn back** from evil ways and **injustice** (3:8).
Shmuel: return even **a beam in the wall**.
Taanit 16a: **deeds**, not sackcloth, bring atonement.
Resh Lakish: Nineveh's repentance was **partly a trick**.
Jonah is read on **Yom Kippur afternoon** (Megillah 31a).

lessons.title: Jonah (4): The plant and the question
lessons.check_note: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta Pischa 1 read on Sefaria 11/12. Word comparison Exodus 34:6 vs Jonah 4:2 checked by script on the Masorah text.

cards.title: Angry enough to die
cards.body: Nineveh is spared. Jonah, who saved a ship of strangers with his own life, is **furious**, and asks God to take his life.

cards.q: When Jonah quotes God's attributes from Exodus 34, he quotes them word for word.
cards.why: He drops **faithfulness** and adds **renouncing punishment**, the very thing he is angry about.

cards.he: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל אֶל־יְיָ וַיֹּאמַר אָנָּה יְיָ הֲלוֹא־זֶה דְבָרִי עַד־הֱיוֹתִי עַל־אַדְמָתִי עַל־כֵּן קִדַּמְתִּי לִבְרֹחַ תַּרְשִׁישָׁה כִּי יָדַעְתִּי כִּי אַתָּה אֵֽל־חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד וְנִחָם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃
cards.en: He prayed to GOD, saying, “O ETERNAL One! Isn’t this just what I said when I was still in my own country? That is why I fled beforehand to Tarshish. For I know that You are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in kindness, renouncing punishment.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl: Vayitpaleil el Adonai vayomar anah Adonai halo zeh d'vari ad heyoti al admati al kein kidamti livroach tarshishah ki yadati ki atah eil chanun v'rachum erech apayim v'rav chesed v'nicham al hara-ah.

cards.he: אֵֽל־חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד וְנִחָם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃
cards.tl: Eil chanun v'rachum erech apayim v'rav chesed v'nicham al hara-ah.
cards.gloss: "a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in kindness, renouncing punishment" (4:2).

cards.title: Words from Sinai, changed
cards.body: At Sinai God proclaimed: "a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6). In Hebrew, Jonah's list **stops before faithfulness**, וֶאֱמֶת, and ends instead with **renouncing punishment**. He even reverses the first pair: Exodus has רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן; Jonah has חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם.

cards.q: Which attribute from Exodus 34:6 is missing from Jonah's list?
cards.why: Jonah keeps the mercy and leaves out **faithfulness**.
wrong_why: Kindness is there: וְרַב־חֶסֶד.
Slow to anger is there.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר יְיָ אַתָּה חַסְתָּ עַל־הַקִּיקָיוֹן אֲשֶׁר לֹא־עָמַלְתָּ בּוֹ וְלֹא גִדַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁבִּן־לַיְלָה הָיָה וּבִן־לַיְלָה אָבָֽד׃
וַֽאֲנִי לֹא אָחוּס עַל־נִינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה אֲשֶׁר יֶשׁ־בָּהּ הַרְבֵּה מִֽשְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵה רִבּוֹ אָדָם אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־יָדַע בֵּין־יְמִינוֹ לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ וּבְהֵמָה רַבָּֽה׃
cards.en: Then GOD said: “You cared about the plant, which you did not work for and which you did not grow, which appeared overnight and perished overnight. And should not I care about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not yet know their right hand from their left, and many animals as well!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.license: CC-BY-NC (Sefaria lists 'unknown' for Jonah; same edition as Ruth and Zechariah)
cards.tl:
Vayomer Adonai atah chasta al hakikayon asher lo amalta bo v'lo gidalto shebin laylah hayah uvin laylah avad.
Va-ani lo achus al ninvei ha-ir hag'dolah asher yesh bah harbei mishteim esrei ribo adam asher lo yada bein y'mino lismolo uv'heimah rabah.

cards.he: וַֽאֲנִי לֹא אָחוּס עַל־נִינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה
cards.tl: Va-ani lo achus al ninvei ha-ir hag'dolah
cards.gloss: "And should not I care about Nineveh, that great city" (4:11). The book ends on God's question.

cards.title: The king was Pharaoh
cards.body: **Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer** opens with "Know thou the power of repentance." Its example: **Pharaoh**, who defied God by asking who the Lord was, and at the Sea turned with the words of **Mi Chamocha**. God saved him, and he went on to **rule in Nineveh**. When Jonah came, he rose from his throne and put on sackcloth. Infants cried for their mothers, and by the merit of **4,123 children**, more than twelve hundred thousand people were saved (4:11).

cards.q: In Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer 43, who was the king of Nineveh?
choices: Pharaoh, who had turned at the Sea
cards.why: The king who once defied God became the king who led a city in repentance.
wrong_why: Not in the Midrash.
Ahasuerus is the king of the Esther story.

cards.title: The son and the Father
cards.body: The **Mekhilta**: "Jonah claimed the honor of the son, but not the honor of the Father." He defended Israel's honor, but not God's. So, it says, God spoke to Jonah a second time, **but not a third**.

cards.title: A question, not a command
cards.body: God does not force Jonah. God teaches with **a plant, a worm and a question**, and the book stops before Jonah answers. This fits your rabbi's teaching of a people **growing up**: God present less as a hand that compels and more in the choices we make. The answer to God's question is left to the reader.

src.ref: Jonah 4:6-11; teaching from Jamie's rabbi (oral, as Jamie retold it)
src.note: connection is mine; check with Jamie

cards.prompt: Jonah wanted justice for Nineveh; God asked him to care. Who is it hardest for you to wish well?

points: Jonah quotes Sinai, but **drops faithfulness** (4:2).
"**Should not I care** about Nineveh?" (4:11).
Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer: the king was **Pharaoh**, saved by **the children**.
Mekhilta: the honor of **the son**, not **the Father**.
A question, not a command: **the reader answers**.

units.title: Ruth
units.subtitle: The scroll of chesed: choosing, sheltering, and a God found in human kindness

lessons.title: Ruth (1): Your people, my people
lessons.check_note: Yevamot 47b and Berakhot 7b read on Sefaria 11/11. English: JPS Tanakh gender-sensitive.

cards.title: Three widows on the road
cards.body: In Moab, **Naomi** has lost her husband and both sons. She hears that Adonai "had taken note of the people" back home, and sets out with her two Moabite daughters-in-law, **Orpah and Ruth** (1:1-6).

cards.q: What happens when Naomi tells Ruth to go back to her own people?
choices: Ruth refuses and binds herself to Naomi
cards.why: Orpah kisses her goodbye; **Ruth clings to her** and refuses to leave (1:14-17).

cards.he:
וַתֹּאמֶר רוּת אַל־תִּפְגְּעִי־בִי לְעׇזְבֵךְ לָשׁוּב מֵאַחֲרָיִךְ כִּי אֶל־אֲשֶׁר תֵּלְכִי אֵלֵךְ וּבַאֲשֶׁר תָּלִינִי אָלִין עַמֵּךְ עַמִּי וֵאלֹהַיִךְ אֱלֹהָי
בַּאֲשֶׁר תָּמוּתִי אָמוּת וְשָׁם אֶקָּבֵר כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂה יְיָ לִי וְכֹה יוֹסִיף כִּי הַמָּוֶת יַפְרִיד בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵךְ
וַתֵּרֶא כִּי־מִתְאַמֶּצֶת הִיא לָלֶכֶת אִתָּהּ וַתֶּחְדַּל לְדַבֵּר אֵלֶיהָ
cards.en: But Ruth replied, “Do not urge me to leave you, to turn back and not follow you. For wherever you go, I will go; wherever you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus and more may GOD do to me if anything but death parts me from you.” When [Naomi] saw how determined she was to go with her, she ceased to argue with her;
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vatomer Rut al tifg'i vi l'ozveich lashuv mei-acharayich ki el asher teilchi eileich uva-asher talini alin ameich ami veilohayich Elohai
Ba-asher tamuti amut v'sham ekaveir ko ya-aseh Adonai li v'cho yosif ki hamavet yafrid beini uveineich
Vateire ki mit'ametzet hi lalechet itah vatechdal l'dabeir eileha

cards.he: עַמֵּךְ עַמִּי וֵאלֹהַיִךְ אֱלֹהָי
cards.tl: Ameich ami veilohayich Elohai
cards.gloss: "your people shall be my people, and your God my God" (1:16): four Hebrew words that change the history of Israel.

cards.title: When Naomi stopped arguing
cards.body: "When [Naomi] saw how determined she was to go with her, she ceased to argue with her" (1:18). **Rabbi Elazar** learns from this how to receive someone who wants to become a Jew: you may test their resolve, but once it is clear, **you stop arguing**.

cards.q: What does the Talmud learn from Naomi falling silent (1:18)?
choices: Once a person's resolve to join is clear, you stop dissuading them
Naomi didn't want Ruth to come
cards.why: Ruth becomes **the model** for choosing to join the Jewish people.
wrong_why: Naomi did test her first; the point is when to stop.
The verse says Naomi saw her determination.

cards.title: What's in the name Ruth?
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan**: she was called Rut because from her came **David**, who **saturated** (riva) the Holy One with songs and praises.

cards.he:
וַתֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶן אַל־תִּקְרֶאנָה לִי נׇעֳמִי קְרֶאןָ לִי מָרָא כִּי־הֵמַר שַׁדַּי לִי מְאֹד
אֲנִי מְלֵאָה הָלַכְתִּי וְרֵיקָם הֱשִׁיבַנִי יְיָ לָמָּה תִקְרֶאנָה לִי נׇעֳמִי וַיהֹוָה עָנָה בִי וְשַׁדַּי הֵרַע לִי
cards.en: “Do not call me Naomi,” she replied. “Call me Mara, for Shaddai has made my lot very bitter. I went away full, and GOD has brought me back empty. How can you call me Naomi, when GOD has dealt harshly with me, when Shaddai has brought misfortune upon me!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vatomer aleihen al tikrenah li no-omi k'rena li mara ki heimar shadai li m'od
Ani m'lei-ah halachti v'reikam heshivani Adonai lamah tikrenah li no-omi vaihovah anah vi v'shadai heira li

cards.he: קְרֶאןָ לִי מָרָא
cards.tl: K'rena li mara
cards.gloss: "Call me Mara" (1:20), bitterness. Naomi says it plainly: "I went away full, and Adonai has brought me back empty." The book lets her say it.

cards.q: What name does Naomi ask to be called?
cards.why: **Mara**: "for Shaddai has made my lot very bitter" (1:20).
wrong_why: Ruth is her daughter-in-law.
Orpah went back to Moab.

cards.prompt: In the same scene, Ruth binds herself to a people and a God before anything has gone well, and Naomi names her bitterness out loud. Which voice do you recognize today?

points: "**Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.**"
Yevamot 47b: when resolve is clear, **stop arguing**.
Berakhot 7b: Ruth, ancestor of David who **saturated God with song**.
Naomi: "**Call me Mara.**"

lessons.title: Ruth (2): Under whose wings
lessons.check_note: Mishnah Berakhot 9:5 read on Sefaria 11/11. The kanaf link between 2:12 and 3:9 is in the Hebrew text itself.

cards.title: A field of strangers
cards.body: Ruth goes out to **glean** behind the reapers, and happens to come to the field of **Boaz**, a relative of Naomi's husband (2:1-3).

cards.q: The Mishnah learns from Boaz to greet people with God's name.
cards.why: **Mishnah Berakhot 9:5**, from Boaz's "Adonai be with you!" (2:4).

cards.he: וְהִנֵּה־בֹעַז בָּא מִבֵּית לֶחֶם וַיֹּאמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִים יְיָ עִמָּכֶם וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ יְבָרֶכְךָ יְיָ
cards.en: Presently Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. He greeted the reapers, “GOD be with you!” And they responded, “GOD bless you!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'hinei vo-az ba mibeit lechem vayomer lakotzrim Adonai imachem vayomru lo y'varech'cha Adonai

cards.title: A blessing for hello
cards.body: Boaz greets his workers, "Adonai be with you!" and they answer, "Adonai bless you!" The **Mishnah**: from this the Sages instituted that people **greet one another using God's name**.

cards.he: יְשַׁלֵּם יְיָ פׇּעֳלֵךְ וּתְהִי מַשְׂכֻּרְתֵּךְ שְׁלֵמָה מֵעִם יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר־בָּאת לַחֲסוֹת תַּחַת־כְּנָפָיו
cards.en: May GOD reward your deeds. May you have a full recompense from the ETERNAL, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have sought refuge!”
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Y'shaleim Adonai po-oleich ut'hi maskurteich sh'leimah mei-im Adonai Elohei Yisrael asher bat lachasot tachat k'nafav

cards.he: תַּחַת־כְּנָפָיו
cards.tl: Tachat k'nafav
cards.gloss: "under whose wings you have sought refuge" (2:12). Boaz prays that **God** will shelter Ruth, the stranger in his field.

cards.he:
וַיֹּאמֶר מִי־אָתְּ וַתֹּאמֶר אָנֹכִי רוּת אֲמָתֶךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ כְנָפֶךָ עַל־אֲמָתְךָ כִּי גֹאֵל אָתָּה
וַיֹּאמֶר בְּרוּכָה אַתְּ לַיהֹוָה בִּתִּי הֵיטַבְתְּ חַסְדֵּךְ הָאַחֲרוֹן מִן־הָרִאשׁוֹן לְבִלְתִּי־לֶכֶת אַחֲרֵי הַבַּחוּרִים אִם־דַּל וְאִם־עָשִׁיר
cards.en: “Who are you?” he asked. And she replied, “I am your handmaid Ruth. Spread your robe over your handmaid, for you are a redeeming kinsman.” He exclaimed, “Be blessed of GOD, daughter! Your latest deed of loyalty is greater than the first, in that you have not turned to younger men, whether poor or rich.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl:
Vayomer mi at vatomer anochi Rut amatecha ufarasta ch'nafecha al amatcha ki go-eil atah
Vayomer b'ruchah at laihovah biti heitavt chasdeich ha-acharon min harishon l'vilti lechet acharei habachurim im dal v'im ashir

cards.he: וּפָרַשְׂתָּ כְנָפֶךָ עַל־אֲמָתְךָ
cards.tl: Ufarasta ch'nafecha al amatcha
cards.gloss: "Spread your robe over your handmaid" (3:9). In Hebrew, "robe" here is **kanaf**, the very word for God's **wings** in 2:12. Boaz prayed for God to shelter Ruth; now Ruth asks **Boaz** to be that shelter.

cards.q: What links Boaz's blessing (2:12) to Ruth's request (3:9)?
choices: The same Hebrew word, kanaf: wings, or the corner of a robe
Both happen at the city gate
cards.why: God's **wings** and Boaz's **robe** are one word. Boaz becomes **the answer to his own prayer**.
wrong_why: Naomi isn't named in either verse.
2:12 is in the field and 3:9 at the threshing floor.

cards.he: הֵיטַבְתְּ חַסְדֵּךְ הָאַחֲרוֹן מִן־הָרִאשׁוֹן
cards.tl: Heitavt chasdeich ha-acharon min harishon
cards.gloss: "Your latest deed of loyalty is greater than the first" (3:10). The Hebrew word for loyalty is **chesed**.

cards.prompt: Boaz becomes the answer to his own prayer. Is there a prayer of yours that you could help answer?

points: Boaz's "Adonai be with you": greeting with God's name (Mishnah Berakhot 9:5).
"**Under whose wings** you have sought refuge."
"**Spread your robe**": the same word, kanaf.
Boaz becomes **the answer to his own prayer**.
**Chesed**, loyalty, greater the second time.

lessons.title: Ruth (3): The night at the threshing floor
lessons.check_note: Sanhedrin 19b read on Sefaria 11/11. Eshet chayil: Ruth 3:11 and Proverbs 31:10.

cards.title: Naomi's plan
cards.body: Naomi, who once said she came back empty, now makes a plan: "Daughter, I must seek a home for you, where you may be happy" (3:1). She sends Ruth to the threshing floor, at night, to Boaz (3:1-4).

cards.q: Boaz calls Ruth an eshet chayil, the phrase that opens the poem in Proverbs 31.
cards.why: **Eshet chayil** (3:11), the same words as Proverbs 31:10.

cards.he: וַתֹּאמֶר לָהּ נׇעֳמִי חֲמוֹתָהּ בִּתִּי הֲלֹא אֲבַקֶּשׁ־לָךְ מָנוֹחַ אֲשֶׁר יִיטַב־לָךְ
cards.en: Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, “Daughter, I must seek a home for you, where you may be happy.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vatomer lah no-omi chamotah biti halo avakesh lach manoach asher yitav lach

cards.he: וַיְהִי בַּחֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה וַיֶּחֱרַד הָאִישׁ וַיִּלָּפֵת וְהִנֵּה אִשָּׁה שֹׁכֶבֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָיו
cards.en: In the middle of the night, the man gave a start and pulled back—there was a woman lying at his feet!
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vay'hi bachatzi halaylah vayecherad ha-ish vayilafeit v'hinei ishah shochevet marg'lotav

cards.title: Stronger than Joseph
cards.body: At midnight Boaz wakes to find a woman at his feet, and he acts with complete honor. **Rabbi Yochanan**: what Joseph is praised for, resisting temptation, was for Boaz **a small thing**, his humility. (And Palti son of Laish, he adds, was greater still.)

cards.q: How does Rabbi Yochanan compare Boaz to Joseph?
choices: What was Joseph's great strength was a small thing for Boaz
They never faced the same test
cards.why: Joseph's **power** is Boaz's **humility**: the same restraint, held more lightly.
wrong_why: He says the opposite.
He compares them precisely because they did.

cards.he: וְעַתָּה בִּתִּי אַל־תִּירְאִי כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמְרִי אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּךְ כִּי יוֹדֵעַ כׇּל־שַׁעַר עַמִּי כִּי אֵשֶׁת חַיִל אָתְּ
cards.en: And now, daughter, have no fear. I will do in your behalf whatever you ask, for all the elders of my town know what a fine woman you are.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'atah biti al tir'i kol asher tomri e-eseh lach ki yodeia kol sha-ar ami ki eishet chayil at

cards.he: אֵשֶׁת חַיִל אָתְּ
cards.tl: Eishet chayil at
cards.gloss: "what a fine woman you are" (3:11). The Hebrew is **eshet chayil**, the words that open the poem of Proverbs 31 (31:10), which many families sing at the Friday night table.

cards.q: What Hebrew phrase does Boaz use for Ruth in 3:11?
cards.why: **Eshet chayil**, a woman of valor.
wrong_why: Go'el, redeemer, is Boaz's role.
That's the unnamed relative in chapter 4.

points: Naomi: "**I must seek a home for you.**"
Midnight at the threshing floor: Boaz acts with honor.
Sanhedrin 19b: Joseph's strength was **Boaz's humility**.
Ruth, an **eshet chayil**.

lessons.title: Ruth (4): At the city gate
lessons.check_note: Ruth Rabbah 7:7 read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: So-and-so
cards.body: Boaz goes to the town gate, where business was done in public, and calls over the relative who has the first right to redeem: "Come over and sit down here, **So-and-so**!" (4:1). The book never gives his name.

cards.q: What is the closer redeemer's name in the Book of Ruth?
choices: He has none: he is only "So-and-so"
cards.why: **Peloni almoni**, So-and-so (4:1).

cards.he: וּבֹעַז עָלָה הַשַּׁעַר וַיֵּשֶׁב שָׁם וְהִנֵּה הַגֹּאֵל עֹבֵר אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר־בֹּעַז וַיֹּאמֶר סוּרָה שְׁבָה־פֹּה פְּלֹנִי אַלְמֹנִי וַיָּסַר וַיֵּשֵׁב
cards.en: Meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the gate and sat down there. And now the redeemer whom Boaz had mentioned passed by. He called, “Come over and sit down here, So-and-so!” And he came over and sat down.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Uvo-az alah hasha-ar vayeishev sham v'hinei hago-eil oveir asher diber bo-az vayomer surah sh'vah po p'loni almoni vayasar vayeisheiv

cards.title: The man with no name
cards.body: Why no name? In the midrash, **Rabbi Yehoshua** says Peloni Almoni really was his name. **Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman**: he was **mute from matters of Torah**. Afraid that marrying Ruth had doomed Naomi's sons, he refused her.

cards.q: What does Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman say about the unnamed redeemer?
choices: He was mute from matters of Torah, and refused Ruth out of fear
He was a stranger to Bethlehem
cards.why: **Mute in matters of Torah**: afraid of what happened to Naomi's sons, he walked away from Ruth.
wrong_why: He was a relative of Elimelech.
The midrash doesn't say that.

cards.he: וְזֹאת לְפָנִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־הַגְּאֻלָּה וְעַל־הַתְּמוּרָה לְקַיֵּם כׇּל־דָּבָר שָׁלַף אִישׁ נַעֲלוֹ וְנָתַן לְרֵעֵהוּ וְזֹאת הַתְּעוּדָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
cards.en: Now this was formerly done in Israel in cases of redemption or exchange: to validate any transaction, one party would take off a sandal and hand it to the other. Such was the practice in Israel.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: V'zot l'fanim b'Yisrael al hag'ulah v'al hat'murah l'kayeim kol davar shalaf ish na-alo v'natan l'rei-eihu v'zot hat'udah b'Yisrael

cards.title: The sandal
cards.body: To seal the deal, one man **takes off a sandal** and hands it to the other (4:7-8). The book stops to explain the custom, as if writing for readers who had forgotten it.

cards.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ כׇּל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־בַּשַּׁעַר וְהַזְּקֵנִים עֵדִים יִתֵּן יְיָ אֶת־הָאִשָּׁה הַבָּאָה אֶל־בֵּיתֶךָ כְּרָחֵל וּכְלֵאָה אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶם אֶת־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל וַעֲשֵׂה־חַיִל בְּאֶפְרָתָה וּקְרָא־שֵׁם בְּבֵית לָחֶם
cards.en: All the people at the gate and the elders answered, “We are. May GOD make the woman who is coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, both of whom built up the House of Israel! Prosper in Ephrathah and perpetuate your name in Bethlehem!
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vayomru kol ha-am asher basha-ar v'haz'keinim eidim yitein Adonai et ha-ishah haba-ah el beitecha k'racheil uch'lei-ah asher banu sh'teihem et beit Yisrael va-asei chayil b'efratah uk'ra sheim b'veit lachem

cards.he: כְּרָחֵל וּכְלֵאָה אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶם אֶת־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
cards.tl: K'racheil uch'lei-ah asher banu sh'teihem et beit Yisrael
cards.gloss: "like Rachel and Leah, both of whom built up the House of Israel!" (4:11). The elders bless Ruth, a woman from Moab, by **the two sisters** you met in Genesis.

cards.q: Which two women do the elders name when they bless Ruth?
cards.why: "**Like Rachel and Leah**, both of whom built up the House of Israel."
wrong_why: They're matriarchs too, but not the ones named here.
Naomi and Orpah are in Ruth's own story.

points: "**So-and-so**": the redeemer without a name.
Ruth Rabbah 7:7: "mute from matters of Torah," he **refused Ruth**.
A **sandal** seals the deal.
The elders bless Ruth: **like Rachel and Leah**.

lessons.title: Ruth (5): A son for Naomi
lessons.check_note: Bava Batra 91b read on Sefaria 11/11.

cards.title: Full again
cards.body: Boaz marries Ruth, and she bears a son. The neighbors don't say "a son is born to Ruth." They say: "**A son is born to Naomi!**" (4:13-17).

cards.q: Who do the neighbors say the baby is born to?
cards.why: "**A son is born to Naomi!**" (4:17).

cards.he: וַתִּקְרֶאנָה לוֹ הַשְּׁכֵנוֹת שֵׁם לֵאמֹר יֻלַּד־בֵּן לְנׇעֳמִי וַתִּקְרֶאנָה שְׁמוֹ עוֹבֵד הוּא אֲבִי־יִשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד
cards.en: and the women neighbors gave him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi!” They named him Obed; he was the father of Jesse, father of David.
cards.en_src: THE JPS TANAKH: Gender-Sensitive Edition
cards.tl: Vatikrenah lo hash'cheinot sheim leimor yulad bein l'no-omi vatikrenah sh'mo oveid hu avi yishai avi david

cards.title: Empty, then full
cards.body: In chapter 1 Naomi said, "I went away full, and Adonai has brought me back empty" (1:21). Now a child is placed in her lap, and the women name him **Obed**, father of Jesse, **father of David**. Her emptiness is filled through Ruth's loyalty.

cards.q: Why do the neighbors call Ruth's son Naomi's?
choices: Naomi, who came back empty, is made full again
cards.why: The story ends where Naomi's grief began, **reversed**.
wrong_why: The text speaks of joy, not law.
Ruth is still there; she is the one who gave Naomi this.

cards.title: Ruth saw Solomon
cards.body: The Talmud says **Ruth the Moabite lived to see the kingship of Solomon**: the stranger who chose to belong saw her great-great-grandson on the throne.

cards.q: According to Bava Batra 91b, whose reign did Ruth live to see?
cards.why: **Solomon**, son of David, her great-great-grandson.
wrong_why: Saul was not of her line.
Moses lived long before Ruth.

cards.prompt: The line of David begins with a woman who chose to belong. What does that say to you about who belongs?

points: "**A son is born to Naomi!**"
Naomi, **empty**, is made **full** again.
Obed, Jesse, **David**.
Bava Batra 91b: Ruth **saw Solomon's kingship**.

lessons.title: Ruth (6): Where is God in Ruth?
